[1. PURPOSE]
Korean smart-store product detail page review-card section, 16:9 wide layout for e-commerce trust-building.
Designed as a realistic marketplace social-proof block with one strong header, product context, verified-purchase UI details, and exactly four review cards for a product detail page.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Canvas: 16:9 horizontal composition with the header and summary UI occupying the top 22%, and the four review-card grid filling the lower 68%.
- Header placement: {헤더} centered near the upper third, with the exact sub-line "실제 구매자 12,847명의 솔직한 후기" rendered just beneath it, followed by a compact rating summary.
- Product context: {제품} appears as the review subject in a slim product-info strip or small thumbnail area near the header, with realistic smart-store UI labels such as "베스트 리뷰", "사진 후기", "재구매율 92%".
- Review cards: exactly four evenly spaced cards in a single horizontal grid, each card with consistent padding, rounded corners, star rating, verified-purchase tag, Korean review content, option line, author/date metadata, helpful count, and tiny photo-review thumbnail area where appropriate.
- Background treatment: warm off-white or pale gray matte marketplace page background with subtle section dividers, faint UI chips, small sorting tabs, and realistic commerce-page micro elements.
- Spacing and framing: clear gutters between cards, consistent alignment, and a balanced marketplace-infographic structure with a believable product-detail-page section rhythm.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header zone (top 22%): Set {헤더} in a strong Korean sans-serif headline, centered. Directly below, render the exact line "실제 구매자 12,847명의 솔직한 후기" in a lighter weight.
- Rating summary line: Place a compact row of yellow star icons, "평점 4.9 / 5.0", "리뷰 12,847", and "사진 리뷰 3,206" beneath the header, using small but readable UI text.
- Product-info strip: Add a slim rounded strip below the rating summary showing a small square thumbnail placeholder for {제품}, the label "구매 고객 리뷰", and small pill tags such as "무료배송", "오늘출발", "재구매 많아요".
- Review navigation row: Above the cards, include tiny smart-store style sorting chips: "추천순", "최신순", "평점 높은순", and a small filter label "옵션별 보기" with a down arrow.
- Review card 1: White rounded card with a yellow 5-star row at the top, a green "실구매" badge, a bold Korean review title from the provided {4개 후기} set, a short supporting body sentence from the same entry, one option line like "옵션: 기본 / 1개", a small photo-review thumbnail area, and the author initial/date at the lower-right corner.
- Review card 2: Same layout and proportions as card 1, with distinct review copy from the provided {4개 후기} set, preserving the same typography hierarchy, verified badge, option metadata, helpful-count micro text, and thumbnail placement.
- Review card 3: Same card system, maintaining even line breaks, consistent margins, identical icon styling, and realistic UI metadata such as "도움돼요 128" or "한달 사용 후기".
- Review card 4: Same card system, aligned perfectly with the others, preserving a uniform grid, equal spacing, matching card height, and the same internal review hierarchy.
- Footer micro UI: At the bottom of the section, include a small page indicator "1 / 321" and subtle text buttons "후기 더보기" and "상품 문의하기" without adding extra testimonials.
- Product relevance: Use {제품} as a contextual cue through the product strip, option text, and review copy framing, while keeping the primary focus on the review-card section.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all UI text; headline semibold to bold 28–34px, body 18–22px, metadata 12–14px, with crisp Korean character rendering.
- Color palette: warm off-white #F4F1EA, soft gray #E9E9E9, charcoal text #222222, muted mid-gray #6B6B6B, review-star yellow #F6C445, card white #FFFFFF, verified green #00A86B, light beige divider #DED8CC.
- Border/shadow: cards with 16px radius, soft drop shadow 0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,0.10), subtle 1px border #EFEFEF; product strip and filter chips use lighter borders and soft inset highlights.
- Icon treatment: five-star icons should be flat, clean, and uniformly spaced, using a warm yellow tone with no gloss or 3D effect.
- Marketplace details: Add believable small UI elements such as verified-purchase badges, option labels, helpful counts, photo-review thumbnails, sorting chips, and page indicators while keeping exactly four main review cards.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing UI mockup style, as if captured with a 50mm equivalent product-design screenshot aesthetic, no perspective distortion.
- Lighting: evenly diffused studio-style illumination from front-top, with soft UI shadows and gentle separation between background, product strip, and cards.
- Color grade: soft beige-neutral UI grade with warm yellow accents, verified green micro badges, and restrained grayscale text, optimized for e-commerce readability.
- Rendering quality: sharp vector-like UI edges, readable Korean typography, realistic smart-store spacing, subtle texture in the matte background, and polished high-resolution commerce-page presentation.

[6. MOOD]
Naver Smart Store / 11st-style review section — trustworthy marketplace UI with a real product-detail-page feeling, warm customer proof, verified purchase signals, and polished Korean e-commerce credibility.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "실제 구매자 12,847명의 솔직한 후기" must appear exactly as written.
- Korean text accuracy: the 4 review entries from {4개 후기} must be rendered in Korean without broken characters, preserving star symbols and author initials/dates as part of the UI.
- Layout invariant: exactly 4 review cards in one horizontal grid, each with the same internal structure and visual hierarchy.
- Rating invariant: each card must show a 5-star row in yellow, with consistent spacing and alignment.
- Required Korean UI labels: include realistic micro text such as "실구매", "추천순", "최신순", "사진 리뷰", "도움돼요", and "후기 더보기" in small readable areas.
- Product reference: {제품} must appear as the reviewed product context in the header/product strip or card metadata.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-070.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean smart-store product detail page section showing a practical 4-step usage guide for a home appliance, designed for a 16:9 wide ecommerce banner.
Realistic, conversion-focused marketplace content that feels like an actual Naver SmartStore / Coupang product-detail image, with helpful micro labels, usage tips, small product callouts, and a polished product photography layout.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Top header band occupies about 14% of the frame, with {헤더} centered in a prominent Korean headline.
- Add a small supporting label above or beside the header such as “EASY GUIDE”, “처음 사용도 간편하게”, or “4 STEP 사용법” in Korean-friendly ecommerce styling.
- Main content area below is split into 4 equal horizontal columns, each taking roughly 21% width with 3% gutter spacing.
- Each column features a large step number, a realistic usage visual, a bold step title, a short explanatory line, and one small helpful micro-tag such as “준비”, “투입”, “설정”, “완성”.
- Keep the product object {제품} visually consistent across all steps, with realistic highlights, shadows, material texture, buttons, vents, lid edges, reflections, and small functional details appropriate to the product.
- Use {4단계} as the exact step-copy source, preserving the 4-step sequence and concise instructional tone.
- Insert thin dotted dividers, small arrows, or connected progress markers between columns to imply progression left-to-right.
- Add a realistic ecommerce information strip near the bottom with small Korean text such as “사용 전 설명서를 확인해 주세요”, “권장 사용 시간 10~15분”, “고객센터 1588-0000”, and a tiny QR/barcode-style support box, without overpowering the four main steps.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header band: Place {헤더} centered at the top in a bold Korean sans-serif, with a small eyebrow label “4 STEP GUIDE” and a compact sub-copy line like “누구나 쉽게 따라하는 스마트 사용 방법”.
2. Step 1 column: Show a large “01” near the upper-left of the column, then a realistic visual of {제품} in a prep state on a light kitchen counter or tabletop, followed by the first line from {4단계} as the step title and a short Korean subtext beneath. Include a small tag “준비하기”.
3. Step 2 column: Show “02” with a visual of ingredients, parts, water, food, or relevant contents being placed into {제품}, keeping the same visual scale and alignment as step 1 for consistency. Include small motion arrows and a tag “넣기”.
4. Step 3 column: Show “03” with a close, clear usage visual of the dial, touch button, switch, or control panel being adjusted, with the action emphasized by a small arrow, fingertip highlight, or accent glow. Include a tag “설정하기”.
5. Step 4 column: Show “04” with the finished result or completion state, making the final panel feel slightly celebratory with tiny sparkle accents, steam, glow, or a check mark while staying product-first. Include a tag “완료”.
6. Between columns: Use dotted progress lines, small arrowheads, or circular connector nodes aligned around the center height of each column so the sequence reads naturally from left to right.
7. Bottom utility strip: Add small realistic ecommerce details such as “TIP. 사용 후 전원을 끄고 내부를 건조해 주세요”, “A/S 문의 1588-0000”, “스마트스토어 전용 안내”, and a small rectangular barcode/QR support graphic.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all Korean text; header weight 700-800, step numbers in extra-bold sans-serif, body text 400-500, with sizes roughly 44-56px for header, 34-40px for step titles, 20-24px for descriptions, and 12-16px for micro labels and footer information.
- Color palette: white #FFFFFF, warm light gray #F6F7F8, charcoal #222222, and one accent color chosen from mint #7ED9C1 or peach #F6B39A.
- Border/shadow: very light card borders 1px #E9ECEF, subtle shadow 0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.06), clean rounded corners around visual blocks, with realistic contact shadows under the product.
- Use Korean ecommerce editorial styling with layered cards, soft gradient header accents, small info badges, dotted progress connectors, product callout lines, and practical usage notes.
- The design should look like a finished product-detail banner captured from a real smart-store listing, with polished photography, readable Korean copy, and believable appliance-use context.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm standard product photography look or 35mm hybrid ecommerce composition, straight-on framing with no distortion.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left with gentle fill on the right, even exposure across all four columns, natural contact shadows, and controlled reflections on plastic, metal, glass, or glossy surfaces.
- Color grade: neutral white balance with slight warm tone, crisp blacks, and restrained pastel accent treatment.
- Product rendering: realistic material finish, visible seams, handles, display area, buttons, labels, container edges, and subtle texture appropriate to {제품}.
- Background treatment: bright Korean ecommerce studio setup with light counter texture, gentle depth, soft gradient panels, and small practical visual cues that support the usage guide.

[6. MOOD]
Korean smart-store conversion section — polished Coupang / Naver SmartStore product guide aesthetic with a modern D2C marketplace editorial finish, practical household realism, clear instructional flow, and friendly trust-building details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: {헤더}, {4단계}
- Four-step ordering must read clearly from left to right as a sequential usage guide.
- All four columns should keep the same layout structure and consistent spacing.
- The product should remain identifiable as {제품} across all steps.
- Render added Korean microcopy cleanly, for example: “4 STEP 사용법”, “준비하기”, “넣기”, “설정하기”, “완료”, “사용 전 설명서를 확인해 주세요”, “TIP. 사용 후 전원을 끄고 내부를 건조해 주세요”.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-069.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean smart-store product detail page before/after comparison section, 16:9 horizontal wide layout for high-trust conversion.
Designed as a realistic e-commerce detail-page comparison block that visually contrasts pre-use and post-use results with credible product photography, review-style microcopy, and practical shopping-context information.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall composition: 16:9 wide canvas with an exact center vertical divide line; left half is BEFORE, right half is AFTER, each occupying exactly 50% of the frame.
- Header placement: {헤더} sits centered in the top 12–15% band, large and readable, with small supporting eyebrow text above or beside it such as “REAL COMPARISON” / “동일 조건 촬영”.
- Product placement: {제품} appears as the core visual subject in both halves, matching scale, angle, and camera height for comparison consistency.
- Before/after descriptions: left side follows {Before} and right side follows {After}, with short Korean supporting captions near the lower third and small comparison-point chips.
- E-commerce detail-page realism: include subtle smart-store style elements such as a small product name tag, review snippet strip, star rating micro row, “촬영 조건 동일” note, and a compact comparison table footer without overwhelming the main visual.
- Footer placement: a small disclaimer line centered at the bottom, readable but secondary, e.g. “개인차가 있을 수 있으며 사용 환경에 따라 결과가 달라질 수 있습니다.”
- Background treatment: warm off-white / light beige studio backdrop with real paper-like surface texture, soft shadows, natural contact shadows under the product, and a few relevant comparison-context details such as tiny check icons, measurement ticks, or small label stickers.
- Framing direction: symmetrical, editorial, highly legible, with balanced text hierarchy and a polished Korean smart-store product-detail look.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header band (12–15% height): place {헤더} centered in bold Korean typography; add a small top-left detail label such as “스마트스토어 상세 비교” and a small top-right issue-style code such as “DETAIL SECTION 03”. Add a thin separator line below in soft beige or white.
2. Left BEFORE panel (50% width): show {제품} in a clearly less favorable pre-use state aligned to {Before}; keep lighting slightly flatter and contrast more restrained than the right side while preserving realistic product detail and texture.
3. Right AFTER panel (50% width): show {제품} in an improved post-use state aligned to {After}; use the same framing and camera angle as the left panel for direct comparison, with cleaner highlights and more polished finish.
4. Center divide: add a thin vertical line at the exact midpoint, 1–2 px visual thickness, in off-white or warm gray; add a small centered vertical badge reading “동일 조건 비교” to clarify that the split is intentional.
5. Label treatment: place large bold labels “사용 전 BEFORE” on the left and “사용 후 AFTER” on the right, both in Korean-friendly typography with strong legibility; use muted taupe on BEFORE and dark brown-gray / warm ivory contrast on AFTER.
6. Supporting text zone: add concise supporting copy beneath each image region. Left: include {Before} with a small tag like “체감 포인트 01”. Right: include {After} with a small tag like “체감 포인트 02”. Add 2–3 tiny checklist chips such as “질감”, “정돈감”, “만족도” as visual comparison cues.
7. Review and info strip: along the lower 15–18% area, add a realistic product-detail micro section: “리뷰 기반 비교”, “★ 4.8 / 구매자 후기 1,247건”, “사용 기간 예시 2주”, and a short caption line. Keep all text small enough to support the main comparison.
8. Footer disclaimer: place the footer line centered along the bottom edge in small type, low contrast, and unobtrusive, but still legible on the beige background.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all Korean text, Bold 700–800 for header, Medium 500–600 for labels and chips, Regular 400 for captions and footer; header size should dominate the top band while labels and microcopy create a real product-detail hierarchy.
- Color palette: warm ivory #F6F1E8, soft beige #E7DCCB, muted taupe #B9AA97, dark brown-gray #4B423A, clean white #FFFFFF, with small accent marks in warm caramel #C89F6A for checklist icons or comparison chips.
- Border/shadow: use a subtle 4px y-offset, 10–12px blur, 12–15% opacity soft shadow for product cards, chips, and photo panels when needed; keep the center divider crisp and thin, not heavy.
- Graphic details: add fine hairline rules, rounded rectangular caption chips, tiny check icons, product-detail page markers, and small review metadata to make the layout feel like a finished smart-store sales section.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: high-resolution commercial photo look, 85mm f/1.8 or 50mm f/2.0 for product/body detail consistency, straight-on framing with low distortion.
- Lighting: soft studio softbox at 45° from upper-left, gentle fill from right, slightly more diffused and subdued on the BEFORE side, cleaner and brighter on the AFTER side; include believable contact shadows and material texture.
- Color grade: warm neutral editorial grade with creamy whites, soft beige highlights, and controlled brown-gray shadows; avoid oversaturation and harsh contrast.
- Rendering quality: crisp Korean typography, realistic product texture, clean e-commerce retouching, high-resolution detail-page presentation suitable for a smart-store product page.

[6. MOOD]
Trustworthy Korean smart-store comparison graphic — clean e-commerce editorial feel with a Daiso / Olive Young-style utility presentation, but elevated like a modern product case-study layout. The image should feel like a real product detail-page section from a high-converting Korean online store, with practical captions, review cues, and polished commercial photography.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표시될 문구는 {헤더}, {Before}, {After}.
- Required Korean labels to render clearly: “사용 전 BEFORE”, “사용 후 AFTER”, “동일 조건 비교”, “리뷰 기반 비교”, “개인차가 있을 수 있습니다”.
- Visual comparison rules: left and right panels must use the same camera angle, framing scale, and subject size so the before/after contrast feels credible.
- Layout invariants: 16:9 horizontal wide, exact vertical split, top header, bottom disclaimer, and clear left/right separation must all remain intact.
- The footer disclaimer must stay small and unobtrusive, such as “개인차가 있을 수 있으며 사용 환경에 따라 결과가 달라질 수 있습니다.”
- Make the comparison richer with realistic Korean smart-store detail elements, but keep {제품} as the dominant subject in both panels.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-068.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean smart-store product detail infographic for an e-commerce listing, 3-column feature showcase in a polished horizontal wide layout.
Designed to communicate three buying reasons quickly for mobile-first shoppers and desktop viewers while feeling like a real SmartStore product-detail section with practical shopping micro-information.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall canvas: 16:9 wide composition with a compact commerce header band at the top, followed by 3 equal-width feature columns across the full width, plus a slim product-info footer strip.
- Main product reference: {제품} should appear as the central topic across the three columns through iconography, feature text, small product silhouette details, and shopping information chips, not as a large hero photo.
- Header area: {헤더} centered near the top as the main Korean headline, supported by small realistic e-commerce labels such as "스토어 상품상세", "BEST POINT", "2026.05 업데이트", and "상품코드 PRD-068".
- Feature row: {3가지} is split into three visually balanced cards/columns with refined dividers between them, each column containing one icon, a bold feature title, and a short supporting line; add small supporting badges inside each card such as "핵심 기능", "실사용 체크", "구매 포인트" without adding extra feature columns.
- Background treatment: pale beige or warm off-white base with subtle paper grain, faint rounded panel layering, and gentle cream-to-beige tonal variation for realistic printed-detail-page depth.
- Framing direction: clean retail infographic with a clear grid, consistent padding, useful commerce details, small caption labels, and believable product-detail page finishing touches.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top commerce strip (top 6%): place a small left-aligned label "스토어 상품상세" and tiny metadata "2026.05 업데이트 · 상품코드 PRD-068"; on the right add compact chips "리뷰 4.8", "무료배송", "오늘출발" in muted teal and beige.
- Header strip (next 12%): place {헤더} in bold centered Korean text; include a smaller subtitle beneath reading "{제품} 구매 전 꼭 확인할 핵심 기능" and a tiny category label "SMART STORE INFOGRAPHIC".
- Column 1 (left 33%): show the first feature from {3가지} as a large flat vector icon above a bold feature label, then a one-line supporting description beneath; include a small numbered marker "POINT 01" and a micro caption line such as "일상 사용 기준" while keeping exactly one primary icon, one primary title, and one short description.
- Column 2 (center 34%): present the second feature with the same icon/title/description hierarchy, matching scale and spacing to the left column; add a soft teal accent tint behind the card and a small marker "POINT 02" so the center panel feels slightly emphasized without breaking balance.
- Column 3 (right 33%): show the third feature from {3가지} with the same structure, ensuring all three columns are visually consistent in icon size, text width, and padding; include a small marker "POINT 03" and a micro caption line such as "휴대성 체크".
- Product integration: {제품} should be implied through the feature content and visual language; add a small simplified product silhouette, tiny measurement tick marks, or line-art detail near the footer only as supporting context, secondary to the three-column information layout.
- Divider treatment: use refined vertical rules between columns, light gray or muted beige, with soft inner card shadows and rounded panel edges to resemble a finished marketplace 상세페이지 graphic.
- Footer strip (bottom 10%): add realistic shopping-detail microcopy: "구매 전 체크", "사용 시간은 환경에 따라 달라질 수 있습니다", "고객센터 10:00–17:00", "상세정보 · 배송안내 · 교환/반품"; include a small barcode-like SKU block or QR-style square purely as decorative product-code graphics, not an official certification.
- Copy hierarchy: feature titles should be the largest text inside each column, followed by a compact explanatory line in smaller weight; commerce metadata and captions should be tiny but legible.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all Korean text; header in Bold 34–42px, feature titles in SemiBold 24–30px, descriptions in Regular 16–20px, metadata and footer captions in 11–14px.
- Color palette: off-white #F7F3EA, beige #E9DFC9, soft teal #5FAEAA, muted peach #F2A987, charcoal #2E2E2E, light gray #D8D8D8.
- Icon style: flat vector, two-tone or monochrome with simple fills, rounded edges, clean geometric construction, marketplace-friendly pictograms.
- Panel/shadow: subtle card separation with 1px divider lines, rounded rectangles, soft shadow 0px 4px 10px 8% opacity, and tiny label pills for realistic e-commerce information density.
- Text alignment: centered within each feature column, with consistent baseline alignment across all three feature blocks; top metadata and footer microcopy may use left/right alignment for realistic product-detail-page structure.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: graphic design infographic style, no photographic camera look; if rendered with product mockup detail, use an orthographic flat-lay presentation with no perspective distortion.
- Lighting: diffuse studio-style even lighting simulation with soft panel shadows and gentle highlight separation on cards, avoiding harsh directional cast shadows.
- Color grade: clean e-commerce palette with warm cream base, soft teal and peach accents, neutral charcoal text, slightly muted saturation for a trustworthy marketplace look.

[6. MOOD]
Practical Korean e-commerce editorial — clean Market Kurly / Musinsa-style product communication with a modern D2C brochure feel, enriched with believable SmartStore detail-page labels, shopping chips, review cues, and product-support captions.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear correctly in the rendered image: "이 제품을 추천하는 3가지 이유", "7단 강도 조절", "4시간 연속 사용", "1.1kg 초경량".
- Also render supporting Korean commerce text cleanly where included: "스토어 상품상세", "리뷰 4.8", "무료배송", "오늘출발", "구매 전 체크", "상세정보", "배송안내", "교환/반품".
- The feature layout must remain exactly 3 equal columns with one primary icon, one primary title, and one short description per column.
- Maintain clean, legible Korean sans-serif typography with no broken characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean smart-store product detail page hero section, square 1:1 main visual for e-commerce conversion.
Realistic Naver SmartStore-style product hero with premium photography, clear purchase cues, trust signals, delivery information, and content-rich seller-page details optimized for mobile scrolling and quick decision-making.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Canvas: 1:1 square layout with a centered dominant hero product occupying about 58–62% of the frame, slightly tilted for dimensional depth and photographed as a real product placed on a warm tabletop surface.
- Background treatment: warm gray and ivory studio backdrop with subtle paper-matte texture, faint tabletop horizon, soft fabric or paper shadows, and natural e-commerce styling details that support the product without stealing focus.
- Spacing and framing: place the main headline in the upper zone, product in the center, trust and USP blocks in the lower zone, with additional tiny seller-page UI labels, shipping info, and product metadata arranged along the sides for a realistic detail-page hero.
- Use {제품명}, {메인 카피}, {평점·후기}, {USP} placeholders as the exact primary on-image content.
- Add realistic Korean microcopy around the hero such as “스마트스토어 단독 구성”, “오늘출발 · 무료배송”, “구매 포인트”, “상품코드 SS-067”, “옵션 선택 가능”, and “상세페이지 HERO” in small readable UI-style labels.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero product area (center 60%): {제품명} shown as a polished front-facing or slightly angled product hero shot with crisp edges, realistic material detail, gentle highlights, and a soft physical shadow on the surface beneath it.
2. Top headline band (upper 18%): {메인 카피} placed in large Korean sans-serif type, spanning the width with strong hierarchy above the product, aligned for immediate readability on mobile. Add a small eyebrow label above it: “SMART STORE BEST ITEM”.
3. Trust block (lower-left 14%): {평점·후기} set as a compact review badge line with a star-rating motif, tiny “실구매 후기 기반” caption, and a small profile-dot row suggesting multiple buyers.
4. Feature block (lower-right 14%): {USP} split into three short lines or slash-separated benefits, arranged as a compact spec list with small icon-like separators, plus a small heading “구매 포인트”.
5. Seller information strip: include a slim lower information bar with “오늘출발 · 무료배송”, “네이버페이 적립”, “교환/반품 안내”, and a small product code label “상품코드 SS-067” to make the hero feel like a real Korean commerce page.
6. Decorative commerce details: add subtle thumbnail cards or small rounded chips near the product edge, such as “NEW”, “인기 옵션”, “선물 추천”, and tiny line icons for delivery, review, and quality check.
7. Balance and flow: keep the product as the unmistakable focal point, with copy blocks framing rather than covering it; maintain a premium seller-page feel with realistic overlays, labels, and conversion-oriented information hierarchy.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all Korean text; headline in Bold 800, body in Medium 500, small details in Regular 400; headline size about 68–84 px equivalent, supporting text 24–34 px equivalent, microcopy 13–18 px equivalent.
- Color palette: ivory #F5F1E8, warm gray #D8D2C8, charcoal #2B2B2B, soft beige #E7DDCF, muted accent gray-blue #8A93A0, with small warm taupe and cream UI chips.
- Border/shadow: soft drop shadow under product, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; use refined rounded panels, thin divider lines, small icon marks, and subtle paper-card shadows for seller-page realism.
- Layout language: premium Korean D2C commerce aesthetic with clear typographic rhythm, tactile product photography, and useful shopping information integrated into the hero area.
- Text rendering: all Korean labels must appear clean, readable, and aligned like a professionally designed smart-store detail page.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: clean studio product photography look, equivalent to a 85mm f/4 product shot with a slightly compressed perspective and crisp detail.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left at about 45°, with a very subtle fill from the right, a faint underside shadow for depth, and realistic highlights on product edges or packaging surfaces.
- Color grade: warm neutral e-commerce grade with creamy whites, soft beige midtones, restrained contrast, and polished smart-store catalog clarity.
- Surface detail: warm matte tabletop, faint paper grain, soft folded card shadows, tiny printed UI labels, and natural product reflections appropriate to the material.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean smart-store bestseller hero — polished Naver SmartStore / direct-to-consumer product page aesthetic, trustworthy, content-rich, warm, and ready for purchase conversion.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 이미지에 정확히 보여야 함:
  - {제품명}
  - {메인 카피}
  - {평점·후기}
  - {USP}
- Additional Korean text must be realistic smart-store microcopy, for example: “스마트스토어 단독 구성”, “오늘출발 · 무료배송”, “구매 포인트”, “상품코드 SS-067”, “네이버페이 적립”, “옵션 선택 가능”.
- Product must remain the dominant hero object, with clear hierarchy and no text covering essential product details.
- Layout must stay in a 1:1 square composition with top headline, central product, lower-left trust line, lower-right USP block, and a slim commerce information strip.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean cafe menu photo, top-view drink close-up for social media and menu presentation.
Square 1:1 food photography with a clear hero drink, appetizing tabletop details, and a realistic neighborhood-cafe menu atmosphere.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Hero placement: {음료} occupies about 60% of the frame, centered slightly above midline so the rim, foam, ice, cream, or surface details are easy to read.
- Support props: {곁들임} arranged loosely around the drink at 3 o'clock, 7 o'clock, and 10 o'clock positions to create a natural cafe tabletop rhythm, with crumbs, a spoon, napkin folds, or a small saucer adding realism.
- Menu context: include a partially visible printed cafe menu card or receipt-style order slip near one edge, showing short Korean menu text such as "오늘의 추천", "아메리카노 ₩4,500", "라떼 ₩5,500", "시그니처 크림 ₩6,800", and the store name "카페 하루".
- Angle and framing: {구도} with the table surface filling the frame edge-to-edge; compose tightly like an actual menu photograph taken right before serving.
- Background treatment: {배경} rendered as a warm-toned wooden or stone cafe table with visible grain, tiny scratches, cup rings, and subtle real tabletop texture.
- Lighting setup: {조명} used to define the drink rim, highlight the liquid sheen, and cast a gentle shadow toward the lower-right.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Main drink area: {음료} shown as the unmistakable focal point, with clear foam, latte-art detail, ice, syrup layer, crema, garnish, or glossy surface texture depending on the drink.
- Surface styling: Place {곁들임} close enough to feel like a real cafe set; include natural details such as pastry flakes, a small teaspoon reflection, folded tissue texture, a coaster edge, or condensation droplets.
- Table plane: {배경} should read as a tactile cafe tabletop with warm grain, slight wear, soft cup shadows, and believable contact points under every object.
- Printed details: the menu card, order slip, or small table tent should feel secondary but readable in short Korean snippets, with prices and simple dividers like a real cafe menu.
- Light behavior: {조명} should create glossy highlights on the drink surface, a soft contact shadow under the cup, and a gentle falloff across the wood texture.
- Final photo feel: keep the image photo-realistic with overhead depth cues, subtle condensation if the drink is cold, realistic ceramic or glass material, and naturally imperfect tabletop styling.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: any visible printed menu or receipt text must be small, cafe-like, and accurately rendered in Korean; use short lines such as "카페 하루", "오늘의 추천", "바닐라 라떼 ₩5,800", "디저트 세트 ₩9,500".
- Color palette: espresso brown, milk beige, warm wood brown, soft cream, muted caramel, pastry gold, ceramic white, and gentle coffee-black accents.
- Prop styling: use realistic cafe items such as a saucer, spoon, coaster, napkin, sugar packet, menu card, receipt slip, or pastry plate only when they support {음료} and {곁들임}.
- Shadow and depth: use realistic soft shadows, contact shadows, and small reflective highlights to make the objects sit naturally on the table.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with RF 50mm f/1.8 for a natural close-up tabletop look, shot from a true top-down angle.
- Lighting: soft natural window light from the upper-left at about 45°, with a faint fill bounce from the lower-right to keep highlights gentle and even.
- Color grade: warm cream and caramel grade with slightly muted saturation, clean whites, and glossy reflections preserved on the drink surface.
- Texture detail: capture foam bubbles, ice edges, ceramic glaze, glass refraction, pastry crust texture, paper fibers, wood grain, and tiny table imperfections with realistic clarity.

[6. MOOD]
Korean cafe Instagram food photography — polished menu-board editorial with a cozy neighborhood-cafe feel, similar to a premium Seoul brunch cafe feed, inviting enough to make the drink feel freshly served and worth ordering.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if printed menu or receipt text appears, render it clearly and correctly in Korean, using short phrases like "카페 하루", "오늘의 추천", "아메리카노 ₩4,500", "라떼 ₩5,500", "디저트 세트 ₩9,500".
- Composition invariants: the drink must remain the primary subject, and the side props must stay secondary and never block the cup rim, latte art, foam, ice, or garnish.
- Top-view invariant: maintain a consistent overhead tabletop perspective with no tilted perspective drift.
- Realism invariant: all props, printed paper, shadows, condensation, crumbs, and reflections should look like they belong in the same real cafe scene.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]

- Use {카페 이름}, {스탬프 도장}, {칸 수}, {멘트} as the customizable text and design anchors.
- Include small practical loyalty-card details such as an address line, phone number, Instagram handle, open hours, QR-code placeholder, and a short terms line in Korean to make the card feel usable in a real cafe.

- Main grid zone (middle 58%): build a stamp grid with exactly {칸 수} presented as a 2x5 or 5x2 layout; each cell should be evenly spaced, numbered subtly 01–10 if appropriate, with 3–4 cells visibly stamped using {스탬프 도장} as sample filled marks and the remaining cells empty.

- Footer zone (bottom 18%): place {멘트} in smaller Korean handwriting-style text, aligned cleanly within card margins, plus micro copy like "10잔 적립 시 아메리카노 1잔 무료", "사용기한 2026.12.31", and "분실 시 재발급이 어려워요".

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the main readable text, medium to semibold weight, with a small handwritten accent style for the promotional line; size hierarchy should clearly separate header, grid labels, stamp cells, terms, and contact details.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Post 1 (top-left): exterior cafe shot with storefront, real signage reading “{카페}”, glass door reflections, small sidewalk sandwich board, potted greenery, nearby street texture, and a small caption overlay “오늘의 문을 열었어요”.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean café grand opening poster, vertical 9:16 event announcement for social media and print.
Modern editorial cafe launch graphic with cinematic storefront photography, believable event information, and strong typography hierarchy.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Poster uses a vertical 9:16 split: upper 60% hero image, lower 40% typography and event-information block.
- {시각} fills the upper hero area as a cinematic Seoul café storefront scene at night, with visible interior activity through glass: barista at the counter, customers seated near windows, pendant lamps, menu board, plants, coffee cups, and street reflections.
- Lower block sits on a deep navy / charcoal editorial panel with layered text, fine divider rules, small labels, and practical poster details that feel like a real printed opening announcement.
- Place {카페 이름} as the largest text, with {부제}, {오픈 날짜}, {주소}, and {이벤트} stacked beneath in descending scale.
- Add small supporting poster elements: corner label “GRAND OPENING”, Korean date/time row “오전 10시 오픈”, venue label “성수 1호점”, a small QR reservation box, sponsor/partner strip, and ticket-style note “입장 무료 · 예약 없이 방문 가능”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero area (top 60%): {시각} shown as a high-end café exterior at night, warm yellow interior lighting glowing through full-height glass, a few people visible inside, espresso machine and pastry display hinted through the window, subtle wet pavement reflections, indoor plants, small exterior sign, and cinematic depth.
- Photo overlay details: add a small top-left label “NEW CAFÉ IN SEONGSU” and a tiny date caption “OPENING WEEK · 2026” in cream or amber without covering the storefront.
- Transition band: separate photo and text block using a thin amber divider line, soft gradient fade, or deep navy band with a small centered dot motif.
- Title block: {카페 이름} centered and oversized in a refined modern serif or 명조 style, occupying the visual anchor of the lower half.
- Subtitle block: {부제} placed directly under the title in smaller Korean sans-serif, with balanced tracking and a premium editorial rhythm.
- Event information: {오픈 날짜} set larger than the remaining details, followed by {주소} on one line and {이벤트} beneath it as a concise promotional line.
- Detail row: include realistic supporting text in Korean such as “OPEN 10:00–22:00”, “라스트 오더 21:30”, “성수 1호점”, and “입장 무료 · 예약 없이 방문 가능”.
- Sponsor / partner area: near the bottom, add a small strip reading “WITH LOCAL ROASTERY · DESSERT PARTNER · FLOWER STYLING” plus Korean microcopy “협업 로스터리 / 디저트 파트너 / 플라워 스타일링”.
- QR / ticket area: add a small square QR-like graphic block labeled “MAP & MENU” and a tiny ticket-info caption “첫 주 방문 고객 웰컴 쿠폰 증정”.
- Corner badge: “GRAND OPENING” in a compact all-caps label, framed by a refined line box or tab style, with a small Korean label “그랜드 오픈”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: {카페 이름} in Pretendard, Noto Serif KR, or a modern serif similar to Cormorant Garamond / Playfair Display; subtitle and details in Pretendard or Noto Sans KR; title weight light to regular, body weight medium; title size 72–110px, details 24–36px depending on hierarchy; micro labels 12–18px.
- Korean display text should feel like real poster copy: “성수 1호점 그랜드 오픈”, “오전 10시 오픈”, “입장 무료”, “MAP & MENU”, “첫 주 방문 고객 웰컴 쿠폰 증정”, “라스트 오더 21:30”.
- Color palette: dark navy #111827, warm amber #D99A3A, cream #F5EFE6, soft gray #C7CDD6, deep charcoal #1B1B1D.
- Border/shadow: subtle editorial drop shadow under key text blocks, 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; use thin divider lines in muted cream or amber; allow refined decorative linework, small dots, tabs, QR box, and ticket-style labels.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean café new-menu promotional card news for Instagram, 3-slide swipeable square carousel. Realistic editorial food marketing layout with a polished café-launch feel, showing an appetizing beverage photo, readable Korean promo copy, carousel UI details, and café-brand social content cues.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Square 1:1 composition designed as a 3-slide Instagram carousel preview, with the center slide emphasized slightly larger and the two side slides angled or offset just enough to show the swipeable sequence.
- Main subject placement: each slide uses a top-heavy layout where the drink image occupies about 55–60% of the frame, and the lower 40% contains headline, body copy, price/date/store information, slide number, and carousel indicators.
- Background treatment: warm cream or oat-colored paper-like surface with subtle café stationery grain, faint espresso-ring marks, small ingredient accents, soft napkin texture, and gentle natural shadows that make the image feel photographed in a real café.
- Use {카페}, {신메뉴}, and {3슬라이드} as the editable content anchors.
- Add a small Instagram-style handle such as “@brand.cafe” or “@{카페}” in a clean corner, plus tiny save/share micro icons and a short hashtag line like “#신메뉴 #오늘의카페 #시즌음료”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Slide preview structure: show three square cards in a horizontal carousel stack, labeled clearly as 01/03, 02/03, 03/03 so the {3슬라이드} concept is immediately readable.
- Hero image area (top 55–60%): feature a polished realistic beverage photo of {신메뉴} with condensation or creamy foam depending on the drink, glass/ceramic highlights, visible garnish or ingredient detail, and a soft contact shadow on the card.
- Slide 1 content: large launch headline in Korean, for example “이번 시즌, {신메뉴} 출시” and supporting line “{카페}에서 만나는 산뜻한 한 잔”, with a small label “NEW MENU”.
- Slide 2 content: ingredients / preparation explanation with 2–3 concise Korean bullets such as “직접 우린 베이스”, “부드러운 크림 레이어”, “향긋한 시럽 한 스푼”, accompanied by small ingredient close-ups like beans, citrus peel, milk splash, herbs, or chocolate pieces appropriate to the beverage.
- Slide 3 content: price / period / store info + CTA, for example “출시 기념 ₩6,500”, “기간 2026.05.01–05.31”, “매장: {카페} 전 지점”, “지금 저장하고 방문하기”, plus a small end-card CTA button shape reading “SAVE & VISIT”.
- Carousel indicator area: add 3 small dots or a thin page bar near the bottom edge, with the current slide dot filled in the accent color; include “1/3”, “2/3”, “3/3” page indicators on the respective cards.
- Brand/social area: place “@brand.cafe” or “@{카페}” in small legible text, plus tiny heart/comment/share/save icons, a subtle caption line “오늘의 신메뉴 소식”, and a compact hashtag row.
- Design should look like a real Instagram card news ad exported from a café brand account, with layered paper cards, realistic beverage photography, crisp typography, and believable promotional details.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for body copy, with a refined Korean serif such as Noto Serif KR for the main headline; headline weight 700–800, body weight 400–500, headline size roughly 28–40px equivalent in the square preview.
- Color palette: use warm cream #F6F0E6, oat beige #E8DDCF, charcoal #2C2C2C, and one accent color chosen to match the drink mood, such as muted green #7E9B73 or latte brown #8A6A4E.
- Border/shadow: use fine card edges, realistic paper thickness, soft layered shadows, and a soft drop shadow around the hero drink, about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity.
- Add refined café-ad details such as small decorative dividers, price tag chips, ingredient icons, date labels, micro captions, and subtle sticker-like tags while keeping a premium editorial hierarchy.
- Text must remain clean and readable, with strong contrast between charcoal text and cream/oat backgrounds; accent labels and CTA buttons should feel intentionally designed rather than generic.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: realistic café product photography using a Sony A7R IV with 85mm f/1.4 for a softly compressed hero look, or a top-down 35mm equivalent for flat-lay-style menu presentation.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, with a gentle fill from the right to preserve highlight detail on the drink and keep shadows smooth.
- Color grade: warm cream + oat + muted green palette with lightly desaturated highlights and natural beverage tones, resembling high-end café social-media content.
- Material realism: beverage glass or ceramic should show believable reflections, foam texture, condensation, syrup layers, ice, garnish, and surface contact shadows; paper cards should show subtle grain and slight thickness.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean café editorial — a refined Brunch-style Instagram launch card with the inviting, polished atmosphere of a modern specialty café feed, lively enough to feel like an actual seasonal menu announcement.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: “카페”, “신메뉴”, “3슬라이드”.
- Include the editable anchors {카페}, {신메뉴}, and {3슬라이드} clearly in the layout copy without changing the placeholder names.
- Recommended visible Korean copy examples: “이번 시즌, {신메뉴} 출시”, “{카페}에서 만나는 산뜻한 한 잔”, “출시 기념 ₩6,500”, “기간 2026.05.01–05.31”, “지금 저장하고 방문하기”, “#신메뉴 #오늘의카페”.
- If the carousel preview includes copy, keep the Korean typography clean and fully legible with no broken Hangul characters.
- The 3-slide logic must be visually understandable at a glance, with 01/03, 02/03, 03/03 labels or three active-state indicators clearly distinguished.
- All beverage visuals should look like a real café menu photo, not a generic illustration.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Canvas is a perfect square 1:1 composition with a centered 2x2 grid; each cell occupies roughly 24% of the frame, separated by thin white dividers.

- Use {브랜드} as a small circular brand mark at the exact center where the four cells meet; include tiny surrounding text such as "SUMMER DRINKS", "NEW", or "SEASON ONLY" around the badge.
- Place {테마} as the main seasonal headline near the top or bottom margin, paired with a short Korean subtitle such as "시원하게 만나는 오늘의 4잔" or "여름 한정 시즌 메뉴".
- Add practical Instagram ad details: a small handle line "@{브랜드}_cafe", a date label "2026 SUMMER", a promo period "5.01 - 8.31", and a compact CTA like "매장·포장 가능" or "지금 주문하기".

- Composition should feel structured, balanced, mobile-readable, and commercially polished like a real Korean cafe seasonal menu post.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top-left panel: {4종 음료} list item 1 shown as a fresh fruit drink with visible garnish, ice, sparkling liquid, sliced fruit, glass highlights, condensation droplets, and a small napkin or coaster detail; label it with a Korean menu tag near the corner and add a price.
- Top-right panel: {4종 음료} list item 2 shown as a creamy latte-style drink with layered color separation, soft foam, latte swirl, polished glassware, and a spoon or saucer partially visible in the crop; keep the crop tight and appetizing.
- Bottom-left panel: {4종 음료} list item 3 shown as a citrus-forward sparkling drink with mint, lime, bubbles, ice cubes, condensation detail, and a bright fresh tone; include a small caption like "톡 쏘는 청량감".
- Bottom-right panel: {4종 음료} list item 4 shown as a yogurt-based strawberry drink with vivid pink tone, strawberry slices, thick chilled texture, soft whipped or yogurt surface, and realistic fruit pulp detail.
- Center point: add a small circular badge combining a simple brand mark, {브랜드}, and a seasonal label, sitting exactly on the grid intersection without covering the key drink areas.
- Main title zone: place {테마} in a clean, modern header style above or below the grid, with secondary Korean copy such as "4가지 맛으로 즐기는 여름" and a tiny footer line "전국 매장 순차 출시".
- Include small decorative graphic accents that suit a cafe ad: tiny sparkle marks, fruit-outline icons, thin divider ticks, micro menu numbers "01 02 03 04", and a compact hashtag row such as "#여름음료 #카페신메뉴 #시즌한정".

[4. STYLE RULES]

- Color palette: fresh fruit-driven tones with #F6E7D8 cream, #FFB347 mango orange, #FF6B81 strawberry pink, #7ED957 lime green, #8E63D8 accent purple, all balanced with white dividers.
- Border/shadow: thin white grid lines with a subtle 2px soft shadow, and panel edges should remain crisp rather than rounded.
- Use refined Korean menu typography with clear hierarchy: large headline, medium drink names, small prices, tiny promo/footer captions, and readable hashtag text.
- Allow realistic cafe surface details inside panels: ceramic saucer edges, linen napkin texture, fruit wedges, mint leaves, paper straw, coaster shadows, ice refraction, and condensation trails.
- Keep the overall design premium and modern, with carefully placed decorative accents that enhance the seasonal cafe advertisement rather than distracting from the drinks.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

- Lighting: warm natural window light from upper-left at about 45°, with gentle fill from the right to preserve glass reflections and ice texture.
- Color grade: fresh summer editorial grade with bright whites, juicy fruit saturation, soft warm highlights, and clean contrast.
- Texture rendering: emphasize realistic ice clarity, fruit pulp, foam bubbles, yogurt thickness, sparkling carbonation, glass rim highlights, and faint paper grain in the menu-card background.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열 — "{브랜드}", "{테마}", "4종 음료"에 해당하는 각 메뉴의 한글 라벨.
- Additional Korean text should be legible and natural: "여름 한정 시즌 메뉴", "시원하게 만나는 오늘의 4잔", "매장·포장 가능", "지금 주문하기", "#여름음료", "#카페신메뉴".
- Layout invariant: exactly 4 panels in a 2x2 grid, with thin white dividers and a small circular badge centered at the intersection.
- No panel may be empty; each cell must contain one distinct drink image, one Korean menu label, and a small price or taste-note detail.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean small cafe hand-drawn illustrated menu board, 2x3 drink grid layout, vertical poster for in-store display and Instagram sharing.
Watercolor + ink illustration style with handwritten Korean menu text, realistic paper texture, shop details, small decorative cafe graphics, and readable pricing, designed as a cozy local cafe menu sheet that feels actually posted inside a neighborhood cafe.

- The poster should feel handmade and used in a real cafe: slight watercolor bleed, pencil guide traces, paper grain, imperfect ink pressure, and gentle taped-corner or pin-mark details.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Top header: place {카페 이름} in large expressive hand-drawn Korean lettering at the upper center, with a small “SINCE 2024” note and two tiny coffee-bean doodles beside it.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use hand-drawn Korean lettering inspired by brush pen cafe signage, with a secondary clean sans-serif like Pretendard SemiBold for prices if needed for legibility; title around 54-64px, menu names around 24-30px, price around 22-26px, footer details around 14-18px.

- Add cafe-appropriate decorative dividers, tiny drink-size labels, beans, steam curls, ice cubes, straw marks, and small hand-drawn sticker-like tags, while keeping the six drink cells clearly readable.

- Lighting: even diffused studio light, like soft daylight from upper-left with gentle natural shadowing around paper texture, taped corners, and illustrated card edges.

Add 2–3 small fixed Korean supporting lines where natural, such as “대표 블렌드”, “오트 변경 +700”, “시즌 아이스 가능”, and realistic prices like “₩4,800”, “₩5,500”, “₩6,200”.

5. Lower-right decorative area: place {작은 일러스트} as a neat editorial illustration with thin strokes and soft filled shapes; nearby add small breathing rhythm dots, a tiny leaf, or circular calm-wave marks to connect visually with the meditation topic.

  - {브랜드 핸들}: 사용자가 지정한 브랜드 핸들이 정확한 한글/영문 문자열로 렌더링되어야 함

- Main canvas: vertical iPhone screen mockup occupying the full frame, with the phone UI centered for a 9:16 display and realistic device depth.
- Background treatment: {배경} with a pastel peach-to-cream gradient, soft floating star particles, translucent glassy blobs, faint app-themed sparkles, and warm ambient light behind the phone.
- Phone screen environment: show a believable lock-screen or app-home backdrop inside the phone, including status bar, time label “오전 9:41”, date label “5월 1일 금요일”, tiny Wi‑Fi/battery icons, and a subtle home indicator at the bottom.
- Subject placement: one main notification card sits in the central 45% of the screen, slightly raised with a soft shadow; CTA button anchors the right side of the card.
- UI depth: add faint blurred content behind the notification such as a small weather widget, calendar chip, bottom navigation icons, and a soft promotional banner labeled “앱 전용 혜택” so the card feels embedded in a real app ecosystem.
- Spacing and framing: use realistic mobile UI padding around the card; card edges should feel compact and readable, with clear separation between app icon, header, body, timestamp, and CTA.
- Use {앱 이름}, {알림 헤더}, {알림 본문}, {CTA} as the editable Korean content elements.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Background layer: full-bleed pastel gradient base with tiny star-like speckles, soft bokeh dots, warm cream highlights, and a few subtle rounded geometric accents matching the palette.
- Phone frame layer: realistic iPhone-style device outline and screen area, slim bezels, visible Dynamic Island or notch area, crisp top status bar, and a faint edge reflection on the glass.
- Screen UI layer: softly blurred app interface or lock-screen wallpaper with believable Korean microcopy such as “오늘의 추천”, “방금 전”, “앱 전용 혜택”, “마이페이지”, “쿠폰함”, and small icon placeholders.
- Notification card layer: warm white rounded rectangle centered on the screen, with a soft drop shadow, slight glass highlight, and authentic iOS/Android system-notification proportions.
- Card header row: small square app icon at the upper-left, {앱 이름} aligned beside it in a compact label style, a small timestamp “방금 전” on the upper-right, and {알림 헤더} set below in bold Korean text.
- Body text row: {알림 본문} placed under the header, left-aligned with comfortable line spacing and concise mobile-readable sizing.
- Action area: {CTA} appears as a small right-aligned pill button or text button inside the card, using muted coral or soft pink accent color for quick recognition.
- Supporting details: add a tiny campaign chip “오늘만”, a micro badge “NEW”, a subtle bell icon, and a fine divider line inside the card to make it feel like a real marketing notification.
- Finishing details: preserve the phone status bar icons, keep all Korean text crisp, and ensure the card feels like an authentic app retention notification rather than a generic poster.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all UI text; {알림 헤더} in bold 700–800 weight, {알림 본문} in medium 500 weight, {CTA} in semi-bold 600 weight, with mobile-friendly size hierarchy.
- Supporting Korean microcopy should be smaller and realistic: “오전 9:41”, “5월 1일 금요일”, “방금 전”, “오늘만”, “NEW”, “앱 전용 혜택”, “쿠폰함”, “마이페이지”.
- Color palette: peach #F7C9B5, cream #FFF6EC, soft pink #F8DDE4, warm white #FFFFFF, charcoal #2B2B2B, muted coral #FF8A7A.
- Border/shadow: notification card with 20–24px corner radius, soft drop shadow 0px 10px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.12), faint inner highlight, and a thin translucent edge stroke for a polished UI look.
- App icon: create a generic rounded-square icon using the same palette, with a small abstract symbol or bell motif; it should look like a real app icon without requiring a real brand mark.
- UI realism: include tiny touch-friendly icon sizes, subtle screen glare, rounded widgets, realistic notification padding, and a believable hierarchy between the card, background widgets, and phone frame.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing product mockup look, equivalent to a 50mm standard lens with low perspective distortion, clean orthographic presentation of the phone screen.
- Lighting: studio softbox from upper-left at 45° with gentle fill from lower-right, producing even screen visibility, delicate phone-edge highlights, and a soft shadow beneath the raised notification card.
- Color grade: pastel peach and cream with a light airy UI finish, slightly desaturated for a premium app-marketing feel.
- Material feel: glossy phone glass, satin metal device edge, soft translucent UI panels, and subtle paper-like warmth in the notification card background.

[6. MOOD]
Premium mobile app marketing visual — clean App Store / iOS promotional card aesthetic with a calm editorial UI finish, warm retention-campaign energy, and a realistic “just received” push notification moment.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as rendered text:
  - {앱 이름}
  - {알림 헤더}
  - {알림 본문}
  - {CTA}
- Additional Korean UI text may appear as realistic microcopy: “오전 9:41”, “5월 1일 금요일”, “방금 전”, “오늘만”, “NEW”, “앱 전용 혜택”, “쿠폰함”, “마이페이지”.
- The phone mockup must remain vertical 9:16 and the status bar must be visible at the top.
- Notification card layout must clearly separate icon, app name, timestamp, header, body, CTA, and supporting badge elements with legible Korean typography.
- All UI proportions should feel like a real mobile notification inside a phone screen, not a poster or website banner.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-053.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean food and beverage packaging design mockup, square product presentation for portfolio, e-commerce, or pitch deck use.
Create a polished, content-rich single-package hero image that feels like a real retail FMCG package photographed in a professional studio, with authentic printed details, clear Korean typography, and realistic shelf-ready information hierarchy.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main package placement: one {제품 종류} package occupies about 62% of the frame, standing upright or tilted 8–12 degrees, centered slightly below midline for a premium mockup feel.
- Background treatment: soft light gray to ivory seamless studio sweep with subtle paper texture, warm tabletop contact shadow, and a few small contextual food cues such as red chili flakes, sesame seeds, steam-like graphic accents, or a folded napkin placed far behind the package so the package remains dominant.
- Framing direction: front-facing package emphasis with readable label details, full product silhouette, crisp top and side seams, visible gusset folds or carton edges, and believable package thickness.
- Front-facing design elements should include {제품명 KOR} as the dominant title, {부제} as a smaller supporting line, a compact brand mark area, nutrition label, barcode area, net weight, flavor callout, preparation time, date code, and small manufacturer/contact microcopy like a real Korean retail package.
- Visual direction should reflect {시각 컨셉} while preserving a realistic printed-packaging mockup surface, crisp folds, ink density variation, sealed edges, and believable material finish.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero package zone: render {제품 종류} as the sole main package, with crisp die-cut edges, realistic carton/cup/pouch curvature, sealed seams, small wrinkles, subtle corner highlights, and a soft studio shadow directly beneath it.
2. Primary typography zone: place {제품명 KOR} large and centered on the front face in bold Korean lettering, ensuring strong contrast, immediate shelf impact, and realistic ink registration.
3. Secondary copy zone: position {부제} below the main title in smaller type, with tighter tracking and a clean hierarchy that supports the product name without competing with it.
4. Illustration zone: build a large graphic illustration that follows {시각 컨셉}, scaled to occupy the upper or central area of the package face with clear color separation, print-friendly shapes, and appetizing flavor cues such as chili flame shapes, noodle swirl graphics, sauce droplets, or ingredient icons.
5. Utility label zone: add a realistic nutrition-info placeholder area on the lower front or side panel with tiny Korean grid text: "영양정보", "총 내용량 120g", "나트륨", "탄수화물", "당류", "지방", "단백질"; include a barcode block, QR-like square, recycling icon, lot/date code "2026.05.01", and customer service line "고객상담 080-123-4567".
6. Brand mark zone: place a compact generic brand area near the top corner or header strip, using believable Korean microcopy such as "불꽃상회", "SINCE 2026", or "매운맛 연구소" as decorative retail branding, integrated naturally into the package layout without implying official certification.
7. Retail detail zone: add short Korean callouts on the package such as "HOT LEVEL 4", "조리 4분", "진한 양념스프", "NEW", "1인분", "120g", "권장소비자가 ₩1,800" in small badges, tabs, or side-panel text to make the packaging feel complete and commercially real.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold for {제품명 KOR} at very large display size, Noto Sans KR Medium for {부제}, and Noto Sans KR Regular for label text; keep Korean letterforms crisp and fully legible, including small package microcopy.
- Color palette: vivid food-packaging palette matched to flavor, anchored by red, orange, black, and warm cream with optional accent tones from {시각 컨셉}; use clean contrast against the pale background and let the package graphics feel bold, appetizing, and shelf-ready.
- Border/shadow: soft drop shadow with 4px vertical offset, 14px blur, and 18% opacity; add realistic contact shadow, gentle edge shading, and subtle printed fold shadows without harsh outlines or glossy glare that hides text.
- Surface finish: matte or semi-matte printed packaging texture with subtle paper/plastic grain, tiny ink speckling, slight foil or varnish accents where appropriate, realistic seam pressure marks, and believable light falloff across curved surfaces.
- Layout density: use a realistic retail-package information density with title, subtitle, badges, barcode, nutrition grid, ingredient microcopy, preparation cues, and decorative flavor graphics arranged in a clean but fully designed hierarchy.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio product photography look, 85mm lens at f/8, front-facing composition with mild perspective correction and sharp packaging edges.
- Lighting: large softbox key light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, faint rim separation from the background, even exposure across the package face.
- Color grade: clean commercial product grade with vivid red/orange accents, neutral gray-white background, and slightly lifted highlights for print clarity.
- Rendering detail: high-resolution print mockup realism, readable Korean type, natural shadows in package seams, slight tactile texture on the label, and subtle tabletop realism suitable for a premium branding portfolio.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean FMCG packaging mockup — polished studio still life like a high-end branding portfolio shot, but enriched with real supermarket package details, appetizing spicy flavor graphics, authentic Korean retail microcopy, and believable printed-material realism.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly and clearly on the package artwork: "불꽃 비빔라면", "매콤한 한 입, 강렬한 끝맛".
- Also include realistic Korean package text elements such as "영양정보", "총 내용량 120g", "조리 4분", "HOT LEVEL 4", "진한 양념스프", "소비기한 2026.05.01", "고객상담 080-123-4567" where they fit the design.
- Keep all Korean typography clean, correctly spelled, and fully readable; no broken syllables, mirrored characters, or placeholder gibberish.
- The main {제품 종류} package must remain the clear focal object; any surrounding ingredient cues or tabletop details should support the commercial package shot and never compete with the front label.
- Nutrition label, barcode, QR-like square, and logo areas should remain generic retail design elements, not real official certification marks.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-052.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean ambient and guerrilla advertising mockup, square 1:1 photo-realistic OOH concept image for presentation and portfolio use.
A busy Seoul subway interior scene where a product object is integrated into a public transit handgrip with a small copy label, surrounded by real commuter details, route signage, transit notices, and documentary case-study realism.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main scene: {환경} fills about 80% of the frame with a realistic commuter train interior, seen at eye level with slight wide-angle perspective and enough cabin depth to show poles, straps, windows, seats, route map panels, and passengers.
- Hero integration: {컨셉} is placed as the central creative intervention, attached naturally to the overhead handgrip zone or hanging strap area, so it reads as a surprising but believable ad object discovered during a commute.
- Brand/product label: {브랜드} appears as a small, neatly attached product identifier near the installed object, using the proportions of a real transit sticker or hanging tag, with a tiny QR-style square and micro line such as “출근길 캠페인 2026”.
- Copy placement: {카피} sits as a small caption-style line adjacent to the ad element, aligned like a subway notice tag rather than a billboard headline; add a secondary tiny case-study note in Korean such as “잡는 순간, 시선이 머무는 OOH”.
- Environmental text details: include believable Korean subway signage such as “2호선 시청 방면”, “이번 역은 을지로입구”, “출입문에 기대지 마세요”, priority-seat icons, a small route map strip, and faint overhead ad cards in the background.
- Human interaction: commuter hands are naturally gripping the altered handhold and nearby straps, with varied sleeves, bags, phone screens, and casual body positions; the ad remains clearly visible within a real commuter moment.
- Background treatment: authentic Korean subway cabin materials, stainless poles, gray straps, molded plastic seat backs, emergency intercom panel, safety sticker edges, subtle motion blur outside the windows, slightly worn surfaces, smudges, fingerprints, and realistic reflections.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Establish the subway cabin as the full environmental context, with rows of hanging straps, vertical poles, seated and standing commuters, route maps, safety labels, overhead ads, window reflections, and the visual rhythm of a real Seoul train car.
2. Place the modified handgrip or strap replacement at the visual center, making {컨셉} instantly noticeable while still matching the subway interior’s material logic, weight, scale, and attachment hardware.
3. Attach {브랜드} as a compact product identifier on the object using a small label, printed tag, or sticker, sized like a real transit campaign element with a tiny QR-style mark and micro credit text “AD CASE 052”.
4. Position {카피} immediately beside the object in a tiny ad-note format, keeping the typography clean and legible at close viewing distance; add a small date/location line such as “2026.05 · 서울 지하철 출근길”.
5. Frame commuter hands around the object naturally, ensuring the product integration looks discovered in the environment rather than composited on top, with believable grip pressure, skin texture, sleeves, rings, nails, and motion from the train.
6. Maintain photo-realistic mockup behavior: correct perspective, believable shadows, consistent reflections on metal and plastic, accurate hanging tension, practical sticker edges, scuffed materials, and camera-captured depth.
7. Add realistic presentation richness through background campaign artifacts: one small overhead ad card, a route-map panel, a safety notice, a tiny agency credit line “Creative OOH Study”, and partial commuter objects like a tote bag, earbuds, folded newspaper, and phone screen reflections.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the Korean copy, Medium to Semibold weight, small urban-signage size, crisp and modern, with smaller Regular-weight micro text for date, route, and case-study labels.
- Color palette: subway grays, steel silver, off-white plastic, muted navy accents, yellow safety-label details, soft green route-map accents, and restrained product-brand contrast pulled from {브랜드}.
- Material detail: brushed steel poles, matte rubber straps, translucent plastic handgrips, slightly glossy product surface, vinyl sticker edges, adhesive label thickness, paper notice texture, and subtle grime from everyday commuting.
- Border/shadow: subtle realistic ambient shadow under the installed ad object, 8px y-offset, 18px blur, 20% opacity, matching overhead fluorescent lighting and the physical distance from the strap mount.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame documentary look, 28mm or 35mm lens at f/4, eye-level framing with slight perspective depth, editorial OOH mockup realism.
- Lighting: overhead fluorescent subway lighting with soft even coverage, slight specular highlights on poles and straps, gentle reflections on windows and product surfaces, faint exterior light streaks from the moving tunnel.
- Color grade: cool neutral commuter palette with slightly desaturated grays and controlled product accent color, similar to contemporary advertising case-study photography, with realistic skin tones and subtle film-like grain.
- Image behavior: real captured-photo feeling, crisp central ad object, mild background depth falloff, slight handheld immediacy, natural occlusion from hands and straps, and authentic commuter density.

[6. MOOD]
Cannes Lions ambient OOH case-study aesthetic — a clever public-space product intervention like a high-end agency mockup, balancing realism, wit, everyday Seoul subway texture, and immediate street-level surprise.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: "매일 아침, 잡는 순간 길어진다.", "ROUGE LASH 마스카라".
- Render {카피} as the main small copy line and {브랜드} as the product/brand label; for this entry they must read exactly as the required Korean strings above.
- Additional Korean micro text may appear as realistic environmental signage, for example “2호선 시청 방면”, “2026.05 · 서울 지하철 출근길”, “AD CASE 052”, and “출입문에 기대지 마세요”.
- The subway interior must look physically plausible and photo-realistic, with naturally placed commuter hands, correct grip contact, believable fingers, and authentic train-car scale.
- The ad object must feel embedded in the scene through attachment points, shadows, reflections, occlusion, and material consistency.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-051.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean fashion and beauty catalog lookbook two-page spread, landscape editorial layout for seasonal brand presentation and product storytelling.
Designed as a premium, shareable open-magazine spread with realistic model imagery, chapter typography, product detail callouts, price information, styling notes, and beauty/accessory context that feels like an actual printed catalog.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Two-page spread composition with the center gutter slightly visible as a soft paper crease; overall framing should feel like an open fashion magazine spread photographed flat.
- Left page: a full-body model hero shot occupying about 65% of the page, integrated into a contemporary lifestyle setting such as a sunlit apartment corner, boutique fitting room, studio terrace, or calm urban exterior with real surfaces, furniture, fabric, plants, mirrors, or seasonal styling objects.
- Right page: headline typography in the upper-to-middle area, subtitle beneath it, and 2 product close-up frames stacked or arranged in an editorial grid below, with fabric texture, stitching, cosmetics, accessories, or styling details visible.
- Keep {브랜드}, {시즌}, and {챕터} as the visible editorial anchors, with premium catalog spacing, page rhythm, and realistic print hierarchy.
- Use {색감} as the dominant palette across clothing, makeup accents, props, backdrop, divider lines, and graphic labels, while preserving a bright, airy overall page tone.
- Add authentic catalog details: page numbers, chapter marker, small Korean styling caption, product codes, prices, model-name credit, photographer/stylist credit line, QR/barcode-style catalog block, and a small seasonal note.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background and page base: use an off-white paper surface with subtle print texture, faint ink grain, slightly curved page edges, and a visible center crease, like a high-end magazine spread photographed flat.
2. Left page hero zone: place the model in full-length view, shot naturally with realistic posture and expressive fashion styling; include natural environmental details such as a textured wall, window light, chair, rug, garment rack, table, vase, shopping bag, seasonal flowers, or beauty tools that match the brand world.
3. Left page editorial overlays: include small catalog text near the model image such as “LOOK 03”, “MODEL: 서윤”, “STYLING NOTE”, and a short Korean caption like “가벼운 레이어링으로 완성한 데일리 실루엣”. Add a small page number near the bottom corner, for example “024”.
4. Right page title block: set {챕터} as the largest element in bold editorial English typography, with a smaller Korean subtitle placed directly underneath in a refined hierarchy, for example “이번 시즌의 컬러와 질감을 담은 셀렉션”.
5. Right page product section: add 2 close-up product crops below the title block, each with realistic details and a small code/price label area aligned in grid fashion, for example “JKT-2605 / ₩189,000”, “LIP-041 / ₩32,000”, plus one-line Korean descriptors such as “소프트 트윌 재킷” or “글로우 립 틴트”.
6. Brand and season identifiers: include {브랜드} and {시즌} as masthead-style identifiers near the top or upper corner; add catalog issue details like “VOL.247”, “2026 LOOKBOOK”, “PAGE 024–025”, and a small printed credit line “Photo by H. Kim / Styling by J. Lee”.
7. Realistic print extras: include a small QR/barcode-style block labeled “ONLINE CATALOG”, thin section dividers, micro icons for fabric/care notes, tiny swatch chips in {색감}, and a lower-right footer line with address/contact-style copy such as “seoul showroom · weekly edit”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean text, paired with a clean modern sans-serif for English; title weight 700–800, body and labels 400–500, headline size much larger than subtitle and product text.
- Color palette: build the spread around {색감}, supported by warm off-white #F6F1EA, paper white #FCFBF8, soft charcoal #2B2B2B, muted neutral grays for labels, and tactile seasonal accents drawn from garments, makeup packaging, and props.
- Border/shadow: subtle image separation with 1px hairline rules, printed divider lines, soft white gutters, or gentle paper shadows; if shadows are used, keep them very soft, like 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity.
- Editorial detailing: make all Korean text appear printed on the page, crisp and believable, with real catalog labels, product annotations, page markers, and caption hierarchy rather than placeholder blocks.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial fashion photography look, shot on a full-frame camera with an 85mm f/1.8 for the model hero and a 50mm f/2.8 or 70mm for product detail crops, maintaining realistic proportions.
- Lighting: soft natural daylight from a large window at upper-left, gently diffused, with a faint fill from the opposite side to preserve garment texture, makeup finish, product packaging, paper grain, and skin tone detail.
- Color grade: natural beige + dusty teal + soft white, with restrained contrast, clean highlights, and a lightly desaturated premium look.
- Material realism: show fabric weave, leather grain, satin sheen, cosmetic gloss, paper fibers, tiny printing imperfections, and subtle page curvature for a tactile real-catalog feel.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean fashion and beauty lookbook spread — refined, contemporary, tactile, and editorial, like a real seasonal catalog photographed from a Kinfolk x Cereal magazine styling direction with richer lifestyle detail.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: {브랜드}, {시즌}, {챕터}
- Additional Korean text to render cleanly when included: “이번 시즌의 컬러와 질감을 담은 셀렉션”, “가벼운 레이어링으로 완성한 데일리 실루엣”, “소프트 트윌 재킷”, “글로우 립 틴트”, “온라인 카탈로그”.
- Layout invariant: left page must be a full-body model image; right page must contain the large chapter title, a smaller Korean subtitle, and product close-up frames with code/price labels.
- Maintain the visible center crease between pages and preserve a photo-realistic printed catalog spread structure with page numbers, credits, product labels, and seasonal editorial details.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Incorrect or garbled Korean typography
