[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean event poster for a concert or festival, vertical 9:16 format, designed for social media promotion, street posting, ticket booth signage, and venue entrance publicity.
Bold typography-first poster with a vivid graphic + photo hybrid feel, built to read instantly at thumbnail size while still containing realistic event-poster details such as schedule, ticket note, sponsor strip, and venue guidance.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center composition: {이벤트 이름} dominates the middle 50% of the frame as the main hero typography, with strong visual weight, tight vertical stacking, and a slight neon-lit dimensional treatment.
- Subheader placement: {부제} sits directly below the main title in smaller Korean type, aligned to the same center axis with confident spacing and a clear festival-tagline feel.
- Top area: {이벤트 종류} appears as a small category label near the upper margin, paired with compact poster metadata such as "SEOUL SUMMER NIGHTS", "VOL.07", and "LIVE FESTIVAL POSTER".
- Bottom footer: {날짜}, {장소}, and {라인업} are grouped in a structured footer band across the lower 18–22% of the poster, with date/time, venue, lineup strip, ticket info, and small contact details.
- Background treatment: a night festival atmosphere with layered city lights, dark sky gradients, stage beams, LED screen glow, faint confetti, silhouetted crowd hands, speaker stacks, and performance haze, using diagonal or horizontal division to create motion.
- Framing direction: keep the title unobstructed; background visuals, decorative light trails, and crowd silhouettes should frame and energize the typography without covering the letterforms.
- Add realistic event-poster elements: small sponsor area near the lower edge, QR-code-like ticket block, admission note, venue direction line, and tiny production credits.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background layer — Build a deep night backdrop with a gradient from indigo to near-black, then add blurred Seoul urban light clusters, stage glow, smoke haze, lens bokeh, LED particles, and faint reflections like a real outdoor music festival poster.
2. Mood visual layer — Place a diagonal or broad horizontal visual field of night-sky, city nightscape, silhouetted crowd, raised hands, stage truss, and moving spotlights behind the title, with strong contrast separation for legibility.
3. Title layer — Set {이벤트 이름} in very large, bold display type centered in the frame, occupying about half of the poster height, with sharp edges, high contrast, subtle magenta/cyan glow, and a tactile printed-poster presence.
4. Subtitle layer — Place {부제} beneath the main title in smaller Korean typography, slightly lighter weight, with comfortable line spacing and a clean centered rhythm; include a tiny divider line or dot markers around the subtitle if it supports the design.
5. Event info layer — Add {날짜} and {장소} in the footer area using compact but readable type, aligned left-to-right or stacked in a neat block; also render supporting Korean event details such as "입장 16:00", "공연 18:30", "우천 시 정상 진행", and "예매처 안내".
6. Lineup layer — Render {라인업} as a secondary information row in the footer, using smaller tracking and clear separators so it reads like a lineup strip; add label text such as "LINE UP" and separate artists with bullets, slashes, or vertical bars.
7. Category label — Position {이벤트 종류} near the top as a small descriptor, accompanied by a thin rule, issue-like metadata, and a short English event label such as "SEOUL SUMMER NIGHTS".
8. Ticket and sponsor layer — Add a realistic lower-corner ticket block with "TICKET OPEN", "1일권 ₩88,000", "양일권 ₩149,000", a small QR-like square pattern, and a sponsor/partner row reading "주최 서울라이브랩 · 후원 문화도시서울 · 문의 02-0000-2026".
9. Decorative graphic layer — Add neon line arcs, small starbursts, waveform bars, equalizer blocks, thin grid marks, tiny arrows, and magenta/cyan light leaks to make the poster feel printed, promotional, and content-rich.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the main title, Pretendard Medium for supporting Korean text, and a condensed sans for footer details; main title size should feel oversized and poster-defining.
- Color palette: use deep navy #0B1020, indigo #1A2458, neon cyan #39D5FF, magenta #FF4FD8, and warm white #F5F1E8; keep accents to 1-2 dominant highlights while allowing small warm amber stage-light sparks.
- Border/shadow: apply a subtle soft drop shadow behind the main title, around 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; feather stage haze and crowd silhouettes softly into the background.
- Typography treatment: crisp vector-like edges, strong kerning control, and a slight condensed fit for the footer to maximize information density.
- Poster realism: include small-scale production credits, sponsor text, ticket prices, QR-like code, serial note "POSTER NO. 2026-07", and venue guidance text while keeping all important Korean readable.
- Graphic details: use thin divider rules, micro labels, scanline texture, halftone dots, subtle paper grain, and neon glow overlays to create a realistic premium festival print.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: cinematic wide 24mm look with a shallow depth of field feel, as if shot on a Sony A7R IV with a 24mm f/1.4 lens for the background atmosphere, while keeping the typography razor sharp.
- Lighting: stage backlight mixed with city glow, using cool light from the upper-right and a faint rim light on silhouettes; add magenta side light, cyan laser beams, warm stage bulbs, and glossy haze for a real outdoor concert mood.
- Color grade: high-contrast night palette with electric blue, violet, and pink highlights over a charcoal base, similar to a modern music-festival teaser poster.
- Print finish: subtle matte paper texture with slight ink density variations, gentle glow bloom around neon graphics, and clean digital-poster sharpness for social media readability.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean music festival poster — a Seoul night event graphic with the energetic polish of a major concert teaser, the density of real event publicity, and the stylish finish of contemporary editorial poster design.
It should feel like an actual poster someone would see at a subway station, record shop, campus bulletin board, or on an Instagram event announcement.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "여름밤이 가장 짧은 사람들을 위한", "2026.07.18-19", "한강 노들섬 잔디마당"
- English text accuracy: "SEOUL SUMMER NIGHTS"
- Additional Korean poster text to render cleanly: "입장 16:00", "공연 18:30", "TICKET OPEN", "1일권 ₩88,000", "양일권 ₩149,000", "주최 서울라이브랩", "후원 문화도시서울", "문의 02-0000-2026", "우천 시 정상 진행"
- Layout invariants: the main event name must stay centered and dominant; subtitle must remain directly below it; footer must contain date, venue, and lineup in a clearly separated block.
- Typography must remain clean and fully legible, with no broken Korean characters or accidental letter distortion.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likenesses

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall frame: square 1:1 collage on warm off-white textured paper, with slightly imperfect cut-paper edges, washi tape strips, tracing-paper overlays, small sticky notes, binder-clip shadows, and printed proof-sheet details.
- Main structure: five-zone grid with the largest image anchored at upper-left, palette chips at upper-right, smaller reference photos in the center, typography samples at lower-left, and caption block at lower-right.
- Spacing and framing: use editorial module spacing with believable paper layering, slight overlaps, angled tape corners, and natural alignment variations so the board feels hand-curated and photographed on a real desk.
- Use {캠페인}, {콘셉트}, and {시각 톤} as the visible content cues across headings, labels, captions, handwritten notes, project metadata, and tiny production marks.
- Add realistic deck details: small header line "BRAND MOODBOARD / DRAFT 02", project code "CM-2026-05", date label "2026.05.01", team credit "Creative Team Seoul", model/reference credit "Model Ref. YUNA K.", and a small file note "Internal Concept Sheet".

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Upper-left hero module (about 30%): place the largest mood image as a premium rectangular print with a thin white border, showing either a model, landscape, or lifestyle scene that matches {콘셉트}; add a soft paper shadow beneath it, a small caption strip reading "HERO VISUAL / {콘셉트}", and tiny photo-credit text "photo ref. campaign mood".
- Upper-right palette module (about 18%): show 5 color chips in neat rows with readable HEX codes underneath; base the chips on {시각 톤} and make the swatches matte like printed ink on paper. Include labels such as "MAIN", "SUB", "POINT", "BG", "TEXT" and a small note "시각 톤: {시각 톤}".
- Center reference cluster (about 22%): arrange 3-4 small mood photos in a realistic mini-grid with slightly varied sizes, each with tiny handwritten-style labels that echo {콘셉트}; include notes like "texture", "movement", "space", "detail cut", plus one translucent sticky note reading "콘셉트 키워드".
- Lower-left typography module (about 15%): display two font sample lines, one English and one Korean, using clean editorial specimen formatting with font-name labels, weight notes, size annotations, baseline marks, and sample copy. Set Korean sample text: "나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답" and English sample text: "Quiet Confidence".
- Lower-right caption block (about 15%): set a concise text card summarizing {캠페인} and {콘셉트} in Korean, with short lines stacked like a creative brief. Include visible fields: "브랜드/캠페인: {캠페인}", "콘셉트 키워드: {콘셉트}", "시각 톤: {시각 톤}", "타깃 무드: 25-34 / 감도 높은 일상", and "활용 채널: SNS · OOH · 상세페이지".
- Scatter accents: add small keyword tags, paper stickers, page tabs, crop marks, tiny arrows, pencil underlines, and micro labels around the board so it feels like a real agency working document while remaining premium and readable.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold for Korean labels, Noto Sans KR Regular for body captions, and a refined serif such as Cormorant Garamond or Didot for English sample text; sizing should feel like a presentation board, with headers around 24-32px, section labels around 14-18px, body notes around 12-16px, and micro production text around 8-10px.
- Color palette: translate {시각 톤} into a printable palette of soft peach, warm cream, dusty teal, pale beige, and muted sand; if HEX is shown, use tones like #F6E7DD, #FFF6EC, #A7C3BE, #D8C2A8, #E8D6C8.
- Border/shadow: use thin off-white borders around image prints, with soft drop shadows at 3-4px y-offset, 10-14px blur, and 12-18% opacity; sticky notes, tape pieces, and translucent overlays should have believable shadow separation.
- Paper realism: include visible fiber grain, faint ink absorption, slightly curled photo corners, imperfect scissor-cut edges, light pencil registration marks, and subtle print texture on labels and swatches.
- Content density: make the board feel like a complete creative direction sheet, with readable headings, caption fragments, project metadata, reference tags, and small production notes placed naturally across the collage.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial still-life look shot on a full-frame camera with an 85mm f/1.8 for the main mood photo and a 35mm lens for smaller references, as if photographed for a premium campaign deck.
- Lighting: soft diffused daylight from upper-left, like window light through sheer curtains, with a gentle fill from the right to preserve paper texture and readable text.
- Color grade: warm cream + peach + muted teal grade, slightly desaturated and filmic, with soft contrast and no harsh blacks.
- Rendering: realistic top-down product-still composition with shallow tactile shadows, crisp printed Korean text, realistic paper thickness, and photo prints that look physically placed on the board.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean ad agency concept board — feels like a Kinfolk-style editorial layout mixed with a luxury brand strategy presentation, but with believable working-document details, annotated references, and campaign-ready visual direction for {캠페인}.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구 — "브랜드/캠페인", "콘셉트 키워드", "시각 톤".
- Korean text accuracy: {캠페인}, {콘셉트}, {시각 톤}는 렌더링된 보드 안에서 한글/영문 표기와 함께 자연스럽고 또렷하게 읽혀야 함.
- Additional visible Korean text should include: "나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답", "타깃 무드", "활용 채널", "Creative Team Seoul", "DRAFT 02", and "2026.05.01".
- Layout invariants: keep the 5-zone collage structure recognizable; upper-left hero, upper-right palette chips, center mini-grid, lower-left typography samples, lower-right caption block.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean TV commercial storyboard presentation sheet, 6-cut grid (3×2), for agency pitch, production meeting, and animatic planning.
Create a polished, content-rich storyboard page that feels like a real Seoul advertising agency board: readable shot drawings, production notes, timing cues, audio/copy notes, approval metadata, and tactile sketch-paper materials.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall layout: 3×2 grid of exactly 6 storyboard frames, each frame using a 16:9 thumbnail sketch area with a compact memo box directly beneath it.
- Page structure: brand name and campaign title header at the top, small production metadata line under the title, six numbered frames in reading order left-to-right, top-to-bottom, and a footer centered at the bottom reading {하단 문구}.
- Header details: include {브랜드} prominently, {콘셉트} beneath it, plus small realistic pitch-sheet labels such as “TVC 30초”, “STORYBOARD v1.0”, “2026.05”, “대행사 검토용”, “AE / CW / AD”, and “모델: 가족 A”.
- Subject balance: each frame should feel like a practical ad shot board with living-room props, product interaction, shot direction arrows, SFX marks, timing labels, and handwritten production cues that support {6컷 흐름}.
- Background treatment: sketch-paper texture, slightly warm off-white, with subtle paper grain, faint pencil guide lines, marker bleed, tape marks at a few corners, and light watercolor wash bleed around the panels.
- Footer details: keep {하단 문구} centered, and add tiny deck metadata nearby such as “CLIENT REVIEW”, “PAGE 01 / 01”, “러프 콘티”, and a small rectangular reference-code area.
- Use {브랜드}, {콘셉트}, and {6컷 흐름} as the editable content anchors for the page title and frame planning.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header zone (top 12–14%): place {브랜드} as the main brand header in bold, then set {콘셉트} as the campaign title beneath it in smaller type, both aligned across the page width; add a thin metadata strip containing “TVC 30초 | 6 CUT STORYBOARD | 2026.05 | 대행사 검토용”.
- Frame 1 (top-left): visualize the first beat from {6컷 흐름} as a messy living room establishing shot; include sofa cushions, scattered toys, snack crumbs, a rug, sunlight through curtains, a sleepy parent silhouette, and a small memo box with CAMERA / ACTION / COPY notes in handwritten Korean storyboard style. Add timing label “00:00–00:05” and shot tag “WIDE”.
- Frame 2 (top-middle): depict the second beat from {6컷 흐름} with a hand reaching in and grabbing the vacuum cleaner; keep the shot framing slightly tighter than Frame 1 to emphasize action, showing product handle detail, dust on the floor, an arrow toward the vacuum, and small SFX text “딸깍”. Add timing label “00:05–00:09” and shot tag “INSERT”.
- Frame 3 (top-right): show the third beat from {6컷 흐름} as a fast cleaning motion shot with motion lines, speed streaks, quick sketch marks, lifted dust particles, and a dynamic diagonal composition suggesting energetic movement and product performance. Add timing label “00:09–00:15”, shot tag “TRACKING”, and SFX text “슥—”.
- Frame 4 (bottom-left): render the fourth beat from {6컷 흐름} as the cleaned living room, brighter and tidier, with cushions arranged, rug restored, sunlight glow, a small plant, and a calm composition that contrasts clearly with Frame 1. Add timing label “00:15–00:20” and shot tag “WIDE CLEAN”.
- Frame 5 (bottom-middle): illustrate the fifth beat from {6컷 흐름} with the family seated together in a relaxed room scene, using a medium-wide shot feel and stable composition; include warm facial expressions, tea cups, a pet or child’s toy in the corner, and a small caption cue like “우리집이 다시 편안해지는 순간”. Add timing label “00:20–00:25” and shot tag “FAMILY”.
- Frame 6 (bottom-right): present the sixth beat from {6컷 흐름} as a product close-up plus logo/end card composition, with the product occupying the center, soft hero lighting, a simplified living-room background, {브랜드} lockup area, CTA line such as “지금 만나보세요”, and final supers/copy space. Add timing label “00:25–00:30” and shot tag “END CARD”.
- Memo boxes: under every frame, add a compact technical note block containing CAMERA, ACTION, COPY, SFX, and TIME lines in small handwritten Korean tone, legible and consistent across all six panels.
- Number markers: place each frame number in the top-left corner of its panel, small but clearly visible, matching traditional storyboard layout conventions; add small cut arrows between panels and faint editorial notes such as “CUT”, “DISSOLVE”, or “MATCH CUT” where appropriate.
- Realistic board details: include tiny checkboxes for “촬영”, “CG”, “자막”, small pencil correction marks, circled emphasis notes, and one or two sticky-note style callouts with Korean production reminders like “로고 노출 2초 확보” and “제품 손잡이 강조”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for headers in bold weight, with handwritten Korean memo text in a marker-pen style; frame numbers should be compact sans-serif, and the footer should use a slightly condensed sans-serif.
- Color palette: off-white paper #F4F0E6, graphite black #222222, warm gray #7A736A, muted beige #D8CBB8, soft blue-gray #A9B7C6, watercolor accent wash in pale sage and dusty teal.
- Border/shadow: thin black or dark-gray panel rules, very light hand-drawn irregularity, subtle overlapping paper layers, soft graphite smudges, and gentle shadow separation as if the sheet is placed on a desk for a pitch review.
- Sketch treatment: black marker outlines, loose construction lines, selective watercolor wash fills, visible storyboard arrows, shot-size labels, and presentation-board clarity with rich ad-production detail.
- Text density: include enough small Korean notes to feel like a real working storyboard, while keeping the main labels, frame numbers, and required placeholders clearly readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: storyboard-like commercial previsualization, with each panel framed as a 16:9 shot reference rather than a finished photographic still; emulate a 35mm lens perspective for room shots, 50mm for mid shots, and 85mm for close-up product framing.
- Lighting: neutral studio presentation lighting across the physical sheet; inside panels, imply practical Korean TVC ad lighting with soft window key light, warm home ambience, and brighter hero lighting for the product end card.
- Color grade: muted commercial storyboard grade with warm paper tones, soft watercolor neutrals, pale sage and dusty teal accents, graphite linework, and a realistic scanned/photographed agency-board finish.
- Surface realism: slight paper curl, pencil underdrawing, marker pressure variation, watercolor pooling at panel edges, and small annotation marks that make the board feel actually prepared for client review.

[6. MOOD]
Korean ad agency storyboard presentation — premium Seoul commercial planning board with practical TVC production notes, warm family-home detail, and a believable animatic pitch-deck atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 들어가야 하는 문구: {브랜드}, {콘셉트}, {6컷 흐름}, {하단 문구}, 그리고 각 프레임의 CAMERA / ACTION / COPY 메모 항목 표기.
- 반드시 포함할 추가 한글 표기: “TVC 30초”, “대행사 검토용”, “STORYBOARD v1.0”, “모델: 가족 A”, “로고 노출 2초 확보”, “지금 만나보세요”.
- Layout invariant: exactly 6 frames in a 3×2 grid, each frame with a thumbnail sketch area and a memo box beneath it.
- Frame numbers must appear in the top-left corner of each panel.
- All handwritten Korean memo text must remain legible and correctly formed.
- The sheet must retain the storyboard sketch / animatic feel while adding realistic advertising-board details, production metadata, timing cues, and living-room context.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main product placement: {제품명} occupies the center 52–58% of the frame, shown as a refined hero cut with a slight dynamic tilt, crisp product edges, realistic material detail, and a soft realistic shadow beneath.
- Header zone: top 30–35% contains a small category eyebrow label, {헤드라인} in large Korean typography, and a short support line such as "오늘의 생활을 더 가볍게"; align the type with the product silhouette rather than centering mechanically.
- USP zone: one side column holds {USP 3개} as a vertical stack of exactly three compact icon + label rows, each inside a soft rounded micro-card with clear spacing and consistent alignment.
- Trust-detail zone: add small real-commerce UI details around the hero, such as a review star row "★★★★★ 4.8 · 리뷰 2,431", delivery chip "오늘출발", and compact information tags like "무료배송" or "공식몰 단독 구성" without overpowering the product.
- Footer zone: bottom edge includes a small brand-logo placeholder area plus fine product-meta text such as "OFFICIAL STORE · PRODUCT NO. 047 · 2026 NEW" and tiny customer-service/contact style text.
- Background treatment: smooth neutral cream base with subtle studio-paper texture, faint layered beige panels, soft shadows, and small merchandising accents that support the product page feeling.
- Framing direction: square hero composition optimized for e-commerce PDP/landing-page use, with strong hierarchy, readable mobile typography, and a premium catalog-like rhythm.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero center (mid 55%): {제품명} rendered as the visual focal point, cleanly isolated, slightly angled for depth, with soft contact shadow, realistic highlights, crisp product edges, and subtle reflection on a warm matte surface.
- Header band (top 35%): {헤드라인} set in a large bold Korean sans-serif, spanning 2 lines if needed, with enough tracking to feel premium and readable on mobile; include a small top label "공식 스토어 베스트" and a compact date/product tag "2026 NEW · DAILY CARE".
- USP stack (side column): {USP 3개} presented as exactly three separate micro-cards or icon labels, each with a small line icon, a short Korean label, and a tiny secondary line such as "실사용 기준" or "테스트 완료" in smaller text.
- Commerce info chips: place 2–3 small rounded chips near the product or below the headline: "오늘출발", "무료배송", "리뷰 2,431"; keep them secondary to the headline and product.
- Footer strip (bottom 8–10%): a subtle brand lockup placeholder, tiny barcode-like product management mark, product number, and short customer-trust line such as "정품 보증 · 빠른 상담 · 안전 포장".
- Layout rhythm: use precise grid alignment, layered depth, tactile surface shadows, and realistic product-detail-page elements so the image feels like a finished Korean commerce hero, not a blank mockup.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the headline, weight 700–800, very large size; USP labels in Pretendard Medium 18–24px equivalent; metadata and footer text in 10–14px equivalent.
- Korean commerce text: use concise, realistic phrases such as "공식 스토어 베스트", "오늘출발", "무료배송", "리뷰 2,431", "정품 보증", and "2026 NEW" as supporting microcopy.
- Color palette: neutral cream #F5F1E8, soft warm gray #D8D2C8, charcoal #222222, and one accent color pulled from {컬러 팔레트} used for USP icons, small chips, underline marks, or one callout pill.
- Border/shadow: soft drop shadow 0px 10px 24px at 15% opacity under the product, delicate card shadows for micro-cards, thin warm-gray dividers, no hard outline, no glossy UI frame, no heavy borders.
- UI feel: modern Korean e-commerce landing page with crisp alignment, premium merchandising details, subtle rounded information cards, review indicators, delivery chips, and realistic store-page microcopy.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio product shot on a full-frame body with an 85mm lens at f/5.6, or a 70mm equivalent for a clean compressed hero perspective.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left at about 45°, with a gentle fill from lower-right and a faint rim highlight to separate the product from the background.
- Color grade: warm cream + muted beige + one controlled accent tone, with natural contrast and restrained saturation, similar to polished D2C product photography.
- Material realism: show believable product texture, subtle specular highlights, edge detail, soft paper grain in the background, and natural contact shadows so the page feels photographed and commercially usable.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean e-commerce hero — polished D2C product page aesthetic with the clean merchandising clarity of MUJI-inspired catalog design, modern 29CM editorial layout, and realistic marketplace trust details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "가벼운 한 손, 깨끗한 한 시간.", "가벼움", "강력함", "길어진 사용 시간"
- Layout invariant: exactly one main product hero and exactly three USP items in a vertical stack; supporting commerce details must remain secondary and not duplicate the product.
- Include realistic Korean e-commerce microcopy: "공식 스토어 베스트", "오늘출발", "무료배송", "★★★★★ 4.8 · 리뷰 2,431", "정품 보증 · 빠른 상담 · 안전 포장".
- Keep all Korean text crisp, legible, properly spaced, and free of garbled characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

- Use a refined studio, boutique dressing room, hotel suite, or window-lit interior in muted neutrals, with natural surfaces such as linen curtains, stone wall, polished wood floor, brushed metal rail, leather chair, magazine stack, or a blurred vanity mirror to make the page feel photographed rather than mocked up.

- Add realistic magazine-ad details: small issue/date label such as “VOL.247  2026년 5월호”, tiny page folio “AD PAGE 046”, model-name credit “MODEL. 서윤”, styling/photo credit microtext, and a small barcode/QR-style rectangular information area in the footer.
- Reserve a bottom footer zone for a small brand wordmark placeholder, the line/season code, campaign contact details, and fine-print product text.
- Use {브랜드}, {라인}, {메인 카피}, {시각} as the editable campaign content.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero image area (main 75%): {시각} rendered as a high-end fashion editorial photograph, with the model crisply separated from the background and realistic contact shadows, fabric texture, skin detail, hair strands, jewelry highlights, and subtle edge light to enhance depth.
- Magazine environment layer: include tactile printed-page texture, faint ink grain, slight paper sheen, realistic crop alignment, and small editorial markers like “FASHION ADVERTISING”, “SEOUL / PARIS NOTES”, “2026 S/S CAMPAIGN”, and “p.046” placed as micro typography.
- Margin copy area (side strip): set {메인 카피} in Korean with elegant line spacing, aligned to the chosen side; include a smaller supporting Korean blurb such as “계절의 온도와 실루엣을 따라 완성되는 새로운 균형.”
- Header/brand area: place {브랜드} as a refined wordmark near the top or integrated into the footer, using a restrained luxury-magazine treatment rather than an oversized logo.
- Footer area (bottom 8-12%): set {라인} as a compact English season code, centered or lightly offset, with fine rules, barcode/QR-style block, micro contact line “02-0000-2026  /  brand.kr”, and product/editorial credit text like a real Korean magazine ad colophon.
- Overall page balance: keep one dominant visual anchor and one secondary text anchor, with asymmetrical editorial composition inspired by Vogue Korea, W Korea, Marie Claire Korea, and Esquire Korea print advertising.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean copy, weight 500–700, tight luxury editorial spacing; use a clean condensed sans for the footer season code, 12–24 px equivalent sizing for side copy and 20–36 px equivalent for the footer.
- Add typography hierarchy: brand wordmark largest among text elements but still refined, main copy clearly readable, supporting blurbs smaller, and micro credits printed at true magazine scale.
- Korean text elements may include: “우리는 더 천천히 흐른다.”, “새로운 계절, 가장 조용한 태도”, “서울에서 기록한 오후”, “MODEL. 서윤”, “VOL.247  2026년 5월호”, and “AD PAGE 046”.
- Color palette: muted earth tones from warm beige, soft taupe, stone gray, deep brown, and charcoal black; if needed, anchor with #E8DFD3, #B8A99A, #6F6258, #2B2523, and #111111.
- Border/shadow: avoid heavy borders; use a faint 3–5% opacity print shadow, hairline rules, delicate crop/registration-like marks, or subtle edge separation so the page still feels like a premium print ad.
- Visual detail: allow natural fashion-ad props and textures such as garment seams, leather grain, folded fabric, metal zipper glints, perfume bottle silhouette, editorial tear sheet, or soft curtain folds when they support the campaign image.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 85mm f/1.4 portrait lens look or 70-200mm at ~120mm, editorial fashion framing, shallow depth of field, high-resolution magazine photography.
- Lighting: soft natural window light from one side at 45°, with a gentle fill from the opposite side and a faint rim light catching hair and coat edges; keep contrast elegant, not harsh.
- Color grade: desaturated warm neutrals, cream-beige highlights, brown-gray mids, restrained black shadows, refined Seoul fashion-magazine print color science.
- Material realism: visible fabric weave, paper grain, natural skin texture, realistic makeup finish, polished-but-lived-in interior surfaces, and printed ink density consistent with a luxury Korean magazine page.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean fashion editorial — Vogue Korea and Esquire Korea print campaign energy with a calm, high-fashion, gallery-like presence, enriched by believable magazine details, atmospheric Seoul styling, and tactile print realism.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 다음 문구가 보이게 할 것 — "우리는 더 천천히 흐른다."
- Korean text accuracy: brand wordmark placeholder must render as {브랜드} in a clean luxury editorial style if shown.
- Korean text accuracy: include {메인 카피} as the principal campaign copy, and include {라인} in the footer season/code treatment.
- Layout invariant: the model must remain the dominant subject and should occupy approximately 75% of the page.
- Layout invariant: include a small footer treatment with {라인}, issue/date label, model-name credit, barcode/QR-style information area, and restrained magazine-ad composition.
- Realism invariant: the result should look like a photographed and printed Korean fashion magazine advertisement, not a sterile digital mockup.

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean OOH outdoor advertising design for a subway screen-door panel or bus stop backlit display, ultra-wide landscape billboard composition. Realistic editorial product ad with bold Korean copy, premium skincare placement, transport-station context, backlit acrylic panel texture, and high legibility from a distance.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- 좌측 60%에는 {카테고리}의 시원한 product close-up을 배치하고, 우측 40%는 대형 카피 영역, 브랜드 정보, 캠페인 안내, QR/CTA 영역, 작은 매체 관리 정보로 나눈다.
- 배경은 화이트 베이스에 아주 옅은 파스텔 민트 그라데이션을 사용하되, 실제 {역명} 지하철 스크린도어 또는 버스정류장 광고판처럼 알루미늄 프레임, 강화유리 반사, 은은한 LED 백라이트, 바닥 타일 반사광, 상단 노선 안내 스트립이 보이게 한다.
- 전체 프레이밍은 21:9 초광각 가로 구도처럼 보이게 하며, 광고판 가장자리에는 얇은 금속 프레임, 작은 고정 스크루, 투명 보호 패널의 하이라이트, 하단 스테인리스 몰딩을 넣어 현장 설치된 옥외광고처럼 만든다.
- {브랜드 이름}, {메인 카피}, {서브 카피}는 오른쪽 영역에 명확히 읽히도록 배치하고, 제품 이미지와 카피 사이에는 파스텔 빛 번짐, 수분 입자, 부드러운 그림자, 작은 물방울 하이라이트를 사용해 자연스럽게 연결한다.
- 광고판 하단에는 실제 OOH 매체처럼 {캠페인 기간}, {CTA 문구}, {웹사이트}, {문의 번호}, QR 코드 모양의 작은 사각 영역, 미세한 관리 라벨, {패널 번호}를 추가한다.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Left hero zone (60%): {카테고리} 제품을 고급스럽게 클로즈업한다. 마스크 시트라면 부드럽게 접힌 시트와 촉촉한 물방울, 투명한 수분광, 세럼이 맺힌 가장자리, 반투명 핀셋이나 아크릴 트레이를 함께 보여준다. 스킨케어 패키지라면 깨끗한 용기, 젤/에센스 질감, 반투명 아크릴 받침, 물결 반사, 패키지 라벨의 작은 한글 성분 문구를 포함한다.
- Real OOH environment layer: 광고판 앞면에는 얇은 유리 반사선, 지나가는 사람의 흐릿한 실루엣 반사, 지하철 노선 컬러를 연상시키는 작은 상단 안내 스트립, {역명} 표기, 하단 스테인리스 몰딩, 바닥 타일의 희미한 반사광, 광고판 프레임의 작은 먼지와 지문 흔적을 넣어 실제 역/정류장에 설치된 느낌을 만든다.
- Center transition zone: 좌측 제품과 우측 카피 사이에 옅은 빛 번짐, 수분 미스트, 소프트 그림자, 파스텔 민트 입자, 얇은 곡선형 수분 그래픽을 넣어 광고판 전체가 하나의 완성된 비주얼로 보이게 한다.
- Right copy zone (40%): {메인 카피}를 가장 크게 배치하고, 그 아래에 {서브 카피}를 작은 부제로 정렬한다. 중간에는 {제품 혜택}을 작은 라벨형 문구로 배치하고, 한글 가독성을 우선해 자간을 넉넉히 두며 문장 길이에 따라 2~3줄로 안정적으로 줄바꿈한다.
- Bottom-right brand and info zone: {브랜드 이름}을 브랜드 타이포처럼 배치하고, 주변에 짧은 정보 문구를 추가한다: "NEW", "2026 SPRING CAMPAIGN", "수분 장벽 케어", "{제품 혜택}", "{캠페인 기간}", "{CTA 문구}". 하단 기준선에는 "{문의 번호} · {웹사이트}" 같은 작은 인쇄 광고용 텍스트를 넣는다.
- Transit detail accents: 광고판 좌상단 또는 프레임 상단에 작은 매체 표기처럼 "SCREEN DOOR AD 04", "STATION LINE 2", "{패널 번호}"를 넣고, 하단 모서리에 작은 관리 스티커 형태의 "점검 2026.05", "매체관리 1577-0000", "조명 점등 05:30–24:30" 텍스트를 아주 작게 배치한다.
- QR/CTA detail: 우측 하단의 QR 영역은 실제 스캔 가능한 듯한 흑백 모듈 패턴으로 보이게 하고, 바로 아래에 "지금 체험하기", "공식몰 혜택 확인", "첫 구매 샘플 증정" 같은 작은 안내 문구를 넣어 실사용 광고처럼 만든다.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard 또는 Noto Sans KR, headline은 ExtraBold 96–140pt, subcopy는 Medium 28–40pt, brand text는 SemiBold 20–28pt, micro info text는 Regular 12–18pt. 한글은 명확한 획과 넓은 자간으로 옥외광고 가독성을 확보한다.
- Color palette: soft pastel mint #DDF3EE, ice white #F7FAFC, cool gray #D9E1E8, accent color from the ad concept as a single vivid point color, plus deep charcoal #1E1E1E for text. Metal frame uses brushed silver gray and glass reflections use pale cyan highlights.
- Border/shadow: 제품 아래에 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 16% opacity의 부드러운 그림자를 넣고, 광고판 프레임에는 얇은 금속 하이라이트와 유리 반사선을 더한다. 텍스트 영역은 선명한 인쇄물처럼 보이게 하며, 백라이트 패널의 은은한 광량을 유지한다.
- Layout realism: 실제 옥외광고처럼 큰 카피, 작은 캠페인 정보, QR 영역, 프레임 스크루 디테일, 보호 유리의 미세한 먼지와 반사, 역명/패널번호/점검라벨을 균형 있게 포함하되 메인 카피의 가독성이 가장 먼저 보이게 한다.
- Print and installation finish: 백라이트 필름에 인쇄된 듯한 아주 미세한 도트 질감, 아크릴 패널의 두께감, 프레임 모서리의 약한 마모, 유리 위 대각선 하이라이트를 추가해 렌더링이 아니라 실제 설치 사진처럼 보이게 한다.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 85mm f/1.8 product close-up on full-frame, or Phase One IQ4 with 80mm lens for ultra-clean commercial detail.
- Lighting: soft studio softbox from upper-left at 45° with gentle fill from front-right, plus subtle backlight to make droplets and packaging edges pop; realistic backlit ad-panel brightness feel with mild reflections on tempered glass and polished station floor.
- Color grade: airy pastel commercial grade with cool white highlights, soft mint accents, refined saturation, and slight real-world contrast from metal frame shadows, similar to premium Korean skincare campaign imagery installed in a modern subway station.
- Real-world camera feel: 광고판을 약간 사선에서 바라보는 현장 촬영 느낌으로, 프레임은 선명하고 배경의 승강장/정류장 구조물은 살짝 흐리게 처리해 실제 옥외 매체를 촬영한 사진처럼 만든다.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean subway OOH campaign — polished backlit skincare advertising seen in a real station or bus shelter, with crisp Korean typography, luminous product texture, believable public-space details, clean reflective glass, and refined editorial commercial presence.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: "{메인 카피}", "{서브 카피}", "{브랜드 이름}".
- Additional Korean micro-copy must appear clearly where appropriate: "{제품 혜택}", "{캠페인 기간}", "{CTA 문구}", "{웹사이트}", "{문의 번호}", "{역명}", "{패널 번호}".
- 브랜드명 {브랜드 이름}은 우하단에 텍스트 중심으로 표현하고, 제품 광고에 어울리는 프리미엄 타이포그래피로 정돈한다.
- 전체 구성은 좌측 제품 60% / 우측 카피 40% 비율을 유지하고, 한글 카피가 광고판 프레임이나 반사광에 가려지지 않도록 배치한다.
- QR 코드, 캠페인 기간, 광고 문의, 점검 라벨, 상단 노선 안내 스트립은 실제 지하철·버스정류장 광고 매체처럼 작지만 읽을 수 있는 수준으로 배치한다.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-044.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean human-comedy family movie poster, vertical 9:16 theatrical key art for an emotional but playful domestic-release campaign.
Designed to feel like a warm neighborhood story poster with broad audience appeal, suitable for cinema one-sheet, streaming promo, social teaser use, lobby display, and online ticketing thumbnail.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main character grouping: the {시각 컨셉} occupies the central 60% of the frame, with the emotional focal point placed slightly above center for poster readability.
- Title zone: {영화 제목} dominates the upper third in large handwritten Korean lettering, while {영문 부제} sits directly beneath in a smaller clean sans-serif line.
- Supporting text area: {장르} and {태그라인} are stacked in balanced spacing near the lower third, joined by realistic theatrical poster details such as release date, short review-style blurbs, cast-name credits, and a compact billing block.
- Background treatment: a nostalgic Korean neighborhood alley with warm plaster walls, faded signboards, utility wires, potted plants, laundry lines, a parked scooter, delivery boxes, worn doorplates, and soft late-afternoon sunlight, rendered with gentle depth separation and lively everyday detail.
- Framing direction: strong vertical poster framing with readable poster hierarchy, letting the title, characters, props, neighborhood texture, and promotional text all feel integrated like a real Korean cinema one-sheet.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background layer — A lived-in Korean alleyway with old low-rise homes, muted wall textures, green window frames, peeling paint, sunlit utility wires, small restaurant signage, ceramic plant pots, slippers near a doorway, and a slightly blurred distance to create cinematic depth; warm peach and soft yellow light wash across the scene.
2. Character anchor — The {시각 컨셉} placed on a wooden mat or low neighborhood bench, with the older man and child interacting naturally, smiling and leaning toward each other; add believable wardrobe textures such as a faded cardigan, patterned child backpack, comfortable sneakers, and slightly wrinkled everyday clothing.
3. Prop accents — A bowl of tteokbokki, a small vintage radio, paper cups, a plastic market bag, a handwritten snack-shop receipt, and a few everyday street details placed near the characters as emotionally recognizable Korean-life cues.
4. Title build — {영화 제목} set as the largest element in the upper area, with thick brush-like strokes, subtle paper texture, slight ink spread, and strong contrast against the sunlit sky or wall.
5. Subtitle line — {영문 부제} aligned under the Korean title in compact uppercase, clean letterspacing, and restrained sizing so it supports rather than competes.
6. Descriptor stack — {장르} and {태그라인} positioned in the lower zone with poster-like rhythm, using neat spacing and a friendly family-film tone; add short Korean feature blurbs around them: “웃다가 울컥하는 우리 동네 이야기”, “세대 공감 100%”, “올봄, 가장 따뜻한 만남”.
7. Release and credits — Add realistic movie-poster information: large date label “2026.05 대개봉”, small top teaser line “그 골목에서 시작된 뜻밖의 가족”, cast credit strip “김덕수 · 이나은 · 박철민 · 정유진”, director credit “감독 한지우”, and a narrow bottom billing block with dense Korean production text, distributor line, website, and social handle “@woorijip_movie”.
8. Decorative finish — Include subtle ticket-stub graphics, tiny heart doodles drawn on a wall poster, a small torn flyer reading “동네잔치”, warm lens flare dust, mild film grain, and a slightly nostalgic print-poster texture so the whole composition feels like a Korean movie one-sheet from a heartfelt ensemble comedy.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use hand-drawn brush-style Korean lettering for {영화 제목}, with bold weight and very large size; use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for {영문 부제}, {장르}, {태그라인}, release date, cast names, and billing text, with varied weights matching real theatrical poster hierarchy.
- Color palette: warm peach, soft yellow, toasted brown, muted cream, and sunset orange; keep the palette anchored by the exact tones described in the original concept and avoid harsh saturated reds.
- Poster typography details: title may overlap the warm sky-wall area; release date should be bold and centered near the bottom; billing block should be tiny but visibly structured like real film credits.
- Border/shadow: subtle printed-poster edge shadow, 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; title text may have a faint ink spread or paper emboss feel, but no heavy beveling.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 look with 35mm lens at f/2.8 for a natural street-level cinematic perspective, or a 50mm equivalent for a slightly compressed character-focused poster framing.
- Lighting: golden hour sunlight from upper-left at roughly 45°, with soft reflected fill from the right side and a gentle rim light outlining the figures and props.
- Color grade: warm peach + soft yellow + toasted brown with a lightly faded film print curve, keeping skin tones natural and neighborhood textures nostalgic but not oversaturated.
- Realism: photographic character rendering with expressive faces, believable skin texture, natural smiles, imperfect alley surfaces, dust in sunbeams, and tactile food/prop detail; blend the graphic title and credits seamlessly over the cinematic photo base.

[6. MOOD]
Korean family comedy drama poster with the heartfelt ensemble warmth of 7번방의 선물 and 국제시장, plus the approachable neighborhood humor energy of 극한직업 and 과속스캔들.
The final image should feel like a real commercial poster seen outside a neighborhood cinema: funny, affectionate, slightly tearful, full of familiar Korean everyday life, and inviting for all ages.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함
  - 우리집 건너 그 사람
  - 휴먼 코미디 · 가족
  - 그래도 사람 사는 게 좋아서요.
- Additional Korean poster text to render clearly where space allows:
  - 2026.05 대개봉
  - 그 골목에서 시작된 뜻밖의 가족
  - 웃다가 울컥하는 우리 동네 이야기
  - 김덕수 · 이나은 · 박철민 · 정유진
  - 감독 한지우
  - @woorijip_movie
- Layout invariants: keep the old neighborhood alley setting, the older man + young granddaughter pairing, and the tteokbokki + radio props clearly visible; preserve a vertical 9:16 poster composition.
- The image must feel family-friendly, emotional, and lightly comedic, with a rich Korean neighborhood atmosphere and realistic theatrical poster production value.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Asymmetric vertical composition: the upper 60% is dominated by two {시각 컨셉} figures, while the lower 40% holds tagline, main title, English subtitle, release date, billing block, and small cinema-poster information.

- Use {영화 제목}, {영문 부제}, {시대}, {장르}, {태그라인}, {시각 컨셉} as the content anchors.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Upper hero area (top 60%): render {시각 컨셉} as a dramatic medium shot with rich hanbok fabric detail, accurate collar folds, embroidery, layered silk texture, jade norigae, hairpin ornaments, faint moisture on fabric edges, and realistic skin detail; the two figures should appear in side profile or a slight 3/4 angle, facing each other with restrained emotion.
2. Top poster information layer: place a small refined line near the top such as "2026년 겨울 대개봉" and a compact label like "{시대} {장르}"; add one short critic-style Korean line, for example "운명은 가장 고요한 밤에 칼끝처럼 흔들린다", set small enough to feel like real promotional copy.
3. Lighting and silhouette layer: add moonlit backlight behind the figures to carve clean silhouettes, with a cool blue edge light and a restrained warm gold rim light on the cheeks, sleeves, hair ornaments, and embroidered seams; allow lantern reflections and courtyard haze to create depth.
4. Atmosphere layer: place thin drifting mist through the courtyard, with cherry blossom petals crossing diagonally from upper-right to lower-left; include a faint moon disc, soft particulate glow, wet stone highlights, shadowed wooden pillars, and distant palace roof tiles while keeping the main faces readable.
5. Mid-lower text field (middle 30%): place {태그라인} as a small poetic quote near the figures, using a refined high-contrast Korean serif style with wide tracking, so it feels like an excerpt from a prestige film poster; add 2–3 short Korean feature blurbs nearby, for example "왕의 침묵", "금지된 서신", "달빛 아래 맺은 약속".
6. Bottom title block (lower 10%): set {영화 제목} as the dominant title in a large dramatic Korean serif with slight brush-calligraphy influence; place {영문 부제} directly beneath in a thin serif, followed by small cast/director-style credit lines, release details, production/distribution line, ticket information, and a tiny barcode/QR-style rectangle at the lower corner.
7. Real poster micro-details: include a believable billing block such as "감독 김도윤  각본 한서린  촬영 박재오  음악 이현  미술 조윤경", fictional cast names such as "이도현 · 한서아 · 문정혁", a release line "12월 극장 대개봉", ticket copy "예매 오픈 2026.11.20", website "www.moonpalace-film.kr", and a small sponsor/production area reading "제작 달궁필름  배급 한빛픽처스".

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for small credits, Sandoll Myoungjo / Korean serif display styling for the main title, and a thin serif such as Cormorant Garamond or Baskerville for the English subtitle; title weight should feel bold but elegant, around 70–90 pt equivalent, with tight vertical balance and clear legibility.
- Korean text hierarchy: {영화 제목} must be the largest text; {영문 부제} directly supports it; {태그라인} should read like a poetic pull quote; secondary poster copy such as "2026년 겨울 대개봉", "12월 극장 대개봉", and "예매 오픈 2026.11.20" should be smaller but crisp.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame cinematic portrait look, 85mm f/1.8 or 105mm portrait lens with shallow depth of field, crisp fabric detail and softly separated background.
- Lighting: moonlit night scene with a soft key from upper-left, cool backlight from behind the subjects, and a faint warm bounce to preserve facial structure; mist should catch the light naturally without overexposure.
- Color grade: prestige historical drama grade with indigo shadows, subdued plum mids, and restrained antique-gold highlights; slightly desaturated blacks, filmic contrast, and a subtle painterly finish on the faces and hanbok.
- Realism: faces, hands, hair ornaments, hanbok seams, courtyard wood grain, roof tiles, wet stone, petals, and typography should feel integrated into one believable theatrical key art image rather than a flat mockup.

[6. MOOD]
Prestige Korean period romance poster — a theatrical historical drama with the emotional gravity, political secrecy, moonlit longing, and cinematic polish of major Korean sageuk one-sheets.

[7. CRITICAL]

- Korean text accuracy: all visible Korean characters must be clean, correctly formed, and free of garbling or broken glyphs.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean independent art-house film poster for a quiet family drama, vertical 9:16 format for theatrical key art, local cinema display, and festival submission.
Create a real-looking printed movie poster with emotionally rich domestic detail, believable Korean typography, production billing, release information, and a warm photographic still that feels like a captured moment from the film.
Balanced, reflective composition with photo-realistic warmth and restrained typography, inspired by Korean indie cinema poster design.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the main family dinner scene as the visual anchor, occupying about 55% of the frame, with the title zone in the upper 18% and credits/lower billings in the bottom 12%.
- Background: a Korean middle-class detached house garden at dusk, with a dining table near a glowing window, old wooden window frames, potted plants, a low garden wall, faint laundry line silhouette, porch light, soft garden shadows, and slightly textured film-poster paper look with a matte printed finish.
- The dinner table should feel lived-in and natural: rice bowls, small banchan plates, soup pot, metal chopsticks, water glasses, folded napkins, a worn floral tablecloth, and subtle steam catching the dusk light.
- Use {영화 제목}, {영문 부제}, {장르}, {태그라인}, {시각 컨셉} as the editable text and scene-description anchors.
- Add authentic movie-poster information around the scene: release date label, small screening/ticket line, production company names, director/cast credits, and a tiny poster code or catalog number near the bottom edge.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top title area: Set {영화 제목} large and centered, using a refined modern serif or bold Myeongjo style, with crisp Korean kerning and strong vertical presence.
- Subtitle line: Place {영문 부제} directly below the main title in a smaller uppercase sans serif, spaced out subtly for an art-film feel.
- Genre label and tagline zone: Place {장르} as a compact label near the title or upper-right corner; set {태그라인} in a smaller line near the mid-lower area, aligned with the poster’s calm rhythm.
- Main image area: Render {시각 컨셉} as a photo-realistic dinner scene with exactly 4 family members seated naturally, warm dusk light from the window, thoughtful expressions, and no melodramatic gesture.
- Festival / screening details: Add 2–3 clearly fictional festival-style laurels or selection lines, such as “제12회 작은영화주간 초청” and “관객의 밤 상영작”, placed near the upper corners or above the title without resembling an official government seal.
- Release and ticket info: Include a compact line such as “2026.05.01 대개봉”, “저녁 7시 특별 상영”, “예매: 독립영화관 현장 및 온라인”, and “상영관: 서울아트시네마 2관” in small Korean text near the lower third.
- Billing block: Add narrow condensed bottom credits with realistic Korean film-poster wording: “감독 김도윤  출연 한지우 박성민 윤서아 최민재  제작 봄밤필름  배급 고요픽처스”. Include a small model-name / photo-credit style line such as “Still Photography: LEE HANEUL / Poster Design: STUDIO EVENING”.
- Sponsor / partner area: Add a small horizontal sponsor strip at the bottom with fictional text marks only, such as “봄밤필름 · 고요스튜디오 · 동네극장 프로젝트”, separated by thin dividers.
- Decorative graphic elements: Use subtle window-grid lines, small pressed-leaf motifs, faint handwritten date marks, and a tiny ticket-stub icon integrated into the printed poster texture.
- Overall integration: Blend the text and image with poster-like hierarchy so the family scene supports the typography while still feeling like a complete theatrical one-sheet.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo for {영화 제목} at heavy weight, and Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for {영문 부제}, {장르}, release details, screening info, and billing text at light/medium weight; title size should dominate, subtitle around one-third the title height.
- Color palette: muted earth tones, amber dusk, warm cobalt shadow, deep brown, soft beige, and subdued olive; keep saturation low and contrast gentle.
- Text hierarchy: Main title must be readable from a distance; secondary Korean details should look authentic as printed poster text, with proper spacing, alignment, and clean Hangul rendering.
- Printed finish: use subtle vignette, fine paper grain, tiny ink absorption, and soft printed-poster shadow only if needed; avoid hard outlines, neon glows, or glossy gradients.
- Layout realism: include believable margins, imperfect photographic depth, natural household details, and production typography that makes the poster feel physically printed and ready for a cinema lobby.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: cinematic 50mm or 85mm lens look, full-frame, shallow-to-moderate depth of field, poster-grade realism with a composed still-photography feel.
- Lighting: soft window light from the right-rear at dusk, with diffused amber fill from the sky and a faint cool cobalt shadow in the darker areas; no harsh spotlight.
- Color grade: faded earth-brown + dusk amber + muted blue-shadow grade, similar to a restrained Korean festival drama still with gentle film emulation.
- Photographic detail: realistic skin tones, believable seated posture, soft reflections on metal chopsticks and bowls, fabric texture on clothing, dim garden greenery, and subtle interior light spilling through the window.

[6. MOOD]
A quiet Korean family-drama poster with the reflective, human-scale emotional restraint of an Arthouse Cinema One-sheet, like the understated mood of Lee Chang-dong and Kore-eda without copying any specific scene.
The image should feel like one ordinary evening remembered years later: warm food, unsaid words, familiar silence, and the gentle melancholy of home.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly and cleanly in the rendered image: "해 질 무렵의 집", "가족 드라마", "우리 모두 지나온 어떤 저녁의 풍경."
- Preserve all editable anchors exactly: {영화 제목}, {영문 부제}, {장르}, {태그라인}, {시각 컨셉}.
- Family scene invariants: show exactly 4 family members at the dinner table, with natural anatomy and believable seated poses; expressions should remain calm, thoughtful, and emotionally restrained.
- Poster hierarchy must remain vertical and film-poster-like, with the title clearly legible and the scene supporting the typography.
- Add realistic Korean poster microcopy such as “2026.05.01 대개봉”, “예매: 독립영화관 현장 및 온라인”, “감독 김도윤”, and “제작 봄밤필름” as small supporting text.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean casual SD RPG mobile game ad banner, 1:1 square format, lively app-store and social-feed promo graphic for install and pre-registration conversion.
Board-game-like isometric plan view with cute collectible heroes, pets, reward UI, event callouts, and a playable-looking pastel fantasy field that feels like an actual mobile game launch advertisement.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall framing: 1:1 square composition with an isometric top-down view, designed as a compact mobile-game advertisement with real app-ad details, layered UI stickers, reward badges, and readable Korean promotional text.
- Main scene placement: 5–6 small SD heroes and pets are distributed across the center and lower-middle area, each in a different lively pose so the eye travels around the whole frame; include a tiny healer, warrior, mage, archer, mascot pet, treasure pet, and a few animated-looking effect trails.
- Title placement: {게임 제목} sits large at the top center in bold rounded Korean cartoon lettering with a thick navy outline, soft drop shadow, small sparkle highlights, and a tiny “NEW OPEN” ribbon tucked near the title.
- CTA placement: a large rounded button sits at the bottom center, with high contrast and easy tap-readability; button text reads “지금 다운로드” and is clearly separated from the playable scene, with a small “무료 설치” tag and store badge row nearby.
- Feature presentation: four floating speech-bubble icons are placed near the characters, each bubble containing one concise feature line; add tiny related icons such as sword, gem, pet paw, treasure chest, or dice.
- Background treatment: pastel grass field blended with a tiny village edge and dungeon entrance, rainbow sky accents, cloud puffs, sparkle particles, star confetti, stone path tiles, signboards, reward chests, potion bottles, coin piles, and small UI markers so the ad feels content-rich and game-like.
- Use {메인 비주얼}, {배경}, {feature 1}, {feature 2}, {feature 3}, {feature 4}, {장르 라벨}, {태그라인}, {출시 정보} placeholders naturally in the ad layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header zone (upper 18%): place {게임 제목} at the exact top center, oversized, with thick outline and a subtle shadow so it reads instantly on mobile; add small supporting labels around it such as “VOL.01 런칭 기념”, “신규 서버 오픈”, and a tiny decorative crown icon.
2. Genre and tagline cluster (upper-left or upper-right small block): stack {장르 라벨} above {태그라인} in a compact promo-copy arrangement, using smaller but still bold rounded type; include a pill-shaped “전체 이용가” rating tag and a tiny “사전예약 보상 지급” chip beside it.
3. Main character field (middle 55%): render {메인 비주얼} as a cheerful grouped scene of chibi heroes and pets, with each character separated enough to be individually readable; include hand wave, jump, idle victory pose, spell-casting pose, treasure-opening pose, and pet reaction poses.
4. World surface (middle-to-lower area): paint {배경} as a pastel fantasy map surface with soft grass texture, cobblestone paths, small village props, a cozy shop sign, mailbox, mushroom cluster, glowing portal, mini dungeon gate, and tiny quest arrows, all simplified to match SD game UI art.
5. Feature bubbles (around characters): show {feature 1}, {feature 2}, {feature 3}, {feature 4} in four floating speech bubbles or icon callouts, each bubble anchored near a different hero/pet group for visual balance; add small readable secondary micro-copy such as “매일 보상”, “자동 전투”, “펫 수집”, “협동 던전”.
6. CTA zone (bottom 14%): place a large rounded install button with strong contrast and clear button depth; place app-store-style badges beside or below it in a tidy app-ad layout, plus tiny UI labels “무료 설치”, “쿠폰 입력”, “출석 보상”, and a red notification dot.
7. Release note strip (bottom edge): add {출시 정보} as a small but legible status line under the CTA area; include a fine-print event strip reading “런칭 7일 보상 · SSR 영웅 선택권 · 3,000젬 지급” and a compact coupon label “WELCOME2026”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a rounded Korean sans-serif such as Pretendard Rounded or Noto Sans KR Rounded for UI text, with heavy weight for the title and medium weight for feature labels; title size should feel like a banner masthead, while UI copy remains compact and readable.
- Color palette: vivid rainbow pastel set with pink #FF7AB6, mint #8BE6D1, yellow #FFE36E, lilac #BFA7FF, sky blue #79C7FF, plus warm white #FFF9F2 and deep navy outline #2B2B44.
- Borders/shadow: thick cartoon outlines on characters and UI, soft drop shadows on title and CTA button, 4px vertical offset with 14px blur at about 18% opacity for layered pop.
- Icon style: speech bubbles, reward chips, store badges, coupon tags, and feature icons should be glossy, rounded, tactile, and game-like, with tiny sparkle accents, gem highlights, coin glints, and soft sticker edges.

1. Background field: build a sweeping fantasy vista with mountain ridges, bright dawn sky, and drifting magical particles; the scenery should feel dominant and expansive, with layered clouds and a subtle luminous horizon.
2. Title zone (top center): set {게임 제목} in oversized Korean display type with strong contrast and a slight glow edge; place {장르 라벨} as a smaller English subtitle directly beneath it, aligned centrally.
3. Tagline block: place {태그라인} under the title stack or slightly offset near the upper-left of the title area, using compact but highly legible typography.
4. Hero zone (lower center): render {영웅} as a full-body fantasy character standing on a rocky ledge or light platform, small relative to the landscape, with heroic posture and a visible weapon, surrounded by soft magical rim light.
5. Feature row (bottom center): display {feature 1}, {feature 2}, {feature 3} as evenly spaced circular or shield-shaped icons with short labels, using bright pictograms and clean spacing.
6. Promotion zone (lower-right): place {출시 정보} and the CTA button together, with the CTA as the most clickable element; include Google Play / App Store badge cues in a compact stacked arrangement.
7. Atmospheric overlays: add subtle lens bloom, spark particles, and a faint magic circle behind the hero to unify the composition without overpowering the text.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for {게임 제목}, Pretendard SemiBold for {태그라인} and {출시 정보}, and a clean sans-serif for {장르 라벨}; title size should feel billboard-like, with tight kerning and high stroke thickness.
- Color palette: vibrant gold #D6B15A, cobalt blue #2557D6, magenta #D84FA6, deep navy #0E1730, pale sky #EAF3FF, warm highlight #FFE7A3.
- Border/shadow: add a soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity behind the title stack; CTA button should have a beveled glossy edge and 2px outline for app-ad readability.
- Use strong contrast between the title and sky, with subtle outer glow in pale gold; feature chips should have crisp icon circles with thin luminous borders.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: cinematic wide shot, virtual 24mm lens at f/5.6 with deep focus, poster-like perspective, low viewpoint slightly below the hero for scale.
- Lighting: golden sunrise backlight from the upper-left, cool fill from the front-right, soft rim light around the hero, and gentle volumetric rays through the clouds.
- Color grade: epic fantasy teal-and-gold grade with cobalt shadows, magenta accent sparks, and bright dawn highlights, similar to high-end Korean MMORPG promotional key art.

[6. MOOD]
High-budget Korean MMORPG launch banner — polished fantasy game poster energy with the dramatic scale of a Netmarble / NCSoft-style ad creative.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문자열이 정확히 보여야 함.
  - {게임 제목}
  - {태그라인}
  - {출시 정보}
  - {feature 1}
  - {feature 2}
  - {feature 3}
  - 사전예약 받기
  - 지금 다운로드
- Layout invariant: the hero must be small and located near the lower center, not the left/right side hero-ad layout.
- The title must remain at the top center with the fantasy landscape dominant behind it.
- The image must show the full body of the hero character.
- No blood, gore, or realistic violence; combat must be abstracted into light effects.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Real-world IP infringement or copied game characters
- Left-text / right-character ad layout
- Excessive clutter that makes the title unreadable
- Blood, gore, dismemberment, or explicit violence

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean vertical scroll webtoon short comic, 5-6 stacked panels, emotional reunion scene for mobile reading.
Designed as a realistic, content-rich 9:16 webtoon page with cinematic pacing, expressive adult characters, readable Korean dialogue, and a finished episode-page feel.
Include small webtoon publishing details such as an episode label, short title caption, author credit, subtle sound effects, station signage, and a tiny footer teaser without changing the central story.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- The page is a vertical scroll layout with 5-6 horizontal panels stacked top-to-bottom, each panel about 16:9 wide, separated by thin off-white webtoon gutters.
- Add a narrow top header strip before the first panel: “EP.12 비 오는 밤”, small credit text “글·그림 {캐릭터}”, and a tiny date label “2026.05.01 연재”.
- Keep the emotional payoff in the final panel, with the strongest facial expression and the clearest visual resolution.
- Backgrounds are grounded in realistic Seoul subway interiors and rainy-night city atmosphere: route map stickers, priority-seat icons, hand straps, LED station display, window raindrops, wet platform reflections, small subway ads, and believable bench shadows.
- Speech bubbles and caption boxes should feel naturally integrated into the panels, with clear placement that supports mobile reading while still allowing rich subway details around the characters.
- Use {주제} as the central story premise, {캐릭터} as the character setup, {흐름} as the panel-by-panel narrative, and {무드} as the overall color mood.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Opening panel: a nearly empty subway car on a rainy night, cool blue window reflections, blurred neon city lights outside, raindrops streaking across the glass, overhead hand straps, route map, a small LED sign reading “다음 역: 을지로입구”, and a caption box: “비가 그치지 않던 밤.” Wide framing establishes loneliness and the late-night commute.
2) Second panel: one character enters and sits down, coat slightly damp, folded umbrella with water droplets, messenger bag or office tote, tired adult-office-worker posture. Add subtle SFX text like “툭, 툭” near dripping rainwater and a small train-door warning sticker in the background.
3) Third panel: the seated character notices the person beside them, subtle head turn and eye-line shift, close-up crop with reflected city lights in the window and believable facial tension. Include a small inner-caption box: “설마…”
4) Fourth panel: dialogue beat with the reveal line, tighter two-shot composition, both faces visible under cool fluorescent light. Set Korean speech bubbles clearly, for example: “오랜만이야.” / “정말… 너야?” Add background details like a subway advertisement strip and the route-line color band.
5) Fifth panel: both characters soften into a small smile, one holding an umbrella, hands nearly touching on the seat edge or around the umbrella handle, body language relaxed. Warm facial highlights contrast with the cold train interior. Add a tiny caption: “말하지 못했던 시간이, 천천히 풀렸다.”
6) Final panel: emotional payoff of leaving together at the station exit or platform doorway, stronger warmth in the framing, slightly closer crop, clear shared movement and closure. Show wet platform tiles, yellow safety line, open train doors, umbrella opening, and amber city light beyond the exit. Include the final Korean line: “같이 갈까?” and a small footer teaser: “다음 화에 계속 · ♥ 12,483”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Korean webtoon dialogue in clean sans-serif like Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, medium weight for speech bubbles, smaller regular weight for captions, highly legible at mobile size.
- Add realistic webtoon micro-text: episode label, short caption boxes, subtle SFX such as “스륵”, “툭”, “삐—”, station sign text, and tiny footer UI-style text, all in correct Korean.
- Color palette: use {무드} with warm amber, midnight navy, rainy cyan, soft gray-white, and gentle skin-tone highlights; keep whites slightly off-white instead of pure white.
- Border/shadow: thin off-white panel dividers, soft cel-shading on characters, delicate linework, subtle shadow under benches and bodies, refined rim light on damp coats and umbrella edges.
- Character continuity: the same two adult office workers must remain visually consistent across all panels, with repeated clothing, hairstyle, facial proportions, and accessories.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: manga/webtoon cinematic framing with 35mm and 50mm equivalent perspective, occasional close-up crop for dialogue beats, no distortion-heavy wide-angle look.
- Lighting: cool fluorescent subway interior light mixed with soft blue reflections from rainy windows, then a warmer amber accent on the characters’ faces in the later panels.
- Color grade: urban night palette with blue rain reflections balanced by amber skin highlights and a slightly warm final panel for emotional release.
- Rendering: polished Korean romance/drama webtoon finish, semi-realistic anatomy, expressive eyes, natural wrinkles in coats, damp fabric texture, soft reflected highlights on metal poles, glossy wet floor reflections, and cinematic panel rhythm.

[6. MOOD]
Korean webtoon emotional reunion sequence — like a quiet Naver Webtoon romance/drama episode with a subtle cinematic K-drama still feel.
The mood should feel intimate, rainy, nostalgic, and believable, with small environmental details making the reunion feel like it happens in a real late-night Seoul subway.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: every speech bubble, caption, sign, SFX, footer label, and episode label must render clean, correct Korean characters.
- Must reflect the exact story beats from {흐름} across 5-6 panels.
- Include Korean text such as “EP.12 비 오는 밤”, “비가 그치지 않던 밤.”, “오랜만이야.”, “정말… 너야?”, “같이 갈까?”, and “다음 화에 계속” where appropriate.
- Keep the final panel as the emotional payoff with clear shared movement, warm lighting, and readable dialogue.
- Characters must look like adult office workers in their 30s, with believable subway posture, natural expressions, consistent identity, and grounded clothing details.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-032.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean 6-panel manhwa page, 3×2 grid layout, designed as a single-page daily-life comedy comic for easy reading.
Create a complete square webtoon-style comic page with a believable printed/webtoon presentation: title strip, episode/date micro text, consistent characters, clear Korean speech bubbles, office-lunch details, and punchline timing across six cells.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall page structure: strict 3 columns × 2 rows of equal-sized panels, with thin black borders between cells and a tidy outer comic-page frame suitable for a 1024×1024 square.
- Page header details: add a slim top title band above or integrated into the grid area with short Korean title text such as '오늘의 점심 회의', small label 'EP.032', date label '2026.05.01', and tiny creator credit '글·그림 우리팀'. Keep these elements secondary to the panels.
- Character placement: {주인공} should appear in every panel with the same identity and outfit continuity, while facial expressions and gestures change panel by panel. Include one consistent coworker or lunch companion as the second main character across all six panels.
- Background treatment: show recognizable Korean office and lunch-break environment details, such as desks, monitor edges, sticky notes, office chairs, a water dispenser, elevator hallway signage, cafeteria tray, lunch menu board, delivery app screen, or restaurant counter, matched to the story beat in each panel.
- Spacing and framing: each panel uses medium shot to bust shot framing with occasional close-up reaction angles; speech bubbles should sit naturally within each panel while keeping faces, hand gestures, and key props visible.
- The comic should visually support {주제} and follow {6컷 흐름} in strict left-to-right, top-to-bottom reading order.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Panel 1 (top-left): introduce the lunch-topic conflict with both characters facing each other in a casual office break setting; include desk clutter like coffee cup, keyboard corner, lunch flyer, and a wall clock near noon. {주제} should be immediately understandable from the first speech bubble.
- Panel 2 (top-middle): one character gives a vague reply with a relaxed, slightly evasive expression; add a small Korean speech bubble, a tiny reaction mark, and background details such as an office pantry shelf or water dispenser for comedic timing.
- Panel 3 (top-right): the first suggestion lands clearly, with one character proposing a specific lunch option and the other beginning to look uncertain; show a phone screen or small menu poster with Korean food cues like '김치찌개', '제육', '냉면', or '돈가스'.
- Panel 4 (bottom-left): show visible hesitation and mild disappointment; use exaggerated but natural manhwa facial expression, a compact bubble, small sigh effect text like '하아…', and a slightly busier office hallway or elevator backdrop.
- Panel 5 (bottom-middle): the decision is pushed back to the other person; hand gesture or pointing gesture should reinforce the awkward escalation. Add a tiny background gag such as a coworker passing by with a lunch tray or a delivery bag.
- Panel 6 (bottom-right): the punchline lands with both characters ending up at the same place, matching {6컷 흐름}; show a recognizable final destination such as the same restaurant counter, convenience-store table, cafeteria line, or office pantry, with both characters looking resigned but funny. Include a small closing caption or tag like '결국 여기' if it matches the punchline.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: handwritten Korean comic speech bubbles with clean, legible line weight; use a manhwa-style hand-rendered feel rather than digital type, with medium-bold bubble text at roughly 18–24 px equivalent in a 1024×1024 canvas.

- Creator details: Add a small episode tag “{에피소드라벨}” near the upper corner of the comic area and a tiny series label “출근길 관찰일지” like a casual sticker.
- Subject focus: {캐릭터} drawn as the visual anchor in both panels, with the first panel emphasizing setup and the second panel emphasizing reaction.
- Background treatment: recognizable Korean urban café / commuting context with natural details such as a takeaway cup sleeve, phone screen, transit card, café menu board with small prices, window reflection, bag strap, table edge, subway handle, kiosk order number, receipt, or street sign as appropriate to {주제}.
- Text placement: {한글 캡션} should sit inside a speech bubble with comfortable padding, readable spacing, and a clear tail pointing to the speaker.
- Story seed: {주제} should be clearly communicated through body language, eye direction, props, and small environmental cues.
- Instagram caption area: Below the comic panels, include a short caption line “{게시글캡션}” and small hashtag-like text “{해시태그}”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Panel 1 (setup): Show {주제} as a relatable everyday moment, with {캐릭터} in a casual pose, clear surrounding context, and a speech bubble reserved for the first line.
- Panel 2 (punchline): Escalate the awkwardness through a subtle facial expression shift, slightly exaggerated pause, a tiny reaction symbol, and a compact visual beat that lands the joke.
- Dialogue rendering: Place {한글 캡션} in crisp, hand-rendered Korean text with even stroke weight, readable spacing, and clear separation from faces or important gestures.
- UI narrative details: Include tiny readable Korean fragments such as “아메리카노 2,500”, “주문번호 17”, “따뜻한 거 맞죠?”, “카드 승인”, or “출근 08:42” where they naturally fit the café/commute scene.
- Layout control: Keep {레이아웃} aligned like a polished Instagram webtoon post, with both panels sharing a consistent visual rhythm and the divider line straight.
- Extra comic details: Add tiny sound-effect or reaction text where useful, such as “{보조효과음}”, “정적”, “삐질”, or “어색…”, while keeping the punchline immediately understandable.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: hand-drawn Korean comic lettering, medium-weight, 18–24 px feel for speech bubbles, with clean rounded strokes and strong legibility.
- UI typography: tiny Instagram-style interface labels may use neat sans-serif lettering, smaller than the speech bubble text but still recognizable on a 1024x1024 image.
- Color palette: soft pastel flat colors with off-white #FAFAF7, warm gray #D9D6CF, muted sky blue #CFE3F2, pale peach #F6D7C8, cream yellow #F8E7A8, and charcoal linework #2F2F2F.
- Border/shadow: thin white panel divider, fine charcoal outlines, subtle soft shadow under characters and UI card elements, with gentle gradients only in small UI or background areas.
- Background objects: Use simple but specific everyday Korean details, drawn in the same pastel comic style, to make the setting feel lived-in and contemporary.
- Decorative social-feed touches: Add tiny sticker-like labels, a small saved-post bookmark icon, a heart count row, and a light doodle accent near the awkward pause.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat 2D comic composition, top-level editorial framing inspired by Instagram webtoon layouts rather than photographic perspective.
- Lighting: even diffuse daylight look, soft café-window brightness, slightly brighter faces for easy expression reading.
- Color grade: gentle pastel editorial grade with low contrast, warm-neutral whites, and restrained saturation.
- Rendering: polished digital webtoon illustration with clear linework, soft fills, small texture in paper/card areas, and readable mobile-screen composition.

[6. MOOD]
Korean Instagram webtoon comedy — everyday slice-of-life timing with the dry, compact rhythm of modern online gag comics, enriched with familiar social-feed details, tiny café/commute props, and small observational humor.
The mood should be warm, slightly embarrassed, and instantly relatable, like a post viewers would save or tag a coworker in.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: “...저... 안녕하세요...”
- Render {한글 캡션} accurately in Korean inside the speech bubble.
- Include readable Korean micro text: “{계정명}”, “{게시시간}”, “{위치라벨}”, “좋아요 {좋아요수}개”, “{게시글캡션}”, “{해시태그}”, “{에피소드라벨}”.
- Include small realistic detail text where legible: “아메리카노 2,500”, “주문번호 17”, “출근 08:42”.
- The comic must clearly read as a 2-panel daily-life gag with a setup-to-punchline structure.
- Character expressions must remain consistent and anatomically simple, with natural hand and face proportions.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites unless explicitly requested
