[1. PURPOSE]
Korean YouTube thumbnail for a relationship/psychology/self-reflection channel, designed like a premium editorial thumbnail inspired by a relationship essay cover and a high-retention video card.
Make it feel clickable, emotionally specific, and credible, with strong readability at small size, a clear psychological hook, and realistic YouTube thumbnail details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {메인 텍스트} occupies the center 45–50% of the frame, set as the dominant visual anchor with bold line breaks and strong contrast for mobile viewing.
- Subtitle: {부제} sits directly below the main text in a smaller, lighter weight, aligned left or centered depending on balance with the illustration.
- Illustration: {일러스트} placed on the right side third or lower-right corner, showing two side-profile people turned away from each other, with expressive posture and a subtle emotional distance.
- Background treatment: {배경} as a warm editorial paper-board surface with believable paper grain, soft vignette, faint desk-light shadowing, and gentle tonal variation.
- Accent use: {액센트 색} appears in clickable thumbnail elements such as a bold underline, speech-bubble tag, alert dot, arrow, sticker shape, or soft highlight block behind a short phrase.
- YouTube metadata details: add a small channel handle "@mind.note", a compact episode label "연애심리 EP.26", a tiny runtime-style badge "08:14", and a small sticker text such as "저장각" or "댓글 폭주" without weakening the title.
- Spacing and framing: composition is dense enough to feel like a real thumbnail, but the main title remains the largest and clearest element with safe crop space for YouTube UI.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Background layer: build a warm off-white to beige atmosphere using {배경}, with matte paper texture, faint gradient, soft corner shading, and a realistic editorial print surface.
2) Title block: place {메인 텍스트} in very large Korean serif typography, centered or slightly left of center and slightly above true middle, with bold contrast against the background.
3) Subtitle block: place {부제} beneath the title with smaller size, softer contrast, and a concise hook-like layout so it reads as the explanatory promise of the video.
4) Illustration layer: render {일러스트} as a clean line illustration with moderate detail, thin-to-medium strokes, and muted fill accents; position it on the right side so it creates a relationship tension visual.
5) Accent detail: apply {액센트 색} to 2–3 supporting thumbnail devices: a hand-drawn underline beneath a key phrase, a small arrow pointing toward the separated couple, and a rounded sticker tag reading "진짜 이유" or "심리 분석".
6) Thumbnail readability pass: keep the composition bold enough for 1/4 scale viewing, with the main message instantly legible on mobile and secondary details readable at full size.
7) Realistic YouTube card polish: include a small top-left series label "연애심리 EP.26", a tiny bottom-left credit "by 마음노트", a bottom-right runtime badge "08:14", and micro UI-style text like "구독자 질문" as subtle supporting context.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo for the main text, bold weight, large headline size; Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the subtitle and metadata labels, regular to medium weight.
- Color palette: cream #F4EFE6, warm beige #E7DCCB, dark brown-black #2B2019, muted gray #8C8680, and {액센트 색} as the dominant accent for sticker, underline, arrow, and small emphasis marks.
- Border/shadow: avoid heavy framing; use soft printed-card depth, subtle paper-edge shadow, 2px y-offset / 8px blur title shadow at 12% opacity if needed, and light sticker shadows for realistic layering.
- Graphic details: add small editorial symbols such as a tiny heart-break icon, speech bubble, circled number, torn-paper label, or marker highlight, all supporting the relationship psychology theme.
- Text hierarchy: {메인 텍스트} must be much larger than all added labels; metadata and stickers must feel secondary and not compete with the main message.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: clean graphic editorial layout, simulated as if shot on a medium-format 80mm lens perspective with flat front-facing composition, no distortion.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at 45°, diffused and even, with a faint warm fill from the lower-right to keep the paper-like background gentle.
- Color grade: warm cream, muted rose/teal, soft brown neutrals, slightly desaturated for a thoughtful psychology-editorial look.
- Rendering quality: realistic printed thumbnail artwork with tactile paper grain, subtle ink texture, layered sticker pieces, and crisp Korean typography.

[6. MOOD]
Thoughtful Korean relationship editorial meets a polished YouTube psychology thumbnail — calm, emotionally sharp, intimate, and highly clickable without looking sensationalist.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: "좋아하는데 왜 헤어지자고 했을까", "심리상담사가 말해준 진짜 이유"
- Additional Korean thumbnail details may include: "연애심리 EP.26", "@mind.note", "저장각", "댓글 폭주", "구독자 질문", "08:14".
- Keep the main title fully legible, with correct Korean spacing and no broken syllables or mangled characters.
- Illustration must remain simple and non-photorealistic, showing two people in side profile who are not facing each other.
- Layout must read clearly as a YouTube thumbnail at small size, with the title as the dominant element.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean YouTube thumbnail for an office worker daily vlog channel, horizontal thumbnail layout at 1536x1024, designed for high click-through on mobile feeds.
Keep the overall feel of a realistic Korean lifestyle vlog thumbnail with a gentle cinematic diary tone, enriched with believable vlog-channel metadata, small visual hooks, and warm after-work atmosphere.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: {사진} fills the entire background as the hero image, with the subject occupying roughly 55–65% of the frame, naturally framed near the veranda railing or window so the evening city view and title block both feel integrated.
- Background treatment: apartment veranda at sunset, soft peach sky, distant Korean apartment silhouettes, faint indoor reflections on glass, laundry rack or small plant shelf details, coffee steam or mug highlight, subtle depth blur, realistic lived-in evening texture.
- Text layout: main title block sits over a softly darkened readable area in the upper-left or center-left; subtitle placed directly beneath with tighter tracking; add a small channel handle and vlog label near the title cluster for authentic YouTube thumbnail context.
- Overlay: add a slightly dark translucent gradient overlay from bottom-right to center-left for readability, while preserving the peach sunset mood and visible veranda atmosphere.
- Accent elements: add a rounded sticker badge, tiny heart or star, small play-button triangle, and one soft arrow/circle cue pointing toward the mug or sunset moment, styled like a calm lifestyle vlog thumbnail.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Background hero layer: {사진} cleanly occupies the full canvas, with the subject shown from back or side view, holding a mug, framed to emphasize after-work quietness on an apartment veranda.
- Realistic detail layer: include believable daily-life elements such as a veranda plant, faint curtain edge, apartment rail, city windows beginning to glow, a phone or notebook on a small table, and warm reflections on the mug.
- Light control layer: add a subtle dusk-toned overlay to preserve the warm sky while making the foreground text pop clearly.
- Main headline layer: place {메인 텍스트} in large white handwritten-style typography, slightly angled or softly organic, with strong contrast against the overlay.
- Subtitle layer: set {부제} in smaller white text beneath the headline, aligned left or centered with the title block depending on the photo flow.
- Vlog metadata layer: add small readable Korean thumbnail details such as “VLOG #025”, “평일 저녁 7:42”, “퇴근 후 1시간”, and “@office.log” near the lower-left or upper-left text area.
- View-bait cue layer: add a compact sticker badge reading “오늘도 버텼다 ☕” or “리셋 루틴”, plus a small rounded shape or arrow that gives the thumbnail a clickable YouTube feel without turning it into a comic graphic.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a hand-drawn Korean script style for {메인 텍스트}, with a soft brush 느낌; use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for {부제} and metadata labels, medium weight, crisp readability, thumbnail-safe spacing.
- Color palette: peach sunset #F3B39A, dusty teal #7E9A9A, cream #F6EFE3, warm charcoal #2B2A28, white #FFFFFF, with small muted coral or butter-yellow accents for badges.

- Graphic treatment: use rounded pill labels, soft sticker-like shapes, tiny sparkle or heart accents, and a small play icon in a warm cream tone, all integrated into the cinematic photo rather than floating as a flat mockup.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm full-frame look, 50mm f/1.8 portrait-style framing, slightly compressed background with natural everyday realism.
- Lighting: soft golden-hour light from the sunset side, with gentle ambient fill from the veranda and a mild rim light around the subject.
- Color grade: warm cinematic peach + dusty teal + cream, with restrained film grain and slightly lifted shadows for a vlog-thumbnail look.
- Realism: photographic Korean apartment-evening mood, natural skin and fabric texture, real glass reflections, believable city-window bokeh, and subtle handheld vlog warmth.

[6. MOOD]
Korean everyday office-worker vlog thumbnail with a soft cinematic diary feel: calm but clickable, like a warm “퇴근 후 일상” YouTube cover with cozy apartment-evening visuals, gentle emotional storytelling, and realistic lifestyle details.

- Layout invariant: all text must be legible at thumbnail size, with no overlap that obscures the main subject's face or silhouette.

- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean gaming YouTube thumbnail for a reaction-style channel, horizontal 16:9 layout optimized for high click-through on mobile.
Fast, poppy, and instantly readable at small size, with a surprised streamer reaction over a lively game-like pixel world, plus realistic YouTube-thumbnail details such as a channel handle, episode badge, small view-bait captions, and bold graphic emphasis.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Background occupies the full frame as a bright blocky pixel game world, with {게임 화면} filling the scene: blue sky, chunky clouds, green grass, blocky trees, small creatures or items, glowing coins, floating platforms, and a dynamic in-game action moment.
- Right 30%: {캐릭터/유튜버 얼굴} cut out sharply and placed slightly off-center to the right, scaled large enough that the face dominates the thumbnail, with a clean white rim stroke, soft shadow, and a small comic-style burst behind the head.
- Left side 40–45%: {메인 텍스트} stacked in large Korean lettering, balanced vertically so it does not cover the main face; add a secondary mini-caption nearby such as "실화냐?!", "역대급 순간", or "바로 확인" in a small sticker strip.
- Small corner tag: {라벨} tucked into an upper corner as a compact badge, styled like an episode marker with tiny text such as "EP.24", "NEW", or "오늘의 게임" beside it.
- Add a small channel handle near the bottom edge, for example "@game_reaction" or "@오늘겜방", plus tiny YouTube-style micro details like "3분 전", "조회수 폭발", or a red play-button icon.
- One red circle or arrow emphasis element points toward the most surprising area in the background or near the face, without blocking the text; include an accent emoji or shape such as "😱", lightning bolt, question mark, or exclamation burst.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Full-bleed background: {게임 화면} rendered as a bright pixel landscape with blue sky, green grass, blocky trees, depth layers, floating blocks, spark particles, coins, hearts, score-like numbers, and a dramatic action focal point that looks like a captured gameplay moment.
2. Main reaction subject: {캐릭터/유튜버 얼굴} on the right side, cleanly cut out with a strong edge, white contour stroke, soft drop shadow, and slight warm rim light so the face pops forward from the background.
3. Main text block: {메인 텍스트} on the left in oversized Korean sans-serif, arranged for instant readability, with thick black outline, white fill, subtle yellow or cyan highlight strip, and a small red accent word bubble for urgency.
4. Label badge: {라벨} placed near a top corner in a small rounded rectangle or sticker-like badge, using compact typography so it reads as an episode marker; add tiny supporting text like "NEW" or "HOT" inside the badge area.
5. Attention marker: one vivid red circle or arrow placed near the focal point to amplify surprise and guide the viewer’s eye, with small comic burst lines and a nearby short caption such as "뭐야 이거!".
6. Thumbnail realism details: include a small channel handle, subtle bottom progress-bar accent, tiny play icon, view-bait microcopy, and layered stickers so the final image feels like a real gaming channel upload rather than a plain mockup.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for {메인 텍스트}, around 90–120 px equivalent; {라벨} in Pretendard SemiBold around 28–36 px equivalent; micro labels in bold Korean sans-serif around 18–28 px equivalent.
- Color palette: vibrant pop colors with cyan sky #7EC8FF, grass green #5FBF4A, white text #FFFFFF, stroke black #111111, attention red #FF3B30, highlight yellow #FFD84D, electric blue #00B7FF.
- Border/shadow: thick black text stroke 10–14 px equivalent; add a white outer glow or yellow shadow behind the main text for mobile readability; subject shadow as a soft drop shadow with 6 px y-offset, 18 px blur, 20% opacity.
- Graphic accents: comic burst shapes, lightning bolts, red arrow, red circle, small emoji-style reaction mark, tiny sparkle particles, and sticker labels should feel energetic and layered while keeping {메인 텍스트} and the face dominant.
- Composition should feel like a finished YouTube gaming thumbnail: high contrast, saturated, compressed for mobile readability, with all important elements readable within the central safe area.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 85mm f/1.4 portrait-style crop for the subject cutout, with a thumbnail-friendly close framing and slight perspective compression.
- Lighting: bright studio key light from upper-left at about 45°, small fill from front-right, crisp separation from the background, glossy catchlights in the eyes, and warm natural skin tones.
- Color grade: high-saturation gaming thumbnail grade with vivid blues and greens, slight contrast boost, clean whites, warm skin tones, punchy reds, and crisp sharpening on the face and title text.
- Rendering quality: realistic streamer face cutout blended with stylized pixel-game background, sharp edges, layered PNG-like thumbnail graphics, readable Korean lettering, and a polished creator-channel finish.

[6. MOOD]
High-energy Korean gaming reaction thumbnail — loud, exaggerated, funny, and click-worthy, with a surprised open-mouth reaction, playful panic, colorful chaos, and the feeling of a dramatic moment caught right before the viewer clicks.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "{메인 텍스트}", "{라벨}", plus short supporting Korean text such as "실화냐?!", "역대급 순간", "뭐야 이거!", "조회수 폭발", "오늘겜방".
- The face must clearly show a surprised, open-mouth reaction that reads as funny and excited rather than aggressive.
- Keep the layout horizontal and thumbnail-readable, with the main text on the left and the face on the right.
- Add realistic YouTube-thumbnail enrichments: small channel handle like "@오늘겜방", tiny red play icon, episode marker, short hype captions, arrow/circle emphasis, and an accent emoji or comic symbol.
- Maintain a bright blocky/pixel game aesthetic while making the scene feel full of gameplay action, items, effects, and depth.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Broken Korean characters
- Fake official seals or certifications
- Unauthorized celebrity likeness composites

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean YouTube thumbnail for an information-summary-educational channel, built for fast mobile readability and high click-through in a landscape layout.
Flat-vector editorial style with a lively real-channel thumbnail finish: bold Korean headline hierarchy, small channel branding cues, quick-summary labels, and curiosity-triggering visual hooks, similar in tone to 너진똑, 슈카, and 일주일에 책 한 권.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Full-frame background uses {배경 색} as the dominant field, with subtle printed-paper grain, faint halftone dots, and a few soft geometric blocks to make the thumbnail feel like a finished broadcast graphic.
- Left 35% of the canvas: {캐릭터/일러스트} placed as a cropped hero illustration, large enough to be instantly recognizable, with a small desk-note motif, simple chart card, or speech bubble nearby to reinforce the information-summary theme.
- Right 65%: oversized Korean headline block aligned for maximum legibility, with compact subtitle support beneath and a high-contrast title badge above it.
- Add real thumbnail packaging details: a small channel handle label, a bold “오늘의 요약” ribbon, one arrow or circle highlight, and a small emoji/accent shape that increases click appeal without covering the main text.
- Include 2–3 short supporting blurbs around the headline area, such as “핵심 3가지”, “숫자로 보는 이유”, and “팩트 체크”, set smaller than the main title but still crisp.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background layer — Fill the entire canvas with {배경 색}, then overlay faint grain/noise texture, subtle halftone circles, and a few translucent rectangular panels so the flat color feels like a polished Korean YouTube explainer thumbnail.
2. Left hero zone — Place {캐릭터/일러스트} in the left 35% area, cropped dynamically at the edge if needed, with simple flat-vector shading, a soft cast shadow, and small educational props such as a floating memo card, mini bar chart, or question bubble.
3. Right headline zone — Set {메인 텍스트} as the main visual anchor in the right 65%, using very large black sans-serif type with tight line breaks, thick weight, and occasional off-white highlight backing behind key words for instant mobile readability.
4. Subtitle zone — Position {부제} near the lower portion of the text block inside a rounded pill or rectangular tag, keeping it secondary but sharp and readable on mobile.
5. Thumbnail hook layer — Add a red play-button-inspired triangle, a thick arrow, or a circled highlight pointing toward the headline; add one punchy Korean sticker label such as “왜?” or “진짜 이유”.
6. Channel micro-branding — Add a small top or bottom corner handle label reading “@요약연구소”, a tiny episode tag “INFO #023”, and a compact series label “3분 지식” to make the design feel like an authentic uploaded thumbnail.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the main headline, with subtitle in Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Medium; headline size should feel thumbnail-scale dominant, subtitle about 35–45% of headline size.
- Color palette: {배경 색} as the main field, black #111111 for primary text, optional off-white #FFF8E7 for text backing, red #FF3B30 or deep blue #1D4ED8 for arrow/play accents, and muted gray #4B5563 for small metadata.
- Use thick graphic outlines, sticker-like label boxes, and crisp vector shadows around the character and headline so the image reads clearly in a crowded YouTube feed.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean YouTube thumbnail for a real-estate / economy / investing channel, horizontal 16:9 layout.
Designed for high readability at small preview size, with a realistic Korean financial-news commentary look: presenter cutout, dramatic headline, market-data overlays, channel branding, and urgent analysis cues.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Left 35%: {피사체} placed as the main human anchor, cut out cleanly and scaled to occupy most of the left side from bottom-left to mid-height.
- Right 65%: large headline text and supporting graphics arranged as a bold editorial thumbnail block with strong hierarchy, fast scanning, and punchy visual emphasis.
- Background: {배경} as a full-frame economic-news base, enriched with faint apartment silhouettes, stock-index grid texture, subtle map/market dashboard panels, and soft gray depth layers behind the text area for contrast.
- Framing direction: subject facing slightly toward the text block to guide attention from left to right, as if urgently explaining a turning point in the housing market.
- Add YouTube-native details: a small channel handle, short urgency tag, accent emoji or warning shape, and compact market chart elements that make the thumbnail feel like a real upload from a Korean real-estate channel.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero subject area (left 35%): {피사체} shown from waist-up, serious expression, one hand gesturing as if explaining a market point, with crisp cutout edges and a soft drop shadow separating the subject from the background.
- Headline block (right 65%, upper-middle): {메인 텍스트} set in very large bold black Korean sans-serif, stacked for quick scanning, with the most important phrase visually dominant.
- Emphasis treatment: {강조 키워드} highlighted in red or fluorescent marker-style accent, integrated directly into the headline so it pops instantly in the thumbnail grid; add a red underline slash or marker box behind the keyword.
- Data label (right side, lower or near headline): {데이터 라벨} placed as a small gray or charcoal pill-shaped label, clearly readable, paired with tiny supporting text such as "서울 아파트", "거래량", "전세가".
- Supporting graphics: add a compact red downward arrow, a small line chart dipping sharply, two or three bar-chart columns, and a tiny callout bubble reading "하락 신호?" near the lower-right corner.
- Channel identity: include a small handle near the top-left or lower-left, such as "@부동산브리핑", plus a small label "긴급분석" or "오늘의 부동산" in a red tag.
- View-bait accent: include one strong warning shape or emoji-like symbol such as "⚠" inside a red rounded square, positioned near the headline without covering text.
- Background finish: polished presentation-slide/newsroom composite with layered finance-dashboard textures, apartment-photo fragments, faint grid lines, and clean separation between subject, headline, and data graphic.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR bold for the main headline, weight 800–900, with size tuned for thumbnail readability; use smaller 500–600 weight for the data label, handle, and urgency tag.
- Color palette: off-white and light gray base (#F2F2F2 / #E7E7E7), black text (#111111), emphasis red (#E53935 or #FF3B30), muted gray labels (#7A7A7A), charcoal accents (#303030), and small yellow warning highlights (#FFD54F) if needed.
- Border/shadow: subject cutout with soft drop shadow, 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; headline may use a subtle white keyline or soft shadow only to improve legibility against graphics.
- Graphic style: PPT-style Korean finance infographic accents with crisp chart lines, red arrows, pill labels, small dashboard cards, and sharp geometric shapes.
- Preserve exact Korean spelling in all visible text elements.
- Keep the thumbnail dense enough to feel like a real YouTube economy upload while maintaining immediate headline readability.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with 85mm portrait lens, f/2.0, shallow depth of field for the subject cutout, with studio-composite clarity rather than a natural background scene.
- Lighting: soft studio key light from upper-left at about 45°, subtle fill from right, balanced to keep the face readable and the headline area bright.
- Color grade: neutral gray base with black, red, muted charcoal, and small yellow warning accents; slight editorial contrast, no warm filter.
- Composite realism: realistic presenter lighting, natural skin texture, clean hair detail, crisp jacket folds, and believable shadow contact at the bottom edge.

[6. MOOD]

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "강남 집값 진짜 떨어집니다", "진짜", "2026년 1분기 분석" must appear exactly as written.
- The layout must clearly read as a Korean real-estate/economy YouTube thumbnail.
- The subject must look like a Korean man in his 40s, wearing a shirt plus casual jacket, serious and explanatory.
- Headline must remain highly legible at small thumbnail size.
- Include small Korean supporting text elements such as "@부동산브리핑", "긴급분석", "하락 신호?", and "오늘의 부동산" where they fit naturally.

- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
6-cut emoticon sheet for Korean community chat use, arranged as a 2x3 grid with bold readable captions.
Create a rough, friendly DCInside-style sticker pack preview sheet that shows one character in six distinct reactions, enriched with small creator metadata, panel numbers, and playful community-sticker packaging details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {캐릭터} repeated consistently across all 6 panels, with the same body shape, line thickness, and proportions.
- Layout: {레이아웃}; strict 2x3 grid with evenly sized cells, hand-cut white dividers, and a small sticker-sheet header/footer area worked into the square composition.
- Sheet identity elements: add a compact top label reading "{시트 제목}", a tiny pack code "{팩 코드}", creator handle "{제작자 핸들}", and date label "{업로드 날짜}" as if this is a saved community sticker-pack preview.
- Each panel should contain one expression, one matching pose, one Korean caption or speech bubble, a small panel number marker 01–06, and a few accent doodles such as sweat drops, angry veins, sparkle marks, motion lines, check marks, or tiny reaction tags.
- Background treatment: warm off-white digital paper with scanned grain, faint ink speckles, sticker-cut edges, light correction-tape marks, and subtle uneven printing texture while keeping all captions readable.
- Composition should feel like a real uploaded emoticon reference sheet: playful, dense enough to feel designed, but still clearly organized for thumbnail viewing.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Panel 1 (top-left): show {6컷 표정}의 첫 번째 감정에 맞는 얼굴 and pair it with the first phrase from {6컷 멘트}; add a tiny "01" corner label and a small red X or refusal doodle.
- Panel 2 (top-center): show the second expression with a slightly more exaggerated mouth and eyebrow shape, and place the second phrase as bold Korean text near the character’s head; add a sarcastic lightning or zigzag accent.
- Panel 3 (top-right): show the third expression as the most energetic panel, with the character opening wider, laughing or reacting strongly, and keep the caption tightly integrated; add bouncing motion marks and small laughter symbols around the character.
- Panel 4 (bottom-left): show the fourth expression with a sharp change in eyes and mouth, making the emotion immediately distinguishable from the previous three panels; include surprise rays, sweat drops, or a popped speech bubble.
- Panel 5 (bottom-center): show the fifth expression with a waiting/checking pose, such as a small hand gesture, phone-checking stance, or pause stance, and place the text in a speech-bubble style if needed; add a tiny clock/check icon.
- Panel 6 (bottom-right): show the sixth expression as a downbeat or exhausted ending pose, with heavier posture and simplified silhouette for a strong final beat; add drooping motion lines, a small dark cloud, or a crumpled sticker-tag feel.
- Across all panels, preserve the same character design and only vary facial expression, small arm pose, caption placement, and reaction doodles.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: {텍스트 폰트}; large sticker-readable Korean captions, slight outlined lettering, chunky spacing, and hand-adjusted baseline for internet-meme energy.
- Palette: {컬러 팔레트}; use the accent color consistently for cheeks, bubbles, emphasis marks, panel-number stickers, header tags, and small reaction doodles.
- Linework: thick black outer contour with rough hand-drawn edges, uneven ink feel, slight wobble, and simple internal details.
- Dividers and borders: thin white separators between cells with subtle sketchy paper-cut edges; add tiny tape tabs, corner registration marks, or sticker peel shadows where useful.
- Text treatment: strong black or accent-colored Korean captions with clean spacing, no warped distortion, no broken syllables, and every caption placed so it remains legible at 1024x1024.
- Metadata styling: header/footer microtext should feel like a real community sticker sheet: "{시트 제목}", "{제작자 핸들}", "{팩 코드}", "{업로드 날짜}", plus small tags like "디시콘", "6컷", "저장용".

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat graphic illustration, top-down editorial sheet composition inspired by sticker pack layouts rather than photographic perspective.
- Lighting: even diffuse studio-like illumination with no directional shadows, keeping the character, captions, dividers, and metadata fully readable on the textured off-white base.
- Color grade: high-contrast black-and-white base with a single accent color, lightly desaturated and slightly lo-fi like a scanned printed internet meme sheet.

[6. MOOD]
Rough, playful Korean internet emoticon-sheet energy — classic DCInside community sticker pack vibe with a handmade lo-fi zine feel, expressive captions, cheeky micro-labels, and lively doodle reactions.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 한글 문자열이 정확히 보여야 함: "ㄴㄴ 안됨", "어쩔티비", "ㅋㅋㅋㄹㅇ", "헐 진심?", "기다려봐", "끝났네".
- Metadata text accuracy: "{시트 제목}", "{제작자 핸들}", "{팩 코드}", "{업로드 날짜}"가 작은 라벨로 보여야 하며, 깨지거나 영어로 대체되지 않아야 함.
- Same character consistency: all 6 panels must clearly be the same {캐릭터}, with no redesign between panels.
- 2x3 grid consistency: all 6 cells must be present, evenly aligned, visually separated, and numbered 01–06.
- Text must be fully legible, with no broken Korean characters, no garbled jamo, and no missing punctuation.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or garbled jamo
- Celebrity composites or real-person likeness mashups
- Photorealistic rendering that replaces the flat sticker illustration

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean YouTube thumbnail for a movie/drama review channel, cinematic 16:9 wide layout with strong click-through readability.
Create a rich, realistic film-review editorial thumbnail similar to Cineclub / film-enthusiast commentary channels: one dramatic central character, bold Korean headline, review-channel graphic overlays, small handle text, and persuasive view-bait details that feel native to YouTube.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: {인물} occupies the central-right 45% of the frame, with face and upper torso clearly readable at thumbnail size; the left side becomes a strong headline panel integrated into the cinematic scene rather than an empty area.
- Background treatment: {배경 / 영화 무드} rendered as a dark, layered cinematic backdrop with wet street reflections, blurred neon signage, faint film-grain texture, smoky depth, and subtle poster-like fragments that support the review theme.
- Spacing and framing: separate the character from the headline with a soft rim glow, smoky vignette, and shallow-depth blur; the composition should feel like a paused frame from a dramatic Korean movie review video.
- Add a small red circle accent near the key focal point, plus one red arrow or alert-style shape pointing toward the emotional detail being analyzed.
- Place {레이블} in a compact corner tag with a premium review-series feel, visually secondary to the main headline.
- Add small YouTube-native details: a channel handle, a spoiler-warning tag, a short sub-blurb, a tiny play icon, and a view-bait rating chip, all arranged around the headline without covering the face.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background layer — Build a moody urban-night or film-scene atmosphere from {배경 / 영화 무드}, with dark navy and charcoal dominance, wet asphalt reflections, distant amber practical lights, faint bokeh, subtle film-strip edges, and enough tonal contrast to support bold text.
2. Character layer — Place {인물} as a Korean drama-style figure in profile or near-profile, looking into the distance, with a clear shoulder line, readable facial contour, expressive eyes, realistic skin texture, cinematic hair detail, and a faint blue rim light along the outline.
3. Main headline layer — Set {메인 텍스트} in large white bold Korean typography, slightly shadowed for separation, aligned to the left-side text block and sized for mobile readability; emphasize one key word with a red underline or red boxed emphasis.
4. Label layer — Render {레이블} as a compact top-left or top-right corner label, smaller than the headline, with a dark translucent pill background and restrained informational feel.
5. Accent layer — Add one small red circle mark to highlight the chosen point of interest, supported by a subtle red arrow, alert dot, or small magnifier cue.
6. Channel layer — Add a tiny channel handle and micro metadata near the lower-left area, such as @씬리뷰노트, 평점 9.1, and 오늘 밤 공개, using small but crisp Korean text.
7. Engagement layer — Add thumbnail-native graphic elements such as a small play-button triangle, a short yellow or red sticker tag, a reaction emoji-style shape, and a compact caption chip reading 스포주의 or 숨은 복선 3개.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: main headline uses Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Serif KR Bold, approx. 72–96 px equivalent for a 1536x1024 canvas; label uses Pretendard SemiBold, approx. 28–36 px; micro tags use Pretendard Bold around 24–30 px with high contrast.
- Color palette: near-black #111318, deep navy #1B2230, muted gray-blue #5E6A7A, headline white #F5F5F2, accent red #D62828, selective amber highlight #D59A3A for small rating or warning chips.
- Border/shadow: headline gets a subtle soft shadow with 0px x-offset, 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 25% opacity; character edges may have a faint cinematic rim light, not a hard outline.
- Graphic overlays should look like real YouTube thumbnail design assets: red annotation circle, arrow, sticker tag, rating chip, and tiny play icon with slight shadow and believable compositing.
- Keep the overall look premium and cinematic, not cartoonish; overlays should enhance urgency while preserving the film-review editorial atmosphere.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: cinematic still look, 85mm lens at f/2.0, shallow depth of field with clean subject separation and compressed perspective.
- Lighting: soft diffused key light from upper-left at 45°, faint practical streetlight glow from the background, gentle rim light from the right to lift the silhouette.
- Color grade: cold urban noir grade with deep blues, graphite blacks, and restrained warm amber highlights in reflections.
- Texture: subtle realistic film grain, glossy wet pavement highlights, soft atmospheric haze, and faint compression-like edge sharpness typical of high-quality YouTube thumbnails.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean film-review thumbnail — polished, dramatic, and clickable, like a late-night K-drama analysis video freeze-frame with editorial annotations, spoiler-warning energy, and a serious Cineclub / indie cinema commentary tone.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: must appear exactly as written:
  - 이 장면이 명장면인 진짜 이유
  - 2026 추천작 #07
  - @씬리뷰노트
  - 결말 해석
  - 숨은 복선 3개
  - 평점 9.1
  - 스포주의
  - 오늘 밤 공개
- Layout invariant: the character must remain clearly visible and not cover the headline area; the main text must stay legible at thumbnail size.
- {메인 텍스트} is the dominant headline text; {레이블} is the compact series label.
- The red circle accent must point to a meaningful cinematic detail on or near {인물}, while the arrow and sticker tags support the review angle without overwhelming the face.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters

- Left 30%: {피사체} placed as a cropped hero cutout, slightly enlarged so the face and upper torso are immediately recognizable, with a confident expression and natural portrait realism.
- Right 70%: headline area with {메인 텍스트} as the dominant reading element, supported by one highlight treatment on {강조 단어}, short supporting captions, and compact accent graphics that guide the eye.
- Background: {배경} with warm off-white paper texture, faint desk-note / productivity-board details, soft geometric panels, subtle graph-line motifs, and light gray editorial texture that feels like a real creator thumbnail set.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero area (left 30%): {피사체} cut out cleanly with natural edge refinement, placed against the textured background with a soft realistic drop shadow and subtle rim separation so the subject feels integrated but still pops.
- Text block (right 70%, upper-middle): {메인 텍스트} set in large bold Korean sans-serif, stacked for fast reading, with strong line separation, crisp black lettering, and slight white keyline or soft shadow for mobile readability.

- YouTube-native details: include a small channel handle label such as "@growth_lab", a compact category tag like "자기계발 · 돈관리", and a small pill badge reading "오늘부터 시작" near the headline.
- View-bait accents: add a small red arrow, yellow circular callout, or expressive emoji such as "🔥" or "💡" near the highlighted word, scaled to support the headline without blocking it.
- Supporting micro copy: add one short Korean caption below the headline, such as "실천하면 바로 달라집니다", and a tiny lower-right metadata strip like "조회수 128만 · 10분 핵심요약".
- Background handling: {배경} should include tactile paper grain, soft tonal transitions, faint productivity icons, light sticky-note shapes, and subtle chart/arrow motifs related to saving money and self-improvement.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the main headline, roughly 88–120px visual scale, with compact tracking, crisp edges, and strong mobile-thumbnail readability.
- Secondary typography: use Pretendard SemiBold / Noto Sans KR Bold for channel handle, category tag, and metadata labels at smaller scale, with clean rectangular or rounded-pill label treatments.
- Color palette: black #111111 for main text, yellow #FFE95A for highlight bar, off-white #F4F0E6 and light gray #E8E8E8 for the background family, with optional muted accent gray #7A7A7A and small red accent #FF3B30 for arrows or urgency marks.
- Border/shadow: soft drop shadow on the subject only, about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; use very subtle text shadow or white keyline only where needed for legibility, avoiding heavy glow or 3D bevels.
- Layout feel: polished Korean education / finance / IT YouTube thumbnail with PPT-like clarity, strong hierarchy, realistic creator presence, and small believable platform details.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with an 85mm portrait lens look at f/2.8 for the subject cutout, with clean studio-cropped thumbnail aesthetic and realistic facial detail.
- Lighting: soft studio key light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from the front-right, subtle rim separation to keep the subject distinct from the light background.
- Color grade: neutral bright tones with slightly warm off-white paper base, controlled blacks, restrained yellow emphasis, and natural skin tones for a trustworthy information-creator look.
- Texture realism: incorporate fine paper grain, slight marker opacity variation, soft sticker edges, and subtle compression-friendly contrast so the image feels like a real uploaded YouTube thumbnail.

[6. MOOD]
Practical Korean creator thumbnail aesthetic — clean self-improvement YouTube design with the organized clarity of a modern PPT slide, the direct punch of high-performing finance/IT channel thumbnails, and a realistic creator-led atmosphere that feels helpful, urgent, and clickable.

- Subject should look natural and confidently expressive, with no distorted face or incorrect anatomy.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {장소} as the clear focal point, with the strongest visual interest placed across the middle and lower thirds.
- Frame structure: {구도} with a polished vertical cover layout that allows the landmark, coastline, mountain, street, or vista to remain instantly readable.
- Background treatment: distant horizon, atmospheric depth, and natural texture in water, sand, rock, trees, street surfaces, rooftops, or sky depending on {장소}.
- Time and atmosphere: {시간대} to define the color of the sky, reflections, shadow length, and realistic local weather texture.
- Mood layer: {무드} carried through spacing, contrast, horizon placement, human scale, and the rhythm of natural details.
- Regional context: {지역} should be readable as the visual identity of the scene through architecture, coastline, terrain, vegetation, local walking paths, seasonal details, or small authentic travel cues.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero landscape area: {장소} occupies most of the frame with a premium scenic read; keep the primary landmark, shoreline, vista, street, or natural formation sharply legible.

- Magazine details: include a small vertical spine/credit text near one edge, a discreet barcode box in the lower corner, tiny price text “₩7,500”, and photo credit “사진 김하늘”.
- Secondary detail zone: include a small human presence, backpack, camera strap, bicycle, ferry rail, café chair, trail marker, or travel object only if it fits naturally into {구도}, scaled modestly so the landscape remains dominant.
- Sky and light zone: {시간대} creates a layered sky gradient, soft edge highlights, and subtle reflective color on sea, river, terrain, glass, stone, or sand.
- Spatial depth: foreground texture, midground focal area, and distant background should be clearly separated to create a premium editorial travel-photo feel.
- Emotional tone: {무드} should come from the scale of the view, the lived-in travel details, natural weather, and gentle sunset color transition.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Korean magazine-cover typography should feel professionally typeset and printed on top of the photograph; use crisp Hangul, high contrast, elegant hierarchy, and realistic editorial alignment.
- Korean text to render in image: “한국의 길”, “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “나다운 여행이 시작되는 곳”, “{지역} 하루 코스”, “바람이 머무는 전망대”, “해질녘 산책 지도”, “사진 김하늘”, “₩7,500”.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean literary book cover design, vertical paperback dust-jacket style, poetic contemporary indie publishing look with realistic printed-book details.
Designed to feel like a contemporary essay or poetry collection cover suitable for online bookstore thumbnail, editorial catalog listing, and a believable print-ready cover mockup.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical composition with the main title occupying the upper 42% of the cover, the visual concept spanning the middle zone, and author/publisher area across the lower 16%.
- Background treatment: off-white paper base with visible fine fiber texture, faint grain, slight ink absorption, soft scuffs, and a delicate atmospheric wash that supports the visual concept while keeping typography clear.
- Build a refined central publishing layout with realistic book-cover micro details: small series number, edition/date label, price line, ISBN/barcode block, and tiny imprint text placed naturally near the lower edge or back-cover suggestion area.
- Add subtle physical print cues such as a thin dust-jacket fold line near one vertical edge, very light paper waviness, a barely raised ink impression on the title, and a soft studio shadow that makes the cover feel like an actual photographed book surface.
- Use {책 제목}, {영문 부제}, {저자}, {장르}, {시각 컨셉} as editable text/content anchors while preserving the overall refined publishing-house layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top title zone (upper 28%): place {책 제목} in large Korean serif typography, crisp and centered, with strong vertical presence and carefully balanced line spacing; give the title a subtle printed ink texture rather than perfectly flat digital edges.
- Small editorial metadata above or beside the title: add tiny Korean/English text such as “BOOK NO. 014”, “초판 1쇄”, “2026년 봄”, or “LITERARY ESSAY SERIES” in fine type, aligned with the title column.
- Subtitle zone (below title, 6–8% down): set {영문 부제} in smaller clean sans-serif, tracking slightly expanded, aligned to the title axis, with clear hierarchy separation and a quiet editorial rhythm.
- Mid visual zone (center 38–45%): interpret {시각 컨셉} as an atmospheric illustration or gradient field, e.g. misty mountain silhouette, pale dawn haze, window light across a desk, soft layered forms, handwritten paper fragments, or a distant shoreline with gentle depth, integrated into the paper surface with visible print grain.
- Add 1–2 tactile literary details inside the mid/lower visual field when appropriate: a faint pencil line, tiny page-number-like mark, translucent leaf shadow, folded note edge, or pale archival texture that supports the book’s mood without competing with the title.
- Genre cue zone (lower middle 8–10%): place {장르} as a small editorial descriptor, understated and secondary, using thin-weight type and wide letter spacing; include a short Korean category line such as “한국문학 · 에세이” or “시와 산문” if it fits the genre.
- Bottom author zone (lower 10%): position {저자} near the bottom margin, aligned to the main column and visually lighter than the title; add a tiny author-credit line such as “written by” or “지은이” nearby if appropriate.
- Publisher/imprint area: place a small fictional imprint text mark at the bottom corner, plus tiny production details such as “정가 ₩16,800”, “ISBN 979-11-0000-014-7”, and a compact barcode area rendered as cover-print information, not as a certification seal.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Korean title in Pretendard Serif or Noto Serif KR Bold, 64–86px equivalent; English subtitle in Inter or Noto Sans KR Medium, 22–30px equivalent; author, genre, metadata, price, and ISBN lines in smaller regular/medium weights.
- Color palette: off-white #F5F1E8, warm gray #CFC8BE, mist blue #BFC8D2, charcoal #2C2C2C, optional accent in muted sage #A8B6A3 or dusty blue #91A7B8.
- Border/shadow: no heavy border; use a subtle physical book-edge shadow, fine fold-line shading, and very soft ink shadow under text only if needed, around 2px y-offset, 8px blur, 10% opacity.
- Keep the design editorial, tactile, and print-realistic; allow carefully placed microtype, barcode/ISBN information, paper marks, dust-jacket fold cues, and atmospheric illustration details that make the cover feel like a real Korean paperback.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat printed-cover mockup look, equivalent to a high-resolution studio reproduction with a 50mm normal perspective, no wide-angle distortion.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left, gentle ambient fill, slight paper sheen on raised ink, and enough texture visibility to reveal the matte stock and printed grain.
- Color grade: muted cream + mist blue + cool gray with a quiet dawn atmosphere, low saturation, slight analog print softness.
- Material finish: matte uncoated paper, subtle fiber texture, faint ink spread around Korean characters, soft scuffed edges, and a believable dust-jacket surface.

[6. MOOD]
Contemporary Korean indie publisher cover — Minumsa / Munhakdongne editorial poetry aesthetic, like a refined literary magazine spread with quiet dawn atmosphere, tactile bookstore realism, and a thoughtful handmade literary object quality.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문자열이 정확히 보여야 함: “조용한 새벽의 일기”, “김서연 지음”
- Also render realistic Korean cover microcopy clearly where suitable: “초판 1쇄”, “2026년 봄”, “정가 ₩16,800”, “ISBN 979-11-0000-014-7”, “한국문학 · 에세이”.
- Preserve exact layout hierarchy: large Korean title, smaller English subtitle, author name near bottom, genre descriptor, and publisher/imprint information at bottom corner.
- All Korean characters must render cleanly with no garbling, broken spacing, or mixed-up glyphs.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals or certification marks
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-013.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean corporate profile portrait for LinkedIn, company profile, portfolio, and executive bio card use. Photo-realistic vertical business portrait with magazine-quality polish, approachable professionalism, and a subtle profile-card editorial layout.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {피사체 묘사} placed as a centered upper-body hero, occupying about 65% of the frame height, with a confident but natural presence.
- Framing: {구도}; chest-up composition, slight 3/4 angle while maintaining direct eye contact, shoulders relaxed and squared enough to read as trustworthy and competent.
- Background: {배경} with believable corporate context such as softly blurred glass partitions, muted office shelves, a small plant shape, or warm practical light bokeh, while keeping the face clearly dominant.
- Lighting setup: {조명} with clean facial modeling, natural skin texture, catchlights in both eyes, and a gentle jaw shadow.
- Profile-card layer: add a refined lower-third business profile panel at the bottom 18–22% of the vertical frame, semi-transparent off-white or charcoal-accented, aligned neatly with the portrait.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Subject rendering: {피사체 묘사} shown as a polished Korean business portrait, hair neatly groomed, clothing crisp, expression calm and confident, with realistic pores, subtle eye detail, and visible fabric weave in the blazer or shirt.
- Head and shoulders zone: keep the face as the focal point, with the eyes near the upper third line, and the blazer and shirt visible enough to clearly signal business-professional context.
- Background treatment: {배경} softly defocused or smoothly graded, using realistic depth separation and gentle tonal layering rather than an empty studio void.
- Light shaping: {조명} should create a soft key on the face, a gentle shadow under the jaw, and a faint rim or fill that gives dimensionality while preserving a natural corporate look.
- Profile information design: include name, role, company, date/location label, short caption, and small decorative tags as if used on a Korean company website profile card.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: clean Korean editorial typography, crisp and legible, using a modern sans-serif style; hierarchy should make {이름} largest, {직함} and {회사명} secondary, and metadata smaller.
- Color palette: warm neutral skin tones, steel gray, soft charcoal, off-white highlights, muted navy accent, with background tones aligned to {배경}.
- Graphic treatment: subtle rounded lower-third panel, thin divider line, small dot accents, understated tag chips, and a tiny date/location label that feels like a premium corporate profile template.
- Realism: maintain realistic lens perspective, natural facial asymmetry, believable office light reflections, and professional grooming without glamour retouching.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 or Sony A7R IV look, 85mm f/1.8 portrait lens, shallow-to-moderate depth of field, clean facial perspective with minimal distortion.
- Lighting: soft front natural light with a weak key light, approximately 45° fill balance, diffused and even, similar to a high-end corporate studio setup with real office ambience.
- Color grade: warm-but-neutral editorial portrait grade, restrained contrast, natural skin retention, muted gray background separation, no heavy saturation.

[6. MOOD]
Modern Korean corporate portrait — polished LinkedIn headshot combined with a restrained executive profile card, like a Fortune magazine business portrait adapted for a Korean startup or consulting firm website.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean rendered text must be exact and readable on the lower-third profile panel:
  이름: "{이름}"
  직함/회사: "{직함} · {회사명}"
  촬영 라벨: "{촬영일} · {위치}"
  소개 문구: "{한줄소개}"
  태그: "{태그}"
- Anatomy/layout invariants: face must be natural, eyes sharp and aligned, hands not visible, posture professional, no exaggerated fashion pose.
- Text placement: keep all Korean text inside the lower-third panel or small tag area; do not let text cover the eyes, mouth, or key facial features.
- Maintain a realistic business-photo look: skin should retain pores and natural texture, with polished but believable retouching.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or garbled Hangul
- Celebrity composites or public-figure likeness
- Fake government-style ID marks or official document stamps

args.name: 조명
args.default: 부드러운 정면 자연광과 약한 키 라이트, 잔잔한 턱 그림자와 선명한 눈빛 반사

studio:prompts3:ours-012.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Editorial-style Korean Instagram portrait retouch reference, vertical photo for social media feed.
Late-afternoon café scene with cinematic Lightroom color grading, realistic lifestyle details, and subtle painterly enhancement that feels like an actual Korean café snapshot prepared for an Instagram post.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {장면} placed slightly off-center using rule-of-thirds, with the face and upper torso occupying about 55–60% of the frame.
- Background: softly blurred café interior with warm beige walls, muted wood furniture, linen curtains, small plants, ceramic cups, a menu board, and gentle window highlights that add lived-in realism without overpowering the portrait.
- Framing: vertical composition with intimate crop, natural café surroundings visible around the subject, and a feed-ready editorial balance.
- Apply {보정 스타일} as the dominant tonal direction, while preserving natural skin detail, pores, hair texture, makeup softness, and realistic fabric weave.
- Add {질감} subtly across the full frame so it reads like polished 35mm film, not heavy analog noise.
- Include a tasteful Instagram-card layer as part of the final image: small handle text, date/location label, caption line, hashtag-like text, and tiny save/share micro icons placed near the lower edge with translucent cream backing.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Subject area: keep the woman’s profile crisp, with eye line directed toward the light source; hair strands should catch the backlight softly without looking over-sharpened.
- Midground: render the café table edge, open book pages, iced latte glass, folded receipt, small dessert plate, phone, tote strap, and nearby props in gentle focus falloff so they support the scene and make the image feel candid.
- Background wash: push distant chairs, windows, counter shelves, hanging pendant lights, menu chalkboard, and wall tones into a soft creamy blur with teal-muted shadows and pale peach highlights.
- Social feed details: add tiny Korean text elements such as “@sumin.light”, “성수동 카페 · 2026.05.01”, “오늘의 빛은 조금 더 부드럽게”, and “#라이트룸보정 #카페스냅 #웜톤” in clean Pretendard-style typography, positioned like a refined Instagram editorial card.
- Retouch pass: lift shadow detail slightly, compress highlights on skin and window edges, and keep overall contrast low-to-medium for an elegant Instagram edit.
- Finish pass: apply a faint glow around the brightest areas, preserving realism and avoiding a hazy overexposed look.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: render small Korean interface-style caption text in Pretendard Regular and Pretendard SemiBold, with clear readable Korean characters; keep text secondary to the portrait.
- Color palette: warm sandstone #C8A57A, cream beige #F4EBDD, faded teal #8FA9A3, peach skin warmth #E8B79B, soft espresso brown #5B4636.
- Border/shadow: no hard frame; use very soft natural contact shadows where objects overlap, around 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity.
- Decorative details: add subtle translucent caption chips, tiny heart/comment/share/save icons, a small timestamp dot, and café lifestyle accents that match the warm editorial palette.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Sony A7 IV with 85mm f/1.4 portrait lens at f/2.0, shallow depth of field, natural background compression.
- Lighting: late-afternoon window light from camera-left at about 45°, with a gentle bounce fill from camera-right; highlights should be warm and directional.
- Color grade: warm sandstone tones, lifted shadows, slightly soft highlights, faded teal in background, peach-toned skin warmth, medium-low saturation.
- Retouch character: Lightroom-style Korean Instagram edit with smooth tonal transitions, realistic skin, mild grain, softened greens, creamy highlights, and warm café ambience.

[6. MOOD]
Editorial Korean Instagram portrait — a refined magazine-spread look similar to a soft Kinfolk-meets-Aesop aesthetic, with intimate café realism, lived-in table details, polished Lightroom grading, and quiet social-media storytelling.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: any rendered Korean text must be legible and correctly formed, especially “성수동 카페 · 2026.05.01”, “오늘의 빛은 조금 더 부드럽게”, “#라이트룸보정 #카페스냅 #웜톤”.
- Maintain a believable human pose and anatomy; hands, if visible, must be anatomically correct with exactly 5 fingers per hand.
- Preserve the side-profile reading moment and the gentle hair motion implied by the late-afternoon breeze.
- Keep all Instagram-style text and icons subtle, tasteful, and integrated into the editorial portrait rather than becoming the main subject.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals/certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-011.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
한국 먹스타그램 음식 클로즈업 사진. 인스타그램에 바로 올릴 수 있는 4:5 세로형 푸드 포스트로, {음식}과 곁들임 반찬의 식감, 뜨거운 김, 국물의 윤기, 실제 식탁 위 생활감이 살아있는 photorealistic editorial shot. 하단에는 실제 모바일 피드처럼 보이는 인스타그램 카드 UI를 더해 {계정명}, {위치라벨}, {짧은캡션}, {해시태그}, {게시일자}가 자연스럽게 읽히도록 만든다.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- {음식}이 프레임의 약 70%를 차지하도록 배치하고, 메인 볼은 화면 중앙에서 약간 아래에 두어 김과 면, 계란 노른자, 파 고명, 고춧가루 입자, 국물 위 기름 방울이 한눈에 보이게 한다.
- {배경}은 원목 결이 보이는 따뜻한 브라운 톤 표면으로 처리하고, 젓가락 받침, 보리차 컵, 작은 반찬 접시, 접힌 냅킨, 국물 한두 방울, 반찬 양념 자국이 가장자리에서 자연스럽게 보이도록 배치한다.
- {구도}는 45도 하이앵글로 유지하되, 좌우를 풍성하게 채워 한국 집밥 테이블에서 막 찍은 먹스타그램 특유의 현실적인 밀도를 만든다.
- {조명}은 음식의 윤기와 김이 자연스럽게 살아나도록 설정하고, 반사광은 과하지 않게 눌러 국물 표면 디테일과 그릇 테두리의 입체감을 선명하게 유지한다.
- 프레임 하단에는 얇은 인스타그램 카드형 정보 영역을 반투명하게 넣고, 음식 위를 과하게 덮지 않도록 프로필 썸네일, 핸들, 위치, 좋아요 수, 짧은 캡션, 해시태그, 저장/공유 마이크로 아이콘을 실제 앱 화면처럼 배치한다.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Main bowl area: {음식}을 선명한 포커스로 두고, 김이 올라오는 부분과 반숙 계란 노른자, 꼬불한 면발, 송송 썬 파, 고춧가루 입자, 국물의 얇은 기름막에 가장 높은 선명도를 준다.
2. Side dish cluster: {음식}에 포함된 김치와 단무지 작은 종지를 볼 가장자리 한쪽에 밀착 배치하고, 김치 양념의 윤기와 단무지의 아이보리 톤이 붉은 국물과 대비되게 한다. 작은 앞접시에는 면을 한 젓가락 집어 올린 흔적처럼 국물 자국과 파 조각을 남긴다.
3. Table context: {배경} 속 보리차 컵, 나무 젓가락, 금속 숟가락, 젓가락 포장지 일부, 사용감 있는 냅킨을 음식보다 낮은 채도와 얕은 심도로 처리해 실제 식탁의 분위기를 만든다.
4. Light behavior: {조명}으로 인해 국물 표면에 얇은 하이라이트가 생기도록 하고, 김은 배경에서 자연스럽게 떠오르듯 보이게 하며, 그릇 안쪽에는 따뜻한 반사광을 남긴다. 컵 표면에는 작은 물방울과 amber tone 보리차 반사를 표현한다.
5. Instagram layer: 하단 카드에는 작은 프로필 원형 썸네일 자리, 핸들 “@{계정명}”, 위치 라벨 “{위치라벨}”, 좋아요 문구 “좋아요 {좋아요수}개”, 캡션 “{짧은캡션}”, 해시태그 “{해시태그}”, 작은 하트/댓글/공유/저장 아이콘, 게시일 “{게시일자}”를 또렷하지만 과하지 않게 넣는다. 우측에는 작은 북마크 아이콘, 좌측에는 댓글 미리보기 “{댓글미리보기}”를 아주 작은 회색 텍스트로 더한다.
6. Framing finish: 전체 프레임은 인스타그램 피드용으로 정돈하되 실제 촬영한 음식 사진처럼 작은 물방울, 그릇의 세라믹 질감, 나무 테이블의 결, 반찬 국물 자국, 냅킨 주름, 젓가락의 나무 섬유가 자연스럽게 보이게 한다.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: 음식 자체에는 큰 텍스트 오버레이를 올리지 않고, 텍스트는 하단 인스타그램 카드 UI와 작은 위치 태그에 앱 캡션처럼 선명하게 배치한다. 한글은 자모가 분리되지 않고 실제 모바일 화면처럼 읽을 수 있어야 한다.
- Color palette: deep red, soy-brown, warm wood brown, egg yolk yellow, pickled radish ivory, kimchi crimson, muted barley tea amber, soft cream UI white, charcoal gray micro text, tiny red heart accent.
- Border/shadow: 음식 아래에는 아주 약한 soft contact shadow를 넣고, 국물과 그릇 테두리는 선명하게 유지한다. 하단 카드 영역은 subtle translucent white panel with soft shadow로 처리하며, 프로필 원형 썸네일과 아이콘에는 실제 앱 UI 같은 얇은 회색 라인을 준다.
- Texture detail: 면발의 탄력, 계란 노른자의 촉촉한 표면, 파 고명의 절단면, 김치 양념 입자, 나무 테이블 결, 유리컵의 응결감, 세라믹 그릇의 유약 번짐이 실제 macro food photography처럼 보이게 한다.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame DSLR, 50mm macro lens at f/2.8, close food photography with crisp garnish detail and shallow depth of field.
- Lighting: window light from upper-left at 45°, soft diffusion through sheer curtain, faint fill from right, subtle steam visibility without haze washout.
- Color grade: vibrant but natural, warm neutral highlights with rich red broth tones and restrained contrast, similar to high-end Instagram food editorials.
- Rendering: photorealistic, natural lens falloff, realistic bowl curvature, fine ceramic glaze detail, believable steam transparency, appetizing wet highlights without plastic shine.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean comfort-food editorial — like a polished Bon Appétit web feature or Kinfolk-style tabletop spread, but focused on lively instant ramen realism with a believable 먹스타그램 post finish. 따뜻한 점심 햇빛, 막 끓여낸 라면의 온기, 집에서 찍었지만 잡지 화보처럼 정돈된 일상 기록의 분위기.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the visible UI text must read exactly “@{계정명}”, “{위치라벨}”, “좋아요 {좋아요수}개”, “{짧은캡션}”, “{해시태그}”, “{댓글미리보기}”, “{게시일자}”; no broken or garbled Korean characters.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: broth surface must look appetizing and realistic; steam should be faint but visible; all garnish and side dishes should remain in their intended positions; no distortion of bowl shape.
- UI placement: 하단 인스타그램 카드 영역은 음식의 핵심인 면, 계란, 국물, 김을 가리지 않으며, 작은 아이콘과 캡션은 실제 모바일 피드처럼 자연스러운 크기로 보이게 한다.
- Realism details: 김치 양념, 단무지 표면 수분, 보리차 컵의 투명도, 나무젓가락 결, 냅킨 주름, 그릇 유약 질감이 사진처럼 자연스럽게 살아 있어야 한다.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public figures

args.default: 끓고 있는 신라면 한 그릇, 반숙 계란, 송송 썬 파, 김치와 단무지 작은 종지

args.default: 원목 식탁 위, 옆에 작은 도자기 컵의 보리차, 젓가락이 살짝 걸쳐 있음

args.name: 구도

studio:prompts3:ours-010.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean webtoon-style vertical 4-panel comic for social sharing, built as a stacked gag strip with clean readability, realistic everyday details, and punchline timing.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Canvas is a tall vertical page with exactly 4 evenly stacked panels, each panel separated by crisp white gutters and thin white borders.
- Add a small webtoon header strip at the very top containing {웹툰제목}, {에피소드번호}, {업로드날짜}, and {작가명}, designed like a social webtoon upload thumbnail header.
- {주인공묘사} should be the consistent main character across all panels, placed as the clear focal subject in every panel.

- Backgrounds should feel like a lived-in Korean studio apartment: rumpled bedding, phone charger, small folding table, convenience-store receipt, cup ramen, laundry basket, wall calendar, sticky notes, slippers, and soft fabric textures that support the joke.
- Speech bubbles, caption boxes, app UI labels, and sound effects must be placed naturally in Korean comic layout and must not cover the main facial expression.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Panel 1 (setup, top 25%): {1컷장면}. Show {주인공묘사} in a relaxed everyday pose, lightly fiddling with a phone and wearing a small smile. Include a cozy bed edge, striped blanket, a low table with snack crumbs, and a wall calendar circled around payday. Add speech bubble text {1컷대사} and a small location/date label {위치날짜라벨}.
2. Panel 2 (development, second 25%): {2컷장면}. Show {주인공묘사} opening a banking app and checking the balance, with one hand hovering over the phone screen and a slight lean forward. Use a close enough framing to make the fake banking UI clear, including {2컷앱텍스트}, {계좌잔액}, a small “입출금” tab, and recent spending rows like “편의점”, “배달”, “교통비”.
3. Panel 3 (twist, third 25%): {3컷장면}. Show {주인공묘사} reacting with wide shocked eyes, one sweat drop, and a slightly open mouth. Exaggerate the facial expression strongly for comedic impact while keeping the same bedroom context. Add large comic sound effect {3컷효과음}, floating receipt icons, tiny coins, and a dramatic dark-blue impact burst behind the head.
4. Panel 4 (punchline, bottom 25%): {4컷장면}. Show {주인공묘사} collapsed under the blanket on the bed, body slumped dramatically, with the scene dimming toward a darker tone to sell the punchline. Add speech bubble text {4컷대사}, a small caption box {4컷캡션}, and a phone notification bubble near the bed that says {알림문구}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Korean webtoon lettering style, hand-drawn speech bubbles, bold comic sound effects; use clean sans-serif bubble text similar to Pretendard/Noto Sans KR, medium to bold weight, readable at small size.
- Color palette: soft flat webtoon colors with off-white #F7F7F7, pale beige #F2E8D8, light hoodie gray #CFCFD4, muted blue-gray #8FA3B8, warm snack-package yellow #F6C85F, receipt-paper gray #E9E6DF, and a darker navy-shadow tone #2E3A4A for punchline contrast.
- Border/shadow: each panel has a neat white border; use subtle 1–2px line weight and very light shadow separation only if needed.
- Add lively Korean comic details such as small sweat marks, motion lines, impact bursts, hand-drawn arrows, sticker-like labels, app UI cards, and tiny reaction marks around the character.
- Character design should remain appealing and modern: clean line art, expressive eyes, simplified hands, soft cel shading, and consistent hoodie, hair shape, face proportions, and room layout across all panels.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm equivalent comic framing with slight perspective variation between panels, mimicking a modern webtoon storyboard rather than a realistic photo.
- Lighting: soft indoor ambient light from an implied window side in panels 1–3, then reduced brightness and heavier shadow in panel 4 to emphasize defeat.
- Color grade: clean pastel webtoon grade with mild cool-neutral balance, then a slightly darker desaturated finish in the final panel.

[6. MOOD]
Modern Korean webtoon gag strip — crisp weekday-comedy energy with the timing and facial exaggeration of a Daum/Kakao webtoon front-page punchline, grounded in believable 자취방 생활감 and small money-anxiety details.

- Required visible Korean text elements: “{웹툰제목}”, “{에피소드번호}”, “{업로드날짜}”, “{작가명}”, “{1컷대사}”, “{2컷앱텍스트}”, “{계좌잔액}”, “{3컷효과음}”, “{4컷대사}”, “{4컷캡션}”, “{알림문구}”, “{채널핸들}”, and “{하단CTA}”.
- Facial expression continuity: the same character design must remain consistent across all 4 panels.
- Panel structure invariant: exactly 4 vertical panels, all with white borders and clear separation.
- Sound effects, app UI, captions, and speech bubbles should follow normal Korean comic placement and never cover the main facial expression.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean melodrama film poster for theatrical release, vertical 9:16 composition with a festival-circuit indie cinema feel.
Romantic, emotionally restrained one-sheet designed to read from a distance and feel premium on social media, cinema lobby displays, and print.
Include believable theatrical poster information such as release date, genre label, production billing, cast/director credits, and small promotional details to make the image feel like a real Korean movie poster.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical poster composition: main character scene fills the upper 2/3, with title, tagline, release information, and billing anchored in the lower 1/3 for strong theatrical hierarchy.
- {시각 주제} positioned as the hero visual, with the face and upper body occupying roughly 55–65% of the frame height.
- Background treatment: expansive night city skyline with rooftop edge, deep atmospheric perspective, soft bokeh lights, visible concrete parapet texture, faint antenna silhouettes, distant apartment windows, and humid night air for believable Seoul atmosphere.
- Title treatment: {영화 제목 KOR} placed near the top or bottom as the largest text element; {영화 제목 ENG} appears smaller beneath it or nearby as a subtitle.
- Add a small genre/date label near the title block: “{장르} · 2026년 5월 29일 대개봉”.
- Tagline {태그라인} set in a modest size, aligned to the cinematic centerline, with a quiet emotional rhythm.
- Add realistic poster details in the bottom area: director line “감독 김도윤”, cast line “출연 윤서하 · 강도현 · 문지안”, production/distribution line “제작 노을필름  배급 달빛픽처스”, ticket teaser “예매 오픈 2026.05.10”, and tiny website/social text “moonlight-movie.kr  @moonlight_film”.
- Add a compact billing block along the bottom edge with narrow condensed text, plus tiny non-official decorative laurel-style graphic flourishes labeled “서울 프리미어” and “관객 추천작” as poster decoration, not as official certification.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero visual zone (upper 2/3): {시각 주제} shown on a Korean urban rooftop at night, with wind-touched hair, subtle facial emotion, realistic skin texture, small clothing folds, and city bokeh behind them.
- Atmospheric background layer: deep navy night sky blended into dark building silhouettes, with warm amber window lights, rooftop safety railing, faint streetlight glow below, a few dusty rose highlight accents, and slight haze to support the melancholy-romantic tone.
- Typography block: {영화 제목 KOR} in a bold serif Korean title treatment, large and dramatic, with {영화 제목 ENG} in smaller clean sans-serif or condensed serif beneath it for international-film-poster balance.
- Supporting text block: include “{장르}”, “2026년 5월 29일 대개봉”, “상영시간 118분”, “예매 오픈”, and a short quote-style line such as “올해 가장 오래 남을 밤의 이야기” in small Korean type.
- Tagline zone: {태그라인} placed below the main title or above the credits, centered or slightly offset, using restrained spacing and a quieter size than the title.
- Credits / poster billing: director and cast names in tiny sans-serif near the bottom, with production company, distributor, music, cinematography, screenplay, and poster credit text arranged like a real Korean theatrical release billing block.
- Add a small vertical spine/edge credit along one side: “NOEUL FILM PRESENTS · {영화 제목 ENG} · 2026”.
- Surface finish: add slight film grain, realistic printed poster texture, gentle contrast roll-off, subtle halation on city lights, and a painterly enhancement on facial features while keeping the image photo-realistic overall.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold serif Korean title like Noto Serif KR or a high-contrast editorial serif, heavy weight for the main title; English subtitle in clean sans-serif such as Pretendard or Inter, light-to-regular weight; tiny credit text in condensed sans-serif.
- Color palette: use the exact mood of {컬러} — deep navy #0B132B, warm amber #F4A261, muted rose #C98C9C, soft charcoal #1B1F2A, and off-black shadows.
- Border/shadow: subtle title drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 18% opacity; cinematic edge vignette around the frame to draw attention to the face, rooftop, and title without crushing shadow detail.
- Text integration: all added Korean poster copy should feel professionally typeset, aligned to a real print grid, with varied font weights for hierarchy: title, tagline, release date, cast, billing, website/social.
- Graphic details: include small line dividers, tiny dot separators, fine-print production credits, and a discreet QR/ticket placeholder block near the bottom corner labeled “예매 정보” to increase realism.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame cinematic portrait look, Canon EOS R5 with 85mm f/1.4 at f/2.0, shallow depth of field, poster-ready detail and clean facial separation from background.
- Lighting: soft city ambient with a cool overhead night base, plus warm practical lights from the skyline; slight rim light from screen-left to outline hair and shoulders, with gentle fill to preserve facial expression.
- Color grade: moody midnight blue with amber highlights and a faint dusty rose cast on skin and reflective surfaces, similar to a refined Korean indie festival film still.
- Production realism: visible rooftop concrete texture, faint breathy night atmosphere, tiny reflected city lights in the eyes, realistic clothing fabric, and a subtle print-grade grain layer suitable for a theatrical one-sheet.

[6. MOOD]
A Korean indie melodrama one-sheet with the emotional restraint of a Cannes-style festival poster and the romantic night palette of a Park Chan-wook-adjacent cinematic still.
The poster should feel like a real upcoming Korean theatrical release: intimate, cinematic, text-rich in the lower billing area, and emotionally grounded rather than a generic mockup.

[1. PURPOSE]
1990s–early 2000s Korean nostalgia interior scene, photo-realistic cinematic film still.
A vertical poster-like image that recreates a cramped late-night PC room with era-specific details, readable Korean signage, snack-and-cigarette traces, analog clutter, and a slightly hazy, memory-like atmosphere.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main scene should feel like a lived-in nostalgic interior, with {장소} occupying the full frame as the primary environment.
- The camera view is {시점}, keeping the room depth visible while compressing the crowded layout of desks, seats, monitors, vending/payment machines, and wall notices.
- Fill the space with {디테일} arranged naturally across foreground, midground, and background so the room feels dense, tactile, and believable.
- Use {시간대} to justify the exterior reflections, faint streetlight spill, wet pavement glow, and low-light interior mood.
- Preserve narrow walking lanes, tight desk spacing, stacked personal belongings, and layered objects so the scene reads as an authentic old PC room rather than a staged set.
- Add human traces without making people the main subject: half-pushed chairs, a jacket over a chair back, greasy keyboard shine, crumpled receipts, used paper cups, cigarette ash, coin change, mouse pads, floppy disks, CD cases, and a plastic membership card.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground: show a few close beige CRT edges, worn tabletop corners, scratched mouse pads, a chipped keyboard, coins, a half-empty paper cup, and the nearest red plastic chair partially cropped to make the viewer feel inside the room.
- Midground: line up multiple bulky CRT monitors in a checkerboard-like row, each with faint screen glow, old Korean game lobby windows, dial-up-era UI fragments, scattered instant noodle cups, chopsticks, cigarette packs, snack wrappers, wired ball mice, and tangled LAN cables.
- Rear area: place the coin-operated machine, payment counter corner, dim wall surfaces, a small snack price board, a dusty wall clock, a 1990s calendar, taped LAN-party flyers, and diffuse smoky air near the back so the room depth stays visible through the haze.
- Ceiling layer: keep the fluorescent tubes prominent, slightly flickering, with uneven light spill that creates a sickly yellow-green cast across the room; include discolored ceiling panels, exposed cable clips, and a small rotating fan or ventilation grille.
- Window/reflection layer: show muted city-night reflections on glass surfaces using {시간대}, with dark exterior contrast against the interior tungsten warmth; add faint reversed neon, rain-speckled glass, and silhouettes of nearby shop signs outside.
- Wall detail layer: include worn Korean computer-room notices and pricing signs such as “인터넷 1시간 1,000원”, “야간정액 5,000원”, “라면 1,500원”, “프린트 1장 100원”, “회원카드 문의”, and “조용히 해주세요”, taped or laminated with curled corners.
- Atmospheric layer: add humid air, mild heat haze from old machines, cigarette-smoke diffusion, dust motes in fluorescent light, greasy reflections on plastic, and subtle VHS-era texture so the image feels like an old memory captured on film.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: if text appears, use worn 1990s Korean computer-room signage style, bold condensed sans-serif or laminated notice typography, slightly uneven printing, 28–40px equivalent for larger signs and smaller legible text for price boards and flyers.
- Color palette: sickly fluorescent yellow-green, warm tungsten amber, dusty teal shadows, faded gray-brown plastics, muted black, dim off-white highlights, nicotine-stained beige, faded red plastic, and occasional small blue CRT glow.
- Surface detail: emphasize scratched plastic monitor shells, dust on ventilation slots, sticky tabletops, worn chair legs, curled tape, yellowed paper, frayed cable sleeves, ashtray residue, noodle broth stains, and fingerprints on glass.
- Composition density: the frame should feel packed with real late-night PC room life while still allowing the repeated grid of CRT monitors and the narrow aisle to guide the eye into the background.
- Image treatment: use natural cinematic falloff with soft contrast compression, faint 35mm film grain veil, analog color bleed, slight halation around fluorescent tubes, and subtle shadow pooling under chairs and desks.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm film look, full-frame camera feel, 24mm wide lens with a slight fisheye impression, f/2.8, eye-level perspective.
- Lighting: overhead fluorescent tubes as the main source, flickering slightly; weak tungsten practicals from interior fixtures; faint spill from the city night outside; CRT screen glow from several stations; low-key contrast with soft ambient bounce.
- Color grade: slightly desaturated muddy palette with fluorescent yellow-green highlights, warm interior amber mids, dusty teal shadows, nicotine-yellow neutrals, faded red accents, and a subtle analog VHS-era tint.
- Realism: render as a photographic interior still with believable optics, imperfect exposure, shallow grime detail, practical reflections, and physically plausible smoke diffusion.

[6. MOOD]
Korean late-1990s memory piece — like a cinephile still from a retro coming-of-age film, with the tactile grime, machine warmth, stale smoke, fluorescent fatigue, and emotional distance of a Wong Kar-wai urban interior.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render Korean signs cleanly and legibly where visible, especially “인터넷 1시간 1,000원”, “야간정액 5,000원”, “라면 1,500원”, “프린트 1장 100원”, “회원카드 문의”, and “조용히 해주세요”.
- Layout invariants: keep the room crowded but legible; the CRT monitors must read as a repeated grid; the scene must remain photo-realistic and not turn into illustration or anime.
- Era accuracy: use bulky beige CRT monitors, wired keyboards, wired ball mice, old PC towers, analog posters, laminated notices, coin/payment machines, and early-internet Korean PC room details from the late 1990s to early 2000s.
- Atmosphere: the room should feel late-night, humid, smoky, and used, with layered foreground-midground-background depth and natural incidental mess.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
