[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- 2x3 grid layout: six equal square cells arranged inside a rounded square preview card, with consistent gutters, soft cream paper texture, and gentle pastel divider lines between cells.
- Character placement: {캐릭터 디자인} placed as the main subject in each panel, occupying about 65–75% of each cell, with room for speech bubbles, motion marks, hearts, sweat drops, sleep symbols, or tiny decorative reaction stickers.
- Text placement: {6가지 멘트} shown as Korean speech bubbles or floating captions in each cell, clear, bold, and legible at mobile thumbnail size.
- Preview-page details: add a small Korean title strip at the top reading "톡톡 반응 6종 세트", a tiny creator credit such as "작가: 오늘의 캐릭터", a small version label "VOL.06", and subtle bottom metadata like "미리보기" and small page dots; keep these secondary and smaller than the six main captions.
- Background treatment: warm pale cream sticker-sheet background with faint KakaoTalk-like chat wallpaper motifs, small stars, hearts, dots, tape corners, and soft drop shadows that make the sheet feel like a real downloadable emoticon preview.
- Consistency: same character design across all 6 panels, only pose, expression, gesture, emotion icons, and caption change.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Overall sheet: create a polished 2x3 emoji grid on a warm cream rounded card, with six preview cells separated by soft pastel gutters, a small top header bar, and subtle app-preview metadata elements.
2) Top-left panel: show {캐릭터 디자인} with a friendly greeting expression, waving or leaning forward, paired with the first message from {6가지 멘트} in a rounded speech bubble; add small sparkle marks and a tiny pastel hello icon.
3) Top-middle panel: show {캐릭터 디자인} reacting with gratitude, using a soft smile, clasped hands or a polite bow, and the second message from {6가지 멘트}; add blush, small flower or ribbon accents.
4) Top-right panel: show {캐릭터 디자인} with a shocked or flustered face, wide eyes, sweat drop, motion lines, and the third message from {6가지 멘트}; use a playful burst bubble behind the caption.
5) Bottom-left panel: show {캐릭터 디자인} in an angry or annoyed pose, cheeks puffed or tiny stomp gesture, with the fourth message from {6가지 멘트} placed prominently but still cute; add red-orange comic marks and tiny steam puffs.
6) Bottom-middle panel: show {캐릭터 디자인} making a heart/love gesture, holding a heart, finger-heart pose, or surrounded by floating hearts, paired with the fifth message from {6가지 멘트}; make this panel warm peach and pink.
7) Bottom-right panel: show {캐릭터 디자인} sleepy and relaxed, tucked into a tiny cushion or cozy blanket-like sticker shape, paired with the sixth message from {6가지 멘트} in a tiny cozy caption bubble; add moon, zzz symbols, and soft blue accents.
8) Text rendering: all Korean caption text from {6가지 멘트} must be crisp, centered, and evenly spaced within each bubble; header and metadata text should be smaller and secondary, never competing with the six intended captions.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: rounded Korean sans style similar to Pretendard Rounded or Noto Sans KR Rounded, bold for short exclamations, medium for longer lines, size tuned for sticker readability; add tiny secondary Korean UI labels in a lighter weight.
- Color palette: use {아트 스타일} with soft pastel accents; prioritize cream #FFF8EE, light blue #CFE8FF, peach #FFD6C9, mint #D7F4E3, butter yellow #FFE8A3, soft pink #FFC7DE, and charcoal #2B2B2B for text outlines.
- Linework: clean vector outlines with consistent stroke width, smooth curves, expressive face details, soft blush, gentle highlights, and small comic reaction marks for each emotion.
- Border/shadow: rounded sticker-card frame with pale pastel dividers, light soft shadow under the character in each cell, 2px y-offset, 8px blur, 12% opacity; add slight sticker cutline effect around the character for a real emoticon-pack preview feel.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing digital illustration look, equivalent to a clean studio product render, no perspective distortion, flat sticker-sheet composition.
- Lighting: even diffuse studio lighting from above, no harsh shadows, uniform brightness across all six panels, with gentle ambient shading on the card and speech bubbles.
- Color grade: pastel KakaoTalk UI palette with soft cream base and gentle candy colors, slightly warm-neutral overall balance; lively but still readable on a mobile messenger screen.

[6. MOOD]
Cute Korean messenger sticker pack — a cheerful KakaoTalk-style emoticon preview sheet with the playful clarity of a LINE sticker set, enriched with real app-preview details, tiny decorative reaction icons, and a polished downloadable sticker-pack presentation.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: every rendered Korean string from {6가지 멘트} must appear exactly and clearly as specified.
- Include small supplementary Korean preview text only if crisp and intentional, such as "톡톡 반응 6종 세트", "작가: 오늘의 캐릭터", "VOL.06", and "미리보기".
- All 6 panels must use the same character design from {캐릭터 디자인}; only expression, pose, gesture, emotion icons, and caption change.
- Each panel must contain one distinct emotional reaction and one corresponding Korean text bubble.
- Do not let secondary metadata, decorative icons, or wallpaper motifs obscure the six main Korean captions.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Magazine cover base — Build the full image as a 1990s Korean monthly magazine cover with masthead, issue number, date label, barcode area, feature headline blurbs, small spine/credit text, model-name credit, and lightly aged printed-paper finish.
2) Background base — Build {장소} as a nostalgic coastal scene with an expansive sky, a thin horizon line, calm reflective sea, wet sand, distant seawall, small fishing boats, utility poles, and real environmental texture rendered in flat shapes and crisp linework.
3) Subject block — Place {피사체} in the left third, fully visible, with clear bicycle outline, readable clothing folds, natural walking posture, correct wheel geometry, and believable contact shadows on the sand or pavement.
4) Era atmosphere — Infuse {시대 분위기} through subdued pastel contrast, 90s casual wardrobe styling, slightly faded print registration, soft beach signage, analog-magazine layout, and small nostalgic details such as a cassette-player strap, windbreaker texture, or canvas tote if appropriate.
5) Editorial content layer — Add short Korean cover lines that feel like a real lifestyle magazine: a masthead at the top, VOL/date label, 2-3 feature blurbs, a model-name credit near the subject, a barcode at bottom right, and tiny publisher/spine text along one edge.
6) Surface treatment — Apply subtle film grain, paper fiber, halftone dot texture in shadow areas, slight ink misregistration, sun-faded edges, and hand-drawn imperfections while keeping the illustration polished and cover-ready.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: render Korean magazine-cover text accurately, using bold 1990s editorial lettering for the masthead and short headline blurbs; integrate text with the illustration like a real printed cover rather than floating UI labels.
- Required cover elements: large masthead text '청춘해변', issue label 'VOL.006', date label '1996년 8월호', price '₩3,500', model credit '모델: 지은', small credit text '사진풍 일러스트 · 여름 특별호', and a barcode area with small numbers at the lower right.
- Feature headline blurbs: include 2-3 short Korean blurbs such as '바람이 데려온 휴일', '자전거로 가는 바다길', '그 시절 여름의 색', arranged along the right side and lower third in a natural magazine-cover hierarchy.
- Color palette: cream #F4E9D8, coral #E98A7A, dusty teal #6F9A9A, muted sky blue #AFC4D8, soft sand #D8C6A6, charcoal linework #2D2A28.
- Border/shadow: use a soft print-like edge fade, faint fold or scan-edge wear, gentle paper shadow at the perimeter, and subtle atmospheric separation between layers.
- Rendering: flat color blocking, crisp contour lines, low-contrast matte finish, visible paper grain, occasional halftone shading, and slight ink misregistration feel without making the image look damaged.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm documentary wide shot equivalent, vertical editorial framing, low horizon placement, no shallow depth-of-field effect.
- Lighting: late sunset golden-hour light from frame right, gentle backlit rim on hair and shoulders, warm reflections on bicycle metal, soft ambient fill from the sky, and long subtle shadows across the beach foreground.
- Color grade: faded 1990s print palette with warm cream highlights, coral accents, muted teal shadows, slightly washed sky blue midtones, and realistic sun-aged magazine ink density.
- Print realism: emulate a scanned vintage Korean magazine cover with paper fibers, mild corner wear, light halftone texture, tiny registration offsets around charcoal linework, and believable ink absorption on cream stock.

[6. MOOD]
Korean 90s nostalgia mixed with Japanese city pop editorial art — like a summer lifestyle magazine found in an old bookstore, combining Pixiv subculture illustration, gentle seaside melancholy, and warm analog print charm.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: all visible Korean text must be clean and legible, especially '청춘해변', 'VOL.006', '1996년 8월호', '₩3,500', '모델: 지은', '바람이 데려온 휴일', '자전거로 가는 바다길', '그 시절 여름의 색', and '사진풍 일러스트 · 여름 특별호'.
- Keep all text short, cover-like, and properly aligned; do not generate garbled Hangul, random pseudo-Korean, or unreadable character clusters.
- Anatomy/layout invariants when relevant: the bicycle must be anatomically coherent and fully readable; keep {피사체} in the left third; no cropped face, no distorted wheels, no duplicated limbs, and no extra main character competing with the subject.
- Magazine-cover realism: include issue number, date label, barcode area, 2-3 Korean feature blurbs, small spine/credit text, and model-name credit while preserving the coastal illustration as the hero image.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Ultra-detailed photorealistic miniature LED diorama box, 1:6 scale. Korean solo apartment room diorama for product-style showcase, designed to look like a premium handmade miniature set with believable daily-life clutter, tiny printed labels, and warm practical lighting.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: a front-facing miniature room inside a wooden box frame, occupying about 78% of the frame, with the glass panel visible at the front edge and subtle reflections revealing it as a physical display object.
- Camera angle: slightly angled top-down 3/4 perspective, showing the room depth clearly while keeping the front wall, desk surface, bed corner, and right-side storage readable.
- Background treatment: exterior stays dim charcoal gray so the interior emits a strong warm glow; the surrounding studio area should feel like a premium product-photo setup with natural tabletop shadows.
- Spatial layout: {방 컨셉} determines the room footprint and overall density; place {가구·소품} so the layout feels realistic in a cramped Korean studio, with objects tucked under shelves, beside the bed, and near the door area.
- Detail emphasis: {디테일} should be visible as small but readable narrative accents, integrated into the desk surface, bedding, wall, shelf, and floor as everyday traces of someone living there.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Box frame (outer 8%): wooden miniature enclosure with clean handmade edges, matte walnut tone, subtle wear on corners, tiny miter seams, a clear glass front panel with faint reflections, and a small brass-like nameplate on the base reading “자취방 LED 디오라마”.
- Room shell (inner 90%): narrow one-room Korean apartment with off-white walls, light wood floor, compact ceiling height, tiny baseboards, visible wall outlet plates, an intercom panel by the entry side, and a small frosted window hinting at nighttime city lights outside.
- Left zone: place the bed and nearby storage to anchor the sleeping area; bedding should be slightly rumpled with a folded blanket, pillow indentation, small plush keychain, slippers beside the bed, and a tote bag or laundry basket tucked near the storage.
- Center zone: set the desk, monitor, laptop, keyboard, mouse, cup ramen, chopsticks, half-full water bottle, phone charger cable, sticky notes, open notebook, receipts, and a tiny convenience-store snack scene together so the workspace reads as the visual focal point.
- Right zone: position the mini fridge, small TV, hanger rack, potted plant, stacked plastic drawers, umbrella, recycling bag, and a narrow shoe mat to create a lived-in residential corner typical of a Korean studio.
- Wall and shelf layer: add a tiny calendar, delivery menu flyer, transit card, postcard, mini books, skincare bottles, tissue box, and a small framed photo or simple poster; include realistic paper thickness and slight curling at the corners.
- Ceiling layer: add warm yellow LED strip lighting along the ceiling edges, with tiny visible light points, wiring hints, and gentle glow falloff across the walls and furniture so the room appears softly illuminated from within.
- Narrative micro-details: show {디테일} naturally embedded on the desk surface, TV screen, shelf area, and floor corners, with enough clarity to reward close inspection while keeping scale believable.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: any visible miniature text must look physically printed on paper, packaging, labels, stickers, calendars, receipts, or the small base nameplate; use tiny clean sans-serif Korean, not floating UI text.
- Include Korean micro text where appropriate: calendar “2026년 5월”, sticky note “월세 납부”, ramen cup “김치라면”, delivery flyer “분식·치킨”, notebook title “오늘 할 일”, and small shelf label “생활용품”.
- Color palette: warm amber #F4C76A, soft tungsten yellow #FFD98A, off-white #F3EFE7, light oak #C8A97E, neutral gray #A9A9A9, deep charcoal #2B2B2B.
- Border/shadow: crisp product-shadow under the wooden base, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; glass reflections should be faint, realistic, and shaped by the room lights.
- Materials: emphasize tactile handmade realism—slightly uneven wood grain, matte painted walls, translucent plastic drawers, glossy ramen cup, woven fabric texture on bedding, tiny paper edges, reflective monitor glass, and soft dust in corners.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with RF 85mm f/1.2L at f/8, product-photography clarity with deep detail retention and minimal distortion.
- Lighting: studio setup with warm LED practicals inside the room, subtle softbox fill from upper-left at 45°, and a very light rim from the right to separate the box edges; LEDs should cast miniature-scale shadows under shelves, chair legs, and desk objects.
- Color grade: warm cream + amber + muted brown with slightly boosted local contrast; keep blacks clean but not crushed, preserving tiny details in the dim exterior and glass edge.
- Rendering quality: macro product photo realism, crisp focus across the diorama, fine dust specks on glass only where natural, physically plausible reflections, and scale-consistent depth cues.

[6. MOOD]
Premium miniature product photo with the meticulous handcrafted feel of a Museum of Miniature Arts display, combined with the intimate glow of a late-night K-drama apartment set after a long workday, cozy, personal, slightly messy, and emotionally lived-in.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if visible, render Korean micro text correctly: “자취방 LED 디오라마”, “2026년 5월”, “월세 납부”, “김치라면”, “분식·치킨”, “오늘 할 일”, “생활용품”.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: miniature objects must remain proportionally consistent to 1:6 scale; room must stay visually readable as a compact Korean studio apartment; no warped geometry or floating furniture.
- Preserve the requested concept from {방 컨셉}, include {가구·소품} as the main furnishing set, and make {디테일} the close-inspection storytelling details.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
K-pop debut album poster in a vertical 9:16 magazine-cover format, designed for promotional display and social sharing.
High-gloss editorial cover look with a dominant central idol image, headline typography, album-launch information, barcode area, feature blurbs, and cyberpunk neon energy.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center composition: {콘셉트 / 피사체} fills the middle 60–70% of the frame, with the most important face/body posture kept in the upper-center third for cover impact.
- Header zone: {아티스트 이름 KOR} sits at the top as the primary masthead, with {아티스트 이름 ENG} placed directly below in smaller English type.
- Magazine-poster details: add a small issue label near the masthead such as "DEBUT ISSUE VOL.01" and "2026년 5월호", plus a thin vertical spine line with tiny credit text along one side.
- Background treatment: futuristic rooftop cityscape at night with deep navy sky, blurred high-rise lights, LED billboards, distant traffic trails, reflective wet surfaces, metallic rooftop rails, cables, vents, and neon purple/pink glow accents.
- Editorial cover content: place 2–3 short Korean feature headline blurbs around the hero image without covering faces, for example "새로운 밤의 시작", "4개의 빛, 하나의 세계", "데뷔 쇼케이스 공개".
- Bottom metadata area: include an album-release block, hashtag-style text, small barcode box, model-name credit, and compact showcase information as part of the poster design.
- Overall framing: vertical magazine cover crop, tight editorial framing, polished and premium, with dense but controlled real-world magazine details surrounding the central group.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top masthead area (15–18%): set {아티스트 이름 KOR} in large Korean serif display type, centered or slightly arched, with strong contrast strokes and crisp edges; add "DEBUT ISSUE VOL.01" above or beside it in small uppercase type.
2. Subtitle line (5–7%): place {아티스트 이름 ENG} immediately below the Korean title in a smaller clean sans-serif, tracking slightly expanded for fashion-magazine clarity; add a date label "2026년 5월호" near the right side of the subtitle zone.
3. Hero image area (middle 60–65%): render {콘셉트 / 피사체} as the dominant visual, with each member clearly separated by pose, styling, hair silhouette, and expression so faces and shoulders remain individually readable.
4. Background depth: build a neon cyberpunk rooftop scene behind the group, with city bokeh, holographic light streaks, LED signage, rain-slick floor reflections, metal guardrails, rooftop machinery, and glossy reflections on metallic surfaces.
5. Lighting accents: add dramatic rim light around hair and shoulders, plus subtle magenta and cyan edge glow to separate the figures from the dark skyline; include small realistic specular highlights on jewelry, leather, satin, or sequined fabric.
6. Side feature blurbs: arrange short Korean cover lines along left and right edges, such as "나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답", "첫 번째 싱글 공개", and "네온으로 쓰는 데뷔의 순간"; use varied sizes like a real music magazine cover.
7. Bottom information band (8–10%): place "#DEBUT #2026 #VOL01" in a compact editorial block, add "ALBUM RELEASE 6PM KST", "데뷔 쇼케이스 2026.05.01 FRI 20:00", "서울 잠실 아레나", a small barcode area, and tiny credit text "PHOTO BY STUDIO NEON / STYLING TEAM LUMI".

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a high-contrast Korean serif similar to Cormorant Garamond / Noto Serif KR styling for the title, paired with a modern sans-serif like Pretendard or Inter for the English subtitle, feature blurbs, metadata, barcode label, and credits; title weight should feel heavy and premium, subtitle medium weight, metadata small and clean.
- Color palette: {컬러} with blackened navy, electric purple, hot pink, and small cyan highlights; let the neon colors appear as accents rather than fully washing out the scene.
- Editorial decoration: use subtle glossy magazine-style shadowing, soft outer glow around neon elements, a faint vignette at the edges, thin divider rules, small price/date labels, barcode graphics, and tiny production credits; title can have a thin dark outline or shadow for readability.
- Layout behavior: keep the central idol group visually dominant while surrounding them with believable album-poster information, magazine cover lines, and rooftop environment details.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 85mm portrait lens look at f/1.8 for the group hero shot, with shallow depth of field and controlled background separation; magazine cover sharpness on the faces and title.
- Lighting: dramatic studio-style key from upper-left combined with neon rim light from the right and behind, plus reflective bounce from the rooftop surface; maintain high contrast with controlled specular highlights.
- Color grade: glossy cyberpunk grading with deep navy shadows, magenta-purple mids, and electric cyan reflections; preserve skin tone realism while keeping the environment stylized.
- Material detail: realistic makeup, glossy lips, styled hair strands, metallic accessories, layered stage outfits, reflective boots, wet pavement texture, glass highlights, and softly blooming neon signage.

[6. MOOD]
High-fashion K-pop debut editorial — a Vogue Korea / Dazed-style cover with cyberpunk concert energy, premium album-launch polish, and the atmosphere of a real collectible debut poster found inside a special album package.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표시할 문자열: "{아티스트 이름 KOR}", "{아티스트 이름 ENG}", "#DEBUT #2026 #VOL01".
- Additional readable Korean cover text to include: "2026년 5월호", "새로운 밤의 시작", "4개의 빛, 하나의 세계", "데뷔 쇼케이스 공개", "나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답", "데뷔 쇼케이스 2026.05.01 FRI 20:00", "서울 잠실 아레나".
- Four-member group requirement: exactly 4 K-pop girl group members, each with distinct pose and expression, all rendered with realistic anatomy and exactly 5 fingers per hand.
- Cover layout invariant: top masthead, central hero group image, side feature blurbs, and bottom metadata/barcode block must all remain clearly separated and readable.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized real-person likenesses

[1. PURPOSE]
Illustrated Korean city food-map infographic for social sharing, combining tourist landmarks, neighborhood routes, local food spots, and small travel-editorial details in a hand-drawn atlas style.
Editorial poster look with whimsical mascot branding, designed like a vintage Korean travel map you’d frame, save, or post online, with enough real guidebook information to feel useful and lived-in.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the map as a square composition with the title band occupying the top 14% and the footer warning occupying the bottom 8%.
- Use {도시 이름} and {지도 제목} as the main header text, with the mascot placed beside the title as a compact emblem.
- Build the map on a tactile parchment background with yellow street lines, blue river shapes, green park masses, subway dots, market blocks, alley clusters, tiny food doodles, and hand-labeled district callouts.
- Wrap the entire map with {테두리 장식} as a decorative border, keeping corner density slightly heavier than the sides and adding small illustrated corner motifs such as chopsticks, street lamps, leaves, and steam curls.
- Add realistic guide-map details: a compass rose, scale bar, small grid coordinates, illustrated walking-route arrows, a mini transit badge row, page-like registration text, and a compact QR-style square marked 여행 메모.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header area (top 14%): set {도시 이름} + {지도 제목} in a bold illustrated headline, with the mascot directly adjacent to the title block like a stamp logo. Add small guide text such as VOL.003, 2026년 봄 개정판, 오늘의 골목 미식 산책, and a tiny credit line 지도 그림: 로컬에디터.
- Main map field (middle 62%): draw the city network on textured beige parchment, with roads in warm yellow, the river in muted blue, parks in soft green blocks, subway lines in thin charcoal strokes, pedestrian alleys as dotted lines, and small icons for markets, bridges, hills, cafés, and night streets.
- Landmark layer: place {랜드마크 1}, {랜드마크 2}, {랜드마크 3}, {랜드마크 4}, {랜드마크 5}, {랜드마크 6} clearly at their respective city positions, each paired with a small icon or map pin for fast recognition.
- Food-spot layer: place {맛집 1}, {맛집 2}, {맛집 3}, {맛집 4}, {맛집 5}, {맛집 6}, {맛집 7}, {맛집 8} in visually balanced clusters near commercial districts, markets, station exits, and nightlife areas so the map feels navigable and rich with local texture.
- Add 3 short route ribbons across the map: 아침 산책 코스, 점심 줄서는 길, 야식 골목 루트, each drawn as a colored dashed path with tiny numbered circles.
- Legend box: include the category key for 맛집, 랜드마크, 공원, 한강, 지하철역 in a compact corner panel with simple pictograms, plus marker styles for 추천 동선 and 사진 스팟.
- Add a small side-note panel with handwritten guide copy: 현지인 추천, 비 오는 날도 좋음, 웨이팅 체크, 포장 가능, using tiny checkboxes and sticker-like labels.
- Footer strip (bottom 8%): render the warning line in small handwritten-style text, centered and separated from the map body by a thin rule. Include page number MAP 01, tiny copyright-style credit 로컬 미식 지도, and a small barcode-like decorative block.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold for the title at large display size, Noto Sans KR Medium for labels, and a hand-drawn brush style for the footer note and side annotations.
- Color palette: parchment #F3E6C8, warm yellow #D8B14A, river blue #5E8FB8, park green #7DAA63, chili red #C9412A, charcoal ink #2E2A26.
- Border/shadow: apply a thin ink-outline frame with slightly irregular watercolor edges, plus a subtle paper shadow 3px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity.
- Illustration density: use layered watercolor washes, visible paper grain, ink bleeds, pencil-like micro labels, and small food illustrations such as 국수 그릇, 만두, 김밥, 떡볶이, 커피잔, and grilled skewers around the relevant 맛집 pins.
- Layout realism: make the map feel like a printed city-guide page photographed or scanned from a boutique travel booklet, including small imperfections, registration ticks, soft stain marks, and uneven hand-drawn linework.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat lay infographic look, like a scanned illustrated atlas page; emulate a 35mm documentary graphic composition rather than a photo-realistic city rendering.
- Lighting: even studio illumination with gentle paper depth, preserving paper texture, watercolor pigment variation, and ink line clarity.
- Color grade: vintage parchment warmth with restrained teal-blue river accents, muted natural greens, saturated chili-red highlights, and slightly faded printed-ink edges.

[6. MOOD]

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Cinematic editorial photo of a small independent café tucked inside a Seoul alley, designed like a 35mm film still for social media or poster-style display.
Quiet interior scene with a warm late-afternoon window-light mood, combining food, book, tabletop storytelling, and believable neighborhood café details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: the table vignette occupies the lower 55% of the frame, with the window-lit background, alley glimpse, and café interior filling the upper 45%.
- {장면 설명} should be staged as the hero composition, slightly off-center for a natural film-still feel, with clear foreground-to-background depth.
- Background treatment: narrow Seoul alley café interior with pale plaster walls, wood shelving, a small counter, ceramic cups, a chalk menu board, a couple of softly blurred seats, and a partial alley view through the window.
- Framing: use an intimate vertical crop that lets the eye move from the latte cup to the open book, hand gesture, pastry plate, receipt, and softly glowing window area.
- {분위기} should be expressed through restrained posture, late-afternoon quietness, natural café activity traces, and subtle lived-in details such as a spoon, napkin, bookmark, tote strap, or condensation on a water glass.
- {컬러 팔레트} should guide all décor accents, surface tones, ceramics, textiles, book cover, signage, and highlight color balance.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground layer: a warm wooden bar table with visible grain, small scratches, softly reflective finish, and a single latte cup as the primary focal point.
- Hero object cluster: place {장면 설명} on the table surface, with the latte cup closest to camera, the open book slightly behind it, a relaxed hand entering from one side, and supporting details like a small butter pastry plate, folded receipt, teaspoon, linen napkin, and bookmark.
- Midground: café counter edge, chair backs, stacked ceramic cups, a small vase with seasonal flowers, coffee grinder silhouette, and blurred interior elements should remain secondary while adding believable depth.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean city pop lo-fi illustration, Pixiv-inspired subculture artwork for a vertical music-poster layout.
Urban nighttime driving scene with a stylish Korean woman in the driver’s seat, designed as a rich flat-shaded editorial illustration with realistic car-interior details, glowing Seoul night scenery, and integrated retro poster typography.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {인물 묘사} placed in a 3/4 side medium close-up or near-frontal composition, with the face occupying about one-third of the frame and remaining the emotional anchor of the poster.
- Scene setting: {장면 설명} as the core narrative, with the car interior clearly readable in the foreground: steering wheel, dashboard glow, rear-view mirror, seat belt, door trim, side window frame, keychain, cassette tape or small convenience-store drink placed naturally in the cabin.
- Background treatment: {배경 디테일} layered behind the subject with recognizable Seoul night elements such as Han River bridge lights, apartment silhouettes, riverside road lamps, neon shop signs, bus-stop panels, and soft light trails reflected on the glass.
- Framing direction: vertical poster composition with a strong driver-seat viewpoint, keeping the face, hands, steering wheel, window reflections, and outside skyline all visible in a cinematic arrangement.
- Poster overlay: add tasteful city-pop graphic elements around the image area, including a main Korean title, date label, catalog/issue number, barcode area, short playlist/event details, and small sponsor/credit text without covering the face.
- Composition reference: follow {구도} and {비율} while preserving the 1024x1536 vertical poster feeling.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Hero subject area: {인물 묘사} rendered with a calm confident expression, clean facial shapes, realistic proportions, soft retro makeup details, natural hair highlights, and accurate hand anatomy if hands are visible on the steering wheel.
2) Interior foreground: steering wheel, dashboard edge, instrument cluster glow, gear selector, fabric or leather seat texture, door handle, side mirror, and small personal objects arranged as believable shapes that support the driver-seat viewpoint.
3) Window layer: layered reflections across the car window, combining bridge lights, neon signage, rain-speckled glass or faint windshield streaks, passing headlights, and dashboard reflections to create a late-night lo-fi drive mood.
4) Background layer: {배경 디테일} arranged as glowing urban forms, with Han River bridge lights stretching horizontally, riverside apartment windows, street signs, and neon storefront fragments adding Korean city rhythm.
5) Poster information layer: include a retro editorial header and footer such as “SEOUL CITY POP DRIVE”, “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “한강 야간 드라이브”, “20:30 / 반포대교 방면”, “TICKET ₩25,000”, a small barcode block, and tiny credit text like “model: 지윤 / illust: studio 88”.
6) Style integration: {화풍} applied uniformly across character, car, typography, and background, preserving flat shading, smooth outlines, graphic shape language, and carefully placed print-like texture.
7) Palette application: {컬러 톤} used with matte, slightly faded blocks of color; neon accents appear in signage, dashboard indicators, window reflections, and headline accents while the overall palette remains cohesive.
8) Scene emphasis: {장면 설명} should feel like one captured late-night moment, with driving motion implied through light trails, reflections, hair movement, and small dashboard details.
9) Final polish: make the image feel like a finished Korean city-pop poster sold at a record shop or indie illustration fair, with purposeful composition, readable text zones, and atmospheric urban detail.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: include integrated retro Korean/English poster typography using bold geometric sans-serif and condensed 1980s magazine lettering. Set bold cover line in Korean: “나다운 밤, 서울을 달리다”. Add smaller Korean blurbs such as “시티팝 플레이리스트”, “한강의 네온과 라디오”, “오늘의 드라이브 코스”.
- Color palette: use {컬러 톤} as the main palette, with faded cyan, coral, mustard, violet-blue shadows, and neon pink accents; keep blacks softened into deep navy rather than pure black.
- Graphic layout: combine the illustrated driving scene with poster bands, small corner labels, a barcode rectangle, cassette-track numbering, and thin decorative divider lines that match the city-pop theme.
- Shadow and light: use soft cell-shaded shadow blocks, dashboard under-lighting, neon rim highlights, and controlled glow around bridge lights and signage so the scene feels luminous but still hand-drawn.
- Surface treatment: matte vintage print finish with subtle paper tooth, slight offset-print color variation, and gentle halftone or risograph-inspired texture in large color areas.
- Environmental details: include believable Korean urban cues such as road signs, apartment window grids, bridge pylons, taxi-light colors, convenience-store glow, and Hangang riverside reflections.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm standard lens look, medium close-up framing, eye-level to slightly off-center driver perspective, as if viewed from the passenger side.
- Lighting: night interior lighting with soft dashboard glow from below, neon spill from the city outside the window, faint rim light from street lamps and bridge lights, and reflected signage across the side window.
- Color grade: faded city pop grade with cyan-coral balance, muted mustard mids, violet navy shadows, neon pink highlights, and a restrained lo-fi matte finish.
- Illustration finish: Pixiv-inspired Korean subculture poster art with confident linework, flat-shaded faces, detailed but graphic car-interior forms, retro print texture, and cinematic night-drive atmosphere.

[6. MOOD]
Late-night Japanese city pop meets Korean urban lo-fi editorial illustration — a Seoul Han River night-drive poster with the calm confidence of an 80s retro radio program, the intimacy of a passenger-seat snapshot, and the collectible feel of an indie music event print.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render all Korean text cleanly and legibly. Use short Korean strings such as “나다운 밤, 서울을 달리다”, “시티팝 플레이리스트”, “한강의 네온과 라디오”, “오늘의 드라이브 코스”, “2026년 5월호”, “반포대교 방면”, and “티켓 ₩25,000”.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: realistic human proportions only; no exaggerated body shape, and if hands are shown, fingers must be anatomically correct with exactly 5 fingers per hand.
- Composition requirement: the face should remain clearly readable as the focal point, with poster typography, dashboard elements, and background lights arranged around the subject rather than covering the eyes or mouth.
- Text placement requirement: barcode, VOL/date label, credit line, and event details should sit in corners, bottom bands, or side margins of the poster layout while preserving the character-driven driving scene.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Cinematic director-inspired still image series, formatted as a single premium editorial film poster with a believable film-still atmosphere. Designed to feel like a cinephile exhibition key visual, magazine-feature poster, and curated mood-board print, with {감독·영화 톤} as the main creative axis and the surrounding poster details supporting the world of the image.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject area: {감독·영화 톤} should define the visual language across the frame, with the scene reading instantly as a recognizable film-toned still rather than a generic portrait.
- Center of attention: the emotional core should sit in the mid-to-lower 60% of the frame, letting the silhouette, corridor, alley, room interior, vehicle window, landscape, or weathered street lead the eye naturally.
- Background treatment: keep the environment specific and cinematic, using Hong Kong night streets, neon reflections, hallway depth, motel curtains, rain-slick asphalt, mist, pastoral fields, river fog, station platforms, diners, old apartments, or sun-faded rural roads depending on {모드 변주}.
- Framing direction: use {구도·앵글} as a concrete cinematic camera decision, allowing intimate close-up, symmetrical frontal staging, over-the-shoulder framing, low-angle street perspective, or widescreen-inspired vertical poster cropping.
- Poster enrichment: integrate believable film-poster/editorial information around the image, including a short Korean title line, issue-style label, date/time/venue, ticket info, small credit block, sponsor row, and subtle graphic marks that feel printed rather than digitally pasted.
- Scene logic: {장면} must remain legible as an intentional story beat, with the added typography and poster details supporting the cinematic world instead of distracting from it.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Establish the director signature first: translate {감독·영화 톤} into the dominant spatial rhythm, facial distance, environmental texture, light behavior, and pacing of the scene.
2. Build the emotional tone next: {시그니처 무드} should appear through body language, weather, worn surfaces, reflections, practical lights, posture, distance between people, and light falloff rather than through literal symbols.
3. Place the scene anchors: render {장면} with clear environmental cues, such as wet pavement reflections, warm lamps, cigarette-smoke haze, corridor depth, fog banks, tiled walls, paper notices, old signage, sunlit field haze, train windows, or textured curtains.
4. Lock the composition: apply {구도·앵글} as a concrete camera framing decision, with balanced visual weight, clear subject separation, foreground/midground/background layering, and believable film depth.
5. Apply the color system: use {컬러 톤} as the dominant grade, ensuring the palette feels like a coherent film frame rather than isolated color accents.
6. Add editorial poster information: include small but readable Korean poster text such as “감독별 영화 톤 사진 시리즈”, “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “시네마 무드 아카이브”, “상영 토크 19:30”, “서울 필름하우스 B관”, “예매 ₩12,000”, “사진 기획: 무드랩”, and “Model: 이서윤” where appropriate.
7. Finish with capture texture: emulate {카메라·렌즈·필름} through grain, motion blur, highlight rolloff, anamorphic breathing, halation, gate weave, slight dust specks, and filmic edge behavior.
8. If multiple styles are needed, use {모드 변주} as a selectable branch while preserving the same editorial finish and cinematic realism.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Bold for Korean labels, 24–46px range for poster labels and 12–18px for micro credits, with clean tracking, strong editorial hierarchy, and film-festival poster spacing.
- Required Korean text elements: set a bold cover/poster line in Korean such as “나다운 장면의 온도”, plus 2–3 short feature blurbs like “네온 아래의 고백”, “안개 속 롱테이크”, “빛이 남긴 여백감”; include a small date label “2026.05.18”, venue label “서울 필름하우스 B관”, and ticket label “예매 ₩12,000”.
- Color palette: base the frame on {컬러 톤}, then anchor it with deep shadow black, tungsten amber, midnight blue, neon cyan, muted cream, desaturated sage, dusty rose, sodium-vapor orange, or rainy asphalt gray depending on the selected director mood.
- Poster details: add a small barcode area, vertical spine-like credit text, tiny production notes, sponsor strip, page/series marker such as “SERIES 03 / 12”, and understated registration marks or crop marks as printed editorial artifacts.
- Border/shadow: use a subtle film-poster finish with soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity, and no hard digital outline.
- Surface treatment: keep textures photographic and slightly imperfect, with natural grain, light halation, paper tooth, fine scratches, soft ink density variation, fingerprints on glossy print, and restrained contrast.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: emulate Arriflex 35-III with 35mm Lomo Anamorphic and Kodak Vision3 500T, plus a subtle 1/30 motion blur feel where applicable.
- Lighting: use practical cinematic lighting matched to the director mode — for example tungsten street lamps, neon spill, low-key hallway lighting, overcast diffused daylight, greenish fluorescent interiors, sodium-vapor rain reflections, candlelike room glow, or golden-hour rim light; keep directionality obvious and filmic.
- Color grade: follow the selected branch in {모드 변주}, but preserve a coherent film-grade look with tungsten amber, cool cyan, pastel symmetry, misty greens, dusk blue, faded cream, or dense nocturnal contrast depending on the reference.
- Realism cues: include believable environmental details such as damp fabric, dust on windows, street puddles, worn posters, scratched metal, peeling paint, folded paper tickets, grainy signage, old theater walls, and natural imperfections in skin, clothing, and scenery.

[6. MOOD]
Premium cinephile editorial — like a curated film-festival poster, a serious Korean cinema magazine feature spread, and a Christopher Doyle / Roger Deakins reference still printed on tactile archival paper.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: all visible Korean text must render perfectly without broken characters. Use realistic short Korean copy such as “감독별 영화 톤 사진 시리즈”, “나다운 장면의 온도”, “네온 아래의 고백”, “안개 속 롱테이크”, “서울 필름하우스 B관”, and “예매 ₩12,000”.
- Composition invariants: maintain a fully cinematic still-image look, with believable depth, film-like grain, tactile print detail, authentic environmental texture, and no generic stock-photo staging.
- Style fidelity: {감독·영화 톤}, {시그니처 무드}, {장면}, {구도·앵글}, {컬러 톤}, {카메라·렌즈·필름}, and {모드 변주} must remain consistent with the chosen director aesthetic.
- Poster realism: typography, barcode area, credit block, sponsor row, issue/date labels, and ticket/venue information should feel like part of a professionally printed cinephile poster, not floating UI overlays.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

studio:youmind_skill:2791.content:
Act as a Senior Product Designer and Crowdfunding Campaign Manager.

1. ANALYZE INPUT
Look at the attached image. Determine the material properties (Soft vs. Hard), the primary colors, and the texture.

2. AUTO-SELECT SMART WEARABLE
Use this logic to choose the product category. The goal is Clean Modern Tech, not Cyberpunk.

IF the input is Soft or Fabric-like ({argument name="soft input examples" default="Ramen, Towel, Moss"})
GENERATE: The All-Climate Smart Jacket.
Features: Self-regulating temperature control, hydrophobic coating based on the input texture, and hidden magnetic pockets.

IF the input is Rigid, Boxy, or Container-like ({argument name="rigid input examples" default="Toaster, Book, Suitcase"})
GENERATE: The Ultimate Commuter Backpack.
Features: Integrated power bank with solar coating, anti-theft biometric zipper locks, and organized modular compartments.

IF the input is Mechanical or Footwear-shaped ({argument name="mechanical input examples" default="Stapler, Car, Tool"})
GENERATE: The Urban Mobility Smart Sneaker.
Features: Energy-returning sole technology, step-tracking sensors embedded in the heel, and auto-tensioning laces.

3. EXECUTE VISUALIZATION (2x2 GRID)
Generate a single image split into a precise 2x2 grid layout.

Top Left Panel (Hero Shot):
A clean, studio-lit 3/4 angle view of the product on a white or light grey background. It must look refined and manufacturable, using the texture of the input image as a premium material.

Top Right Panel (Detail Shot):
A zoomed-in macro shot focusing on a specific high-tech feature (e.g., a USB-C port, a magnetic buckle, or a waterproof seam) that shows off the input texture quality.

Bottom Left Panel (Lifestyle Shot):
A photorealistic shot of a fashionable model wearing the item in a clean, modern city setting (daytime). They look comfortable and stylish.

Bottom Right Panel (Campaign UI):
A mockup of a Kickstarter campaign page. It should show the product title, a green progress bar at 100% funded, and a bright green button that says Back This Project.

Overall Style: High-key lighting, soft shadows, 8k resolution, commercial product photography, minimalist design aesthetic.
